SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 01 — Core Platform.md

1\. Purpose

The substrate that every other subsystem depends on: config loading and validation, IPC and the ring buffer, trust primitives, crash handling, the process watchdog, the safety invariant, persona constraints, anti-cheat structural refusals, destructive-action detection, the Entity Ledger, and the OODA-Tool scaffold in the safety path. Chapter 1 defines the platform-level invariants — the rules that hold regardless of which module is active — and the process architecture that runs them.

2\. Architecture

2\.1 Modular architecture

Features toggle on and off per documented performance impact. Every non-core feature is exposed as a toggle in \[features.\*], with all shipped features defaulting on. Gated components are off until their A.x gate passes. Safety-critical features — voice-cloning refusal, kernel-AC structural refusals, destructive-action safety invariant — are structurally enforced regardless of toggle state.

The open-source stack is Tauri 2 (desktop framework, tauri-apps/tauri), a Rust core, and a React/TypeScript UI. Target <50 MB idle RAM excluding WebView2, egui, and model weights. Tauri 2 documentation and app-size guidance are in References (R.5).

2\.2 Electron exclusion (structural invariant)

SUL ships zero Electron components. No electron in any manifest; no contextBridge/nodeIntegration/webPreferences/BrowserWindow/BrowserView/&lt;webview&gt;; no ASAR; no bundled Node.js runtime; no Electron sidecar. This is structural — enforced by cargo xtask electron-audit — and paired with the Tauri capability audit (§4 of this chapter, rule set 34 and Part 16 §16.15) that closes the XSS→RCE surface that the Electron exclusion does not itself close.

The exclusion means six attack surfaces are absent from the binary by construction:

There is no Electron code, so there is no Node.js RCE escalation path.
There is no contextBridge to bypass.
There is no ELECTRON\_RUN\_AS\_NODE fuse to pop.
There is no bundled Chromium to run its own CVE treadmill against.
There is no ASAR to tamper with.
There is no Node.js runtime to compromise.

That is a real reduction in the binary's attack surface. It does not, however, make SUL secure on its own. XSS, capability misconfiguration, npm supply-chain exposure, and WebView2 zero-days remain. Those are closed by:

The capability audit (rule set 34).
CSP nonces.
Isolation Pattern.
Strict ESM.
De-elevation.
The three CI gates (electron-audit, tauri-capability-audit, webview-runtime-audit).
The WebView hardening configuration (\[webview] isolation\_pattern = true, enhanced\_security\_mode = "strict", runtime\_floor = "156.0.4314.58").
The vault's anti-tampering layers (Ch. 2 §2.10–§2.11), as defense-in-depth even if WebView is compromised.

The residual is WebView2 zero-days, which no architecture eliminates. Full threat-model paragraph in Ch. 16 §16.4.

2\.3 App-level authentication (pointer)

App-level authentication (\[auth]) is documented in full in Ch. 2 §2.1. The layer loads before the WebView exists, so a compromised WebView cannot bypass it. \[auth] config, AND-logic across factors, reauth intervals, and the --dev-auth-bypass guard all live there. Chapter 1 references \[auth] only as a startup-stage dependency (see §2.7 Step 4.14).

2\.4 Feature classification

Every feature is classified as one of four kinds. This table is the authoritative classification referenced by §2.1, §4.2 (validator rule #29), and every module chapter. The \[features.\*] block that mirrors this table lives in each module's config section; the classification is here because it is a platform-level audit.

Core features (never togglable — code change, not config change):

Feature	Why core

Config loading	Everything depends on it.
Config validator (cargo xtask config-check)	Enforces every compatibility rule in §4 and every module rule.
IPC ring buffers (sul-ring)	Every IPC stream depends on it.
Ed25519 signature verification	Pack, model, and update trust all depend on it.
Trust primitives (sul-trust, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog)	Security substrate.
Crash handlers (sul-crash)	Recovery substrate.
Process watchdog	Recovery substrate.
Safety invariant (destructive-action routes to Thinking)	Non-negotiable. Disabling is Tier 1-core.
Persona constraints	Behavioral substrate.
Anti-cheat structural refusals (kernel-AC → no FG / no flip-model / no mods / no ETW / no optimize)	Non-negotiable.
Destructive-action detection	Safety-critical.
Entity Ledger	Cross-cutting memory.
OODA-Tool scaffold in the safety path	Safety-critical.
TSCG schema compilation in the destructive-action judgment path	Safety-critical.

Shipped features (on by default, toggle available). Every \[features.\*] entry whose source is true in the module chapters. Full enumeration is distributed across Ch. 3–16; each module's config section declares its own shipped features. The master feature classification gate (shipped on / gated off / opt-in off) is what cargo xtask baseline-audit checks — a mismatch between a feature's \[features.\*] value and its classification in the module chapter is E\_CFG at startup.

Gated features (off until A.x passes). Every \[features.\*] entry marked with a gate reference in its module chapter. Each entry's gate ID (A.x) is preserved in SUL-LEDGER/gates.md. The feature's default value is false until the gate passes; the gate's release-class assignment in releases.md determines when the gate becomes testable, and the gate's measurement criterion in gates.md determines when the feature flips to true.

Opt-in features (off by default, safety-critical):

Vault: \[vault] enabled = false.
Auth: \[auth] enabled = true (the default is on because it's the security baseline; "opt-in" here means the user must configure factors).
Uncensored models: \[features.ai.uncensored = false], \[features.ai.local\_uncensored = false].
Global sensor fusion: \[features.vision.global\_sensor\_fusion = false].
Every handoff feature: \[features.csi.enabled = false], etc.

Opt-in features must be Tier 1 events to enable. The full opt-in list is in each module's config section.

The complete feature classification table is therefore distributed by module chapter with the classification visible per entry, plus the core-feature list above as the platform-level invariant. Validator rule #29 (§4.2) ensures every \[features.\*] toggle is assigned exactly one release class in releases.md; validator rule #33 ensures every Tier 1 event is either Tier 1-core or assigned a release class.

2\.5 Performance optimizations

All \[performance] optimizations default on. Gated toggles show "on" but fall back through the fallback chain if the gate hasn't passed — the user's intent is "use it if available," not "force it."

The complete \[performance] config structure is distributed per module (each module's chapter has its \[performance.module\_name] block). The \[performance] block in §4.1 contains only the cross-module overview toggles:

toml

\[performance]

enable\_quantization = true

enable\_kv\_compression = true

enable\_speculation = true

enable\_vision\_compression = true

enable\_audio\_optimizations = true

enable\_runtime\_optimizations = true

enable\_emulator\_optimizations = true

enable\_music\_optimizations = true

enable\_broadcast\_optimizations = true

Each module's \[performance.module\_name] block participates in the same compatibility matrix (§10) and gate ledger (SUL-LEDGER/gates.md). Deep optimizations have \[performance.deep.\*] toggles in Ch. 10 §10.5. The music player has \[performance.music] in Ch. 5 §5.5. The broadcast engine has \[performance.broadcast] in Ch. 6 §6.6. The emulator has \[performance.emulation] in Ch. 3. The audio governor has its decisions in Ch. 4 §4.10.

2\.6 Process architecture

This section is authoritative. It consolidates the previous spec's §3.4 and §11.9 (which self-disclaimed as a duplicate); the §11.9 content is merged here and the duplicate deleted.

Eleven-plus processes (consolidated with handoff additions):

sul.exe (main Tauri shell): UI, game library, mod tooling, packet loading, IPC hub, supervised-thread subsystems, sul-prosody classifier, sul-governor game-state machine, screenshot ring buffer, search pipeline orchestration (RustXNG MCP calls, adblock filter, readdown extract, excerpt select, verification packet builder), sul-agent Combat Full profile router. The sul-wire library runs in sul.exe and provides the memory-mapped ArrayBuffer. Also hosts sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, sul-voice-auth in a dedicated vault thread (not a separate process — the vault is a storage subsystem, not inference). Panic: catch\_unwind, log to sul-crash, respawn after state validation (Mode E, Ch. 14 §14.11). Uses vtcode-process-hardening pre-main to disable core dumps and debugger attach.

sul-ai.exe (separate): LLM inference, model loading, LoRA management, sul-agent orchestration, ReTrace saliency computation and dormant buffer management, Medusa/phrase head loaders, sul-spec-draft RIFT wrapper. Hosts the Combat Full checkpoint; one inference profile active per turn. ggml abort or driver fault takes down only this process.

sul-ipc.exe (separate): Shared-memory ring buffer host. Corrupted buffer recovered by killing + reattaching.

sul-vision.exe (separate, on-demand): OCR (sul-ocr) and scene-understanding (sul-vlm) sidecar. Spawned by any tier, loads the appropriate engine from the routing chain, extracts structured output, exits. Releases VRAM immediately unless --cache-vision.

sul-coder.exe (child of sul-ai.exe, on-demand): Coder-session tool worker. Spawned by sul-ai.exe when a Coder session starts; suspended when a game launches.

sul-gen.exe (child of sul-ai.exe, on-demand): Generation worker for long-running batch inference. Spawned on demand; suspended when a game launches.

sul-music.exe (Ch. 5 §5.4): Music player process. Spawned by sul.exe on demand; terminated when idle for 5 minutes; holds the WASAPI device only while playing.

sul-broadcast.exe (Ch. 6 §6.3): Broadcast engine process. Spawned by sul.exe when broadcast is enabled; terminated when idle for 10 minutes; hosts the compositor, encoder, ISO muxer, and broadcast audio mixer.

sul-csi.exe (Ch. 15 §15.1): WiFi CSI sensing process. Receives raw CSI data from ESP32 nodes via USB serial or network. Runs FFT-based vital sign extraction in Rust. Publishes CsiVitalsUpdated telemetry. Spawned on demand when \[features] vision.csi\_sensing = true.

sul-bci.exe (Ch. 15 §15.2): Brain-computer interface process. Ingests OpenBCI or MEG/EEG data, runs brain2qwerty-rs inference. Publishes BciDecodedText telemetry. Spawned on demand when \[features] bci.brain2qwerty = true.

sul-voicestudio.exe (Ch. 15 §15.4): Voice synthesis and dubbing process. Runs VoiceStudio TTS and voice cloning engine (excluding voice cloning of specific real persons, which is structurally refused). Communicates via sul-ipc. Spawned on demand when \[features] voice.voicestudio = true.

In-process supervised threads:

sul-dsp runs in sul-audio's process (or sul.exe if sul-audio is compiled in).

sul-voice intercepts WASAPI at driver layer and runs as a supervised thread in sul.exe (or sul-audio).

sul-audio-governor is a supervised thread in the same process as sul-audio (Ch. 4 §4.10).

sul-stt runs in sul-audio's process (or sul.exe when sul-audio is compiled in) — it consumes the same dual-track ring sul-audio already produces, so no new audio stream is opened; the whisper.cpp inference thread is pinned per the STT config's thread\_affinity setting, and it publishes no telemetry of its own (STT completion flows into the subtitle/TTS path directly, and prosody classification already covers the intent gate).

sul-voice-fx runs in the same process as sul-dsp and sul-audio; it is part of the sul-dsp graph, not a separate process (Ch. 4 §4.2, §4.11).

sul-toolprm cross-encoder runs in sul-agent's beam search path (within sul.exe) — it is small enough (\~60–180 MB Q4) that a separate process is overkill.

sul-kv-compress runs in sul-ai-native's KV cache layer (same process as model inference).

sul-spec-draft RIFT wrapper runs inside sul-ai-native (same process as model inference).

ReTrace runs in sul-ai-native (same process as model inference).

Search pipeline runs in sul-net (within sul.exe) — RustXNG MCP calls are out-of-process to the RustXNG daemon, but the pipeline orchestration and verification packet builder are in-process.

Combat Full profile router runs inside sul.exe's agent thread as part of sul-agent::combat\_profile. Sends ControlMsg::SetCombatProfile { profile } to sul-ai.exe before each turn. All profiles share the same llama\_context; the profile flip is a runtime parameter change (--reasoning-budget and --ctx-size), not a model reload. Profile-switch latency target: <50 ms. The router publishes TelemetryMsg::CombatProfileSelected { profile, source, confidence, at } on every decision, which backs CombatFullStatusIndicator (Ch. 10 §10.15).

Vault (sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, sul-voice-auth) runs as a dedicated thread inside sul.exe, not a separate process. The vault is a storage subsystem, not an inference subsystem; its threat model is about the encrypted file at rest, not about the runtime process. Process-level isolation for vault I/O is deferred to a future enhancement if a specific threat model warrants it.

Sub-processes (not SUL processes — they run inside other processes):

sul-fg runs as a Vulkan implicit layer inside the game's or emulator's Vulkan process — not as a SUL process. The launcher sets VK\_INSTANCE\_LAYERS on the child process env; there is no SUL-side FG process. See Ch. 9 §9.1.

sul-gb runs inside the emulator process spawned by sul-emu — not a SUL process. Same as any libretro core (Ch. 3 §3.3, §3.5).

sul-savestate is a library, not a process — it runs in the emulator process (for sul-gb) or in the sul-emu-libretro frontend's process (for libretro cores).

IPC topology: Tauri IPC for UI ↔ shell. sul-ipc for shell ↔ AI ↔ subsystem. sul-vision communicates via sul-ipc ring buffer. sul-prosody and sul-governor run in sul.exe (CPU thread pool); they feed sul-ai.exe via ControlMsg::IntentClassified and TelemetryMsg::GameStateUpdated. sul-net runs in sul.exe and feeds sul-ai.exe via ControlMsg::VerificationPacketReady. sul-agent's router feeds sul-ai.exe via ControlMsg::SetCombatProfile.

2\.7 Startup sequence

Base startup sequence:

Load config (%APPDATA%\\SUL\\config.toml).
Verify Ed25519 signing key against %APPDATA%\\SUL\\trust\\pubkey.minisig.
Load signed packs from %APPDATA%\\SUL\\sulpack (Ch. 11).
Initialize IPC ring buffers.
Load models per pre-created contexts (§3.3 of this chapter: Combat Full Instruct 2K, Thinking 4K, Conversation 16K lazy no-game, Coding 8K research; Deep Q5/Q4 4K; Deep 8K on demand with asymmetric KV).
Warm up AI (llama\_decode with prefix cache).
Initialize overlay window and WGC capture (Ch. 7).
Spawn supervised subsystems (sul-prosody, sul-governor).
Start sul-metrics rollup thread.
Enter main loop.

Additional startup steps:

Step 2.5 — Config validator runs. Checks every rule in §4. The module-specific validation rules (music, broadcast, vault, auth, webview, STT, emulation, quant, KV-compress, spec-draft, toolprm, CSI, BCI, GEV, security, VoiceStudio, release-plan) are documented in each module chapter's config section; §4.2 holds the cross-cutting rules.

Step 2.6 — Optimization presets. If \[ai.optimization] is present, the preset manager resolves each field into its target config section (offload\_mode → \[ai.kv\_tier] method, kv\_method → \[ai.kv\_tier] method, spec\_chain → \[ai.speculative] &lt;tier&gt;\_chain, pruning → \[ai.combat\_full], quant → \[ai.combat\_full] weight\_quant). The frame\_gen and audio\_budget presets similarly resolve into \[frame\_gen] and \[audio.governor]. Preset override wins over config.toml defaults but not over per-game game\_registry.json. It also rejects invalid combinations (e.g., offload\_mode = "none" alongside \[ai.deep] planner\_split = true when the planner needs a loaded tier) with E\_CFG. The combat profile override is a separate toggle under the same preset panel, not a preset row — it is a Tier 1 event and does not resolve from \[ai.optimization]. (Full preset resolution matrix in Ch. 10 §10.5.)

Step 3.5 — STAR-KV pair check. For every STAR-KV-activated model, verify decompression sibling exists and pair\_verified\_at is valid. If not, E\_STAR\_KV\_PAIR\_MISMATCH and refuse to load that tier. (Ch. 10 §10.10.)

Step 3.6 — ReTrace saliency layer verification. Verify InternViT attention layers 6–12 are available; dormant buffer allocation on STAR-KV. If unavailable, E\_RETRACE\_UNAVAILABLE and Combat Full falls back to full-token baseline for that session (VRAM +0.3–0.4 GB in all profiles). (Ch. 10 §10.11.)

Step 3.7 — Combat Full profile pre-created contexts. Verify all pre-created contexts exist on the loaded llama\_context: Instruct (2K), Thinking (4K), Conversation (16K, lazy no-game), Coding (8K, research). Verify --reasoning-budget toggles correctly between 0 (Instruct/Coding), 256 (Conversation), and the configured Thinking budget. If Instruct context is available but Thinking context fails, log E\_COMBAT\_PROFILE\_INVALID and disable Thinking profile for the session (all turns Instruct — router bypassed with a warning). If Conversation context fails, disable Conversation profile for the session (all no-game turns Instruct). If Coding context fails, Coding profile stays research (already gated A.101). If no context is available, Combat Full is dropped entirely for the session and the user is notified (E\_COMBAT\_PROFILE\_INVALID at the fatal severity). This check runs before Step 4.5 (DSP artifact load), because Combat Full is the highest-priority tier and its failure is more user-impactful than DSP artifact failure. (Ch. 10 §10.4.)

Step 3.8 — sul-quant SPEED-Q check. If \[ai.optimization] quant resolves to sul\_quant (or per-game \[ai.combat\_full] weight\_quant is a sul-quant output), verify the GGUF file present is the SPEED-Q quantized variant. If A.96 has not passed on the current hardware, sul-quant is hidden and the llama.cpp Q4\_K\_S variant is used. (Ch. 10 §10.14.)

Step 3.9 — sul-kv-compress backend selection. Resolve \[ai.kv\_tier] method to a concrete backend. Run A.97 checks on the selected backend if it's a non-STAR-KV/GAAC backend. If the backend fails A.97, fall back per the fallback chain and log E\_KV\_COMPRESS\_BACKEND\_UNAVAILABLE. (Ch. 10 §10.17.)

Step 3.10 — sul-toolprm cross-encoder check. Verify the cross-encoder loads and passes a smoke test. If not, E\_TOOLPRM\_LOAD\_FAILED and ToolPRM is disabled for the session (falls back to no-PRM baseline). (Ch. 10 §10.21.)

Step 4.5 — sul-dsp artifact load. Verify stability certificate. If unstable, E\_DSP\_ARTIFACT\_UNSTABLE and fall back to AVX2 hand-written chain. (Ch. 4 §4.11.)

Step 4.6 — sul-voice model load. Verify SHA-256. If missing, E\_VOICE\_MODEL\_MISSING and disable voice isolation. (Ch. 4 §4.12.)

Step 4.7 — sul-wire ring map. Map tokens ring to ArrayBuffer. If fails, E\_WIRE\_RING\_NOT\_MAPPED and fall back to Tauri IPC path for tokens. (Ch. 7 §7.3.)

Step 4.8 — Search pipeline verification. RustXNG MCP reachable; adblock filters loaded; readdown extractor initialized; verification packet builder ready. If any fails, E\_SEARCH\_PIPELINE\_DEGRADED and search falls back to direct fetch with truncated context. (Ch. 8 §8.6.)

Step 4.9 — GitHub search check. If \[net.github] enabled = true, verify GitHub API is reachable and auth token valid. If not, E\_GITHUB\_AUTH\_FAILED and disable github\_search for session. (Ch. 8 §8.7.)

Step 4.10 — CIG GPU scheduling initialization. If CIG unavailable, log warning and continue with default scheduling. (Ch. 13 §13.5.)

Step 4.11 — OODA-Tool + TSCG verification. Probe with a scripted tool call; verify all four scaffold fields populate before tool emission; verify TSCG compiler produces ≥51% compression on reference schema set. If scaffold fails, warn and default to unstructured planning for the session. If TSCG fails, E\_TSCG\_COMPILE\_FAILED and fall back to raw JSON schemas. (Ch. 10 §10.11.)

Step 4.12 — Frame generation layer check. Verify VkLayer\_sul\_fg.json (or VkLayer\_LSFGVK\_frame\_generation.json for lsfg\_layer passthrough) is present in %APPDATA%\\SUL\\fg\\layers. Verify Lossless.dll (if required by the selected backend) is importable. If either is missing, log FrameGenUnavailable and default FG to off until the user restores them. (Ch. 9 §9.2.)

Step 4.13 — Audio governor decision loop. Run the six-decision pass; publish AudioGovernorActive. If AG-1, AG-4, or AG-5 fire, log the corresponding event. (Ch. 4 §4.10.)

Step 4.14 — Vault check. If \[vault] enabled = true, verify vault file exists at \[vault] path, header signature valid, TPM/DPAPI wrapping available, auth factors configured. If vault file corrupt → E\_VAULT\_TAMPER\_DETECTED, whole vault to quarantine. If auth factors missing → E\_VAULT\_MISCONFIGURED, vault remains locked. If TPM/DPAPI unavailable → E\_VAULT\_HARDWARE\_ROOT\_UNAVAILABLE, allow user to proceed with passphrase-only (Tier 1 event) or abort unlock. (Ch. 2 §2.9.)

Step 4.15 — WebView runtime check. Verify WebView2 runtime version against \[webview] runtime\_floor, Tauri version against the same, Isolation Pattern enabled status, Strict ESM enabled status. Mismatches raise E\_WEBVIEW\_RUNTIME\_BELOW\_FLOOR (blocking launch) or E\_WEBVIEW\_HARDENING\_DISABLED (warning). (This chapter §4, §10.)

Step 4.16 — Music player binary check. Verify sul-music.exe present; verify library paths exist; verify WASAPI device coordination; verify sul-music-engine decoder initializes. If sul-music.exe missing, music player disabled with E\_CFG (but sul.exe continues). (Ch. 5 §5.10.)

Step 4.17 — Broadcast binary check. Verify sul-broadcast.exe present; verify encoder admission controller probe succeeds; verify WGC capture available; verify USB/IP virtual audio device server enumerates devices without a SUL driver. If sul-broadcast.exe missing, broadcast disabled with E\_CFG (but sul.exe continues). If USB/IP enumeration fails, fall back to VBAN bridge (BR-2). (Ch. 6 §6.10.)

Step 4.18 — CSI subsystem check. If \[features] vision.csi\_sensing = true, verify sul-csi.exe present, ESP32 nodes reachable, FFT processing initialized. If no nodes reachable, log CSI-1 and disable presence detection but retain host-side processing. (Ch. 15 §15.1.)

Step 4.19 — BCI subsystem check. If \[features] bci.brain2qwerty = true, verify sul-bci.exe present, brain2qwerty-rs model loaded, OpenBCI hardware connected. If model load fails, log BCI-2 and disable BCI for session. (Ch. 15 §15.2.)

Step 4.20 — VoiceStudio check. If \[features] voice.voicestudio = true, verify sul-voicestudio.exe present, TTS engine loaded, voice cloning structural refusal in place. If model unavailable, log VS-1 and fall back to Piper TTS. (Ch. 15 §15.4.)

Step 4.21 — GEV check. If \[features] geopolitics.gods\_eye\_view = true, verify GodsEyeView renders 10,000+ objects at 60fps, geolocation from image works. If feed unavailable, log GEV-1 and use cached tiles. (Ch. 15 §15.3.)

Step 4.22 — Security toolkit check. If \[features] security.toolkit = true, verify hashcat, nuclei, mitmproxy\_rs, Shannon Lite available and functional. If any tool container fails, log SEC-1 and report error without executing scan. (Ch. 15 §15.5.)

Step 6.5 — Speculation chain benchmark. For each tier, run 30s benchmark across chain rungs, cache winner to %APPDATA%\\SUL\\bench. If cached result exists and is <7 days old, read cache in <100 ms. Combat Full has one chain (combat\_chain = \["medusa", "phrase", "unispec", "ngram", "none"]) — the benchmark runs once for all profiles. Deep runs \["chainflow", "lilicorr", "unispec", "ngram", "none"]. (Ch. 10 §10.12.)

Step 6.6 — Combat Full profile router initialization. Initialize sul-agent::combat\_profile. Verify the router is reachable (in-process). Run the 200-prompt router accuracy probe from the cached benchmark if it exists (<7 days old); if not, defer to first gameplay turn and log RouterBenchmarkDeferred. Publish CombatProfileSelected telemetry on the first turn to confirm the router is live. If the router fails to initialize, log E\_COMBAT\_ROUTER\_INIT\_FAILED and fall back to fixed-profile selection from \[ai.combat] profile (default: Instruct). A fixed-profile fallback is documented, not silent — the overlay shows the fixed profile with a warning chip on CombatProfileIndicator. (Ch. 10 §10.9.)

2\.8 Precedence rules

Base precedence (highest to lowest): per-game override in game\_registry.json > %APPDATA%\\SUL\\config.toml > built-in defaults.

Additional precedence rules:

Combat profile override precedence (highest to lowest):

Destructive-action safety invariant (always routes to Thinking if destructive\_action\_always\_thinking = true, regardless of any other setting).
Per-game combat.profile in game\_registry.json (fixed profile for that game; overrides \[ai.combat] profile).
\[ai.combat] profile in config.toml (global fixed profile when router\_enabled: false, or when the router is disabled by failure).
\[ai.combat\_router] deterministic signals (when \[ai.combat] profile = "auto" and the router is enabled).
Default = Instruct (fast path).

Precedence 1 cannot be overridden by any lower priority. Setting destructive\_action\_always\_thinking = false at the per-game level disables precedence 1 for that game only, and is a Tier 1 event.

Speculation chain override: \[ai.speculative] &lt;tier&gt;\_chain wins over built-in defaults. --spec-type &lt;type&gt; on the command line overrides the chain entirely for that session (single-rung). Combat Full uses combat\_chain; per-profile chain overrides are rejected by the config validator (E\_CFG).

KV method override: \[ai.kv\_tier] method wins over built-in defaults. --kv-method &lt;method&gt; overrides for that session. KV fallback precedence: \[ai.kv\_tier] fallback\_enabled = false disables GAAC fallback (STAR-KV fail → uncompressed). Default is true.

Config validator precedence: config validator runs before any model loads. If validator fails, startup aborts with E\_CFG. No silent degradation.

Optimization preset precedence (§2.7 Step 2.6): \[ai.optimization] overrides \[ai.kv\_tier] method, \[ai.speculative] &lt;tier&gt;\_chain, and \[ai.combat\_full] weight\_quant when set to a non-auto value. auto means "follow the target config section." Per-game game\_registry.json still wins over \[ai.optimization] for gameplay-scoped settings (offload\_mode, quant, pruning). The combat profile override is a Tier 1 event and is not governed by \[ai.optimization].

Search pipeline override: \[net.search] backend wins over built-in. --no-web-search disables for session. --search-backend=<rustxng|direct\_fetch|disabled> overrides for session.

GitHub search override: \[net.github] enabled wins over built-in. --no-github-search disables for session. --github-search-rate-limit &lt;n&gt; overrides rate limit for session.

ReTrace override: \[vision.retrace] enabled = false disables ReTrace (Combat Full falls back to full-token baseline — VRAM cost +0.3–0.4 GB, all profiles). --no-retrace overrides for session.

OODA-Tool override: \[agent] ooda\_tool = false disables scaffold (not recommended — measurably worse multi-step reliability). --no-ooda overrides for session.

TSCG override: \[agent] tscg = false disables schema compilation (falls back to raw JSON — measurably worse tool accuracy at production catalog sizes). --no-tscg overrides for session.

Frame generation override: per-game frame\_gen block wins over \[frame\_gen] section defaults. Command line --no-fg disables for session, --fg-engine &lt;engine&gt; and --fg-multiplier &lt;n&gt; override for session. Kernel-AC refusal is structural and cannot be overridden by any of these. (Ch. 9.)

Audio governor override: per-game audio block wins over \[audio.governor] section defaults. Command line --audio-budget &lt;budget&gt; overrides for session. (Ch. 4.)

STT config override: per-game vision block currently exposes no STT overrides — \[stt] is a single global section. If a per-game override is ever wanted (e.g., a game with distinct audio characteristics), it would be added to the per-game audio block and follow the same precedence pattern. Not in the shipping release. Command line --stt-model &lt;model&gt; and --stt-quant &lt;quant&gt; override the \[stt] section for the session only; they are diagnostic flags, not persisted. (Ch. 4.)

Vault config override: \[vault] is global, not per-game. extra\_paths cannot be extended via config edit — only via OS file picker. --vault-disable is a diagnostic flag (not for regular use), and it must be followed by a successful Windows Hello auth before the session starts (this is intentional — disabling the vault is a security-sensitive operation). (Ch. 2.)

sul-quant override: \[ai.optimization] quant resolves auto to sul\_quant (SPEED-Q 4-bit for InternVL3-2B, Q5\_K\_M for Deep) when A.96 passed. q4\_k\_m forces llama.cpp Q4\_K\_M. q5\_k\_m forces llama.cpp Q5\_K\_M. Explicit sul\_quant forces SPEED-Q. (Ch. 10.)

sul-kv-compress override: \[ai.kv\_tier] method per backend. --kv-method &lt;backend&gt; overrides for session. KC-1/KC-2 fallbacks apply within the trait's fallback chain. (Ch. 10.)

sul-toolprm override: \[ai.combat\_full] toolprm\_model selects sul\_toolprm\_enc (default) or toolrm\_qwen3\_4b (ED only). --no-toolprm disables for session. (Ch. 10.)

sul-spec-draft override: \[ai.speculative] draft\_kv\_compress\_threshold\_mb (default 32). --no-rift disables the wrapper for session. Dormant by default — the override only matters if draft cache >32 MB. (Ch. 10.)

Music player override: \[music] section. Per-game music settings? None — the music player is global, not per-game. --no-music disables for session. (Ch. 5.)

Broadcast override: \[broadcast] section. Per-game broadcast settings? None — the broadcast engine is global, not per-game. --no-broadcast disables for session. (Ch. 6.)

CSI override: \[csi] section. --no-csi disables for session. \[features] vision.csi\_sensing is the primary toggle. (Ch. 15.)

BCI override: \[bci] section. --no-bci disables for session. \[features] bci.brain2qwerty is the primary toggle. (Ch. 15.)

GEV override: \[gev] section. --no-gev disables for session. \[features] geopolitics.gods\_eye\_view is the primary toggle. (Ch. 15.)

Security toolkit override: \[security\_toolkit] section. --no-security-toolkit disables for session. \[features] security.toolkit and \[features] security.shannon are the primary toggles. (Ch. 15.)

VoiceStudio override: \[voicestudio] section. --no-voicestudio disables for session. \[features] voice.voicestudio is the primary toggle. (Ch. 15.)

3\. Contract

3.1 Core feature list

The 14-item list in §2.4 above. These features are never togglable — a code change, not a config change. The safety invariant, persona constraints, anti-cheat structural refusals, destructive-action detection, Entity Ledger, OODA-Tool scaffold in the safety path, and TSCG schema compilation in the destructive-action judgment path are structural: they are not config options, and disabling them is a Tier 1-core event (§4.2, rule #33).

Key semantics preserved from the original:

ModelLoaded / ModelEvicted telemetry fires once for Tier::CombatFull, not per profile. Profile switches are CombatProfileSelected events, not ModelLoaded events.

EscalationTriggered still uses Tier for from/to — a Combat Full → Deep escalation fires it, but Combat Full Instruct ↔ Thinking ↔ Conversation ↔ Coding switches do not (they are profile switches, not escalations).

Mode is deprecated. New code uses Tier + CombatProfile.

IPC ring-buffer schema: the full ring topology, slot layout, backpressure rules, message size limits, sequence/wrap handling, and recovery procedure are in Ch. 7 §7.3 (the ring buffer is sul-ipc). The 64 KB message-size ceiling is a platform-level constant; the rkyv schema discipline (backward-compatible additions, golden-bytes test) is in sul-ipc-types's contract. Module chapters reference Ch. 7 §7.3 for the ring mechanics and only add their own message types.

3.3 Pre-created contexts

Context length is set at model load via llama\_context\_params.n\_ctx. Pre-created contexts per profile:

Tier / Profile	Context	Base model	When active

Combat Full — Instruct	2K	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	Game running, fast execution
Combat Full — Thinking	4K	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	Game running, planning / destructive-action
Combat Full — Conversation	16K (lazy no-game)	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	No-game open-ended dialogue
Combat Full — Coding (research)	8K (16K ceiling)	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	No-game code work, A.101 gated
Deep Q5/Q4	4K	K2-Horizon-7B	Actively-loaded agentic coding
Deep 8K	8K on demand	K2-Horizon-7B	Asymmetric KV (-ctk q8\_0 -ctv q5\_1)

Cold vs warm: Cold = first turn of session, KV cache empty. Warm = KV cache holds exact prefix (interactive follow-up, or persistent prompt cache). Baselines measure both separately.

Context sweet-spot rationale:

Combat Full — Instruct at 2K. The current-frame task is vision-dominated, not text-dominated. The KV cache is \~50 MB in q8\_0 at 2K. ReTrace's dormant buffer adds \~10 MB. Total \~60 MB. Instruct mode at 2K is the accuracy-equivalent window for the current-frame vision task: extra context does not improve frame comprehension, and does reduce the room available for vision tokens. ReTrace's 11.1% token retention keeps the vision side at 100% benchmark retention at this context. Instruct is the fast path — its 2K window is deliberately narrow because the workload is deliberately narrow (one tool call, one frame, one answer).

Combat Full — Thinking at 4K. The planning/judgment task is text-dominated, not frame-dominated. Thinking mode's 4K window is used for: OODA-Tool scaffold fields (observed state, orientation, decided action), the Entity Ledger (exact IDs, mission IDs, file paths), thread state (current encounter, mission, ship state, session threads), and multi-step reasoning traces. Vision tokens at 4K are the same count as at 2K (max\_dynamic\_patch = 4 caps them); the extra 2K is reasoning headroom, not vision headroom. Both profiles share ReTrace's dormant buffer, sized for Thinking mode's 4K with headroom for Instruct and Conversation.

Combat Full — Conversation at 16K. This is the no-game open-ended dialogue window. 16K is the native Qwen2.5 window — no YaRN required, no double-scaling risk. This is the same window Butler had; the Conversation profile replaces Butler without shrinking the conversational context. Full-history KV reuse (Continuum pattern) keeps the prefix cached across turns, so 16K is practical without re-prefill cost. The pre-existing design's Combat Mid had a similar 8K window; Combat Full Thinking's 4K window is deliberately tighter — its job is planning and reasoning over the current encounter (fits in 4K with the Entity Ledger), not packet-reasoning over long histories. Under the profile design, long histories are stored in address pointers and dereferenced on demand (Ch. 11 §11.6) rather than held in-context.

Combat Full — Coding at 8K (research). 8K is the research profile's working window; 16K ceiling. If A.101 passes, this ships; if not, it stays research and Deep is the only coding path. The InternVL3-2B base is HumanEval 39.0; A.101 requires ≥60 through fine-tune.

16-hour session strategy: A 16-hour session does not need 16 hours of raw context in the window. It needs:

Current segment — the last 1–2 hours, uncompressed. Typically 2K–4K tokens for HUD state, tool calls, and OODA scaffold state. Combat Full Thinking's 4K window holds this with the Entity Ledger. Combat Full Conversation's 16K window holds 8–12 hours of compressed dialogue history plus current segment.

Compressed summaries of earlier segments — 500–1000 tokens per segment. Tighter than the pre-consolidation design's 1K–2K budget, because Thinking's 4K window is tighter than the old Combat Low-era 8K window. Preserves outcomes and persistent facts.

Persistent facts — mission objectives, ship loadout, known threats. Always-loaded Entity Ledger, <1K tokens.

Compression cadence: 1 hour or event-driven (encounter end, mission complete, dock/refuel). Both trigger before the session enters the unreliable regime (research: sessions over 2 hours are unreliable without explicit context management; the tighter 1-hour cadence reflects Combat Full Thinking's tighter 4K window vs the old Combat Low's 8K). Event-driven compression beats time-driven for combat because salience is bursty — a 1-hour peaceful exploration produces little worth keeping; a 10-minute boss encounter produces far more. Compressing after the encounter, when the outcome is resolved, preserves more of what matters.

At a 1-hour cadence, a 16-hour session produces \~16 compressed segments. At 500–1000 tokens per summary, that is 8K–16K of compressed history. This history does not sit in-context all at once; it is stored as address pointers and recalled via recall\_section or deref\_pointer on demand (Ch. 11 §11.6). The live window holds only: current segment, Entity Ledger, recently-dereferenced facts, and the active OODA scaffold. This is why address pointers are load-bearing — without them, the compressed history would overflow Thinking's 4K window. For Conversation's 16K window, the same structure applies but with more uncompressed history retained in-context and a longer compression cadence (2-hour default) since the workload is dialogue rather than combat.

Context resize mechanism (D3): Context length set at model load via llama\_context\_params.n\_ctx. Manual adjustment triggers background thread: construct new llama\_context, atomically swap pointer, drop old. No UI freeze — the swap is atomic from the inference thread's perspective. Old context is dropped after the new one is warm.

YaRN safety gate: read GGUF rope\_scaling metadata. If YaRN already baked in, do not pass --rope-scaling; only --ctx-size. Double-scaling garbles output. Conservative factor for K2 and Qwen at 64K is 2.0 — not the default 4.0. Combat Full uses native contexts — no YaRN. Deep uses native 32K ceiling — no YaRN. The double-scale check in §2.7 step 2.5 prevents accidental YaRN.

Long-context caveats: K2-Horizon's 512K native context exists but at 8 GB the KV cache explodes past \~16K without extreme compression. With STAR-KV's up to 20× KV compression, Deep Q5 at 8K context fits in \~7.2 GB (STAR-KV) instead of \~7.9 GB (q8\_0). 16K becomes plausible; 32K is practical ceiling. Deep ships at 4K–8K by default; 512K capability remains research target for 24 GB+ cards.

Screenshot context for sul-vlm: Scene understanding queries include current frame plus up to 2 recent frames (temporal context — "shield just dropped from 100 to 87"). Frame buffer is 10-second ring at 30 Hz, zero VRAM. On RDP, ring becomes request-scoped at 2s / 5 Hz, and VLM receives only current frame — temporal context disabled on RDP because remote frame pacing is unreliable. The VLM never sees more than 3 frames per query.

KV cache sizing under STAR-KV: estimates. STAR-KV's actual compression depends on learned per-head rank from the model-surgery pass (Ch. 10 §10.10). The baseline entries become real measurements after sul-kv-tier ships and the A.18/A.97 harness runs.

Tier / Profile	Context	q8\_0/q8\_0 KV	GAAC KV	STAR-KV KV	ReTrace (dormant)

Combat Full — Instruct	2K	\~50 MB + vision 50–100 MB	\~50 MB + vision	\~30 MB + vision	\~10 MB dormant
Combat Full — Thinking	4K	\~100 MB + vision 50–100 MB	\~100 MB + vision	\~50 MB + vision	\~20 MB dormant
Combat Full — Conversation	16K	\~800 MB + vision 50–100 MB	\~570 MB + vision	\~40–80 MB + vision	\~20 MB dormant
Combat Full — Coding (research)	8K	\~400 MB + vision	\~285 MB + vision	\~20–40 MB + vision	n/a
Deep Q5	4K	\~1.2 GB	\~850 MB	\~60–120 MB	n/a
Deep Q5	8K	\~2.4 GB	\~1.7 GB	\~120–240 MB	n/a

Combat Full's per-profile KV split: Instruct at 2K halves Thinking's KV (2K vs 4K). Conversation at 16K quadruples it. Vision tokens are capped by max\_dynamic\_patch = 4 regardless of context. The dormant buffer sizes for Conversation's 16K context (operational maximum) so all lower profiles fit with headroom. All profiles share ReTrace's compression ratio (11.1% token retention) — there is no profile-specific ReTrace configuration.

Mode F classification (platform-level mapping from error class to recovery mode):

Mode C (IPC-level recoverable): E\_WIRE\_RING\_NOT\_MAPPED, E\_KV\_COLD\_READ\_FAILED, E\_RELEASE\_FEATURE\_MISMATCH (treated as a recoverable config error — the feature is disabled and a warning is emitted; if the user reinstalls the correct release class, the feature becomes available).

Mode D (model file corruption): E\_STAR\_KV\_SURGERY\_VERSION\_MISMATCH, E\_STAR\_KV\_PAIR\_MISMATCH, E\_DSP\_ARTIFACT\_HASH, E\_VOICE\_MODEL\_MISSING, E\_RETRACE\_UNAVAILABLE.

Mode E (persistent): E\_COMBAT\_PROFILE\_INVALID (Thinking-only failure degrades to Instruct-only with a warning; all-profile failure drops Combat Full entirely), E\_VAULT\_TAMPER\_DETECTED, E\_VAULT\_DECOY\_ACCESSED, E\_ROUTING\_DRIFT\_EXCEEDED (routing disabled for session; escalates to Mode F across sessions), E\_BROADCAST\_BUS\_DRIFT\_EXCEEDED.

Mode F (cascading persistent): any of the above when it repeats across sessions.

Informational (no mode transition): E\_DESTRUCTIVE\_INSTRUCT\_OVERRIDE, E\_DESTRUCTIVE\_PROTECTION\_DISABLED, E\_VOICE\_FX\_NEURAL\_VC\_TOO\_SLOW, E\_VOICE\_CLONE\_REFUSED, E\_VAULT\_UNLOCK\_FAILED, E\_VAULT\_RATE\_LIMITED, E\_MUSIC\_BIT\_PERFECT\_UNAVAILABLE, E\_VOICESTUDIO\_CLONE\_REFUSED.

Module-specific failure codes and their Mode A–F classification are in each module chapter and in SUL-LEDGER/failures.md.

3.5 UI component catalog (base)

Base components preserved: CombatProfileIndicator, VisionPanel, OcrDebugPanel, DiagnosticsPanel, GameLibraryView, PackManager, SettingsView, OverlaySettings, AudioRoutingPanel, ClipSettings, EmulatorConfig, ModManager, BenchResults, TierSelector.

Rename: CombatVariantIndicator → CombatModeIndicator → CombatProfileIndicator. The old indicator showed Combat Low / Combat Mid / Combat Full as three distinct states. Under the multi-profile design, there is one combat tier (Combat Full) with four profiles (Instruct / Thinking / Conversation / Coding / Auto). The new indicator shows: active profile; if Auto, the router's last decision (profile + source) with confidence; if user override, a lock icon; if router disabled, a warning chip. The old CombatVariantIndicator and CombatModeIndicator APIs are removed — they no longer correspond to valid states. CombatFullStatusIndicator (detailed diagnostic view, Ch. 10 §10.15) and CombatProfileIndicator (compact chip) both consume CombatProfileSelected.

3.6 Diagnostics bundle (framework)

Base contents: system info (GPU, RAM, CPU, driver versions), config snapshot, recent logs (last 24h), crash dumps (last 5), telemetry ring dump (last 1000 events), pack manifest, tier load history, benchmark cache.

Additional contents: the module-specific history files (vault\_history.json, music\_history.json, broadcast\_history.json, csi\_history.json, bci\_history.json, security\_toolkit\_history.json, voicestudio\_history.json, degradation.log, kv\_method\_history.json, spec\_chain\_history.json, audio\_artifact\_history.json, combat\_profile\_history.json, search\_pipeline.log, retrace\_history.json, ooda\_tool\_history.json, frame\_gen\_history.json, audio\_governor\_history.json, stt\_history.json, webview\_history.json) are documented in their owning module chapters.

Bundle is zstd-compressed and user-shareable (no PII; redaction applied to paths). Upload to Sentry optional (Ch. 16 §16.11); default is local-only.

4.2 Cross-cutting validator rules

These are the rules that touch more than one module. Module-specific rules are in the owning chapter's config section.

All speculation chains terminate in "none" (E\_SPEC\_CHAIN\_UNTERMINATED).

Every tier with a draft model has an explicit chain (E\_SPEC\_TYPE\_UNSET).

kv\_cache\_k == kv\_cache\_v when fa\_\* = true and \[ai.kv\_tier] method is not star\_kv, gaac, or an asymmetric-friendly backend (palquant/puzzlekv/jolt/turbo3/tcq) (E\_KV\_ASYMMETRIC\_FA).

audio.dsp.stability\_check\_on\_load == true.

wire.ring\_view\_enabled == true requires sul-wire:default Tauri capability.

frame\_gen.enabled = true with any per-game frame\_gen.engine != "off" and anti\_cheat.kernel\_level = true → rejected with E\_CFG.

frame\_gen.base\_fps\_gate < 25 → rejected (safety floor).

audio.governor.max\_buffer\_samples > 2048 → rejected (latency bug, not a feature).

Combat Full has exactly one chain (combat\_chain). Per-profile chains (combat\_instruct\_chain / combat\_thinking\_chain / combat\_conversation\_chain / combat\_coding\_chain) are rejected with E\_CFG — the target model is the same, so there is one chain.

\[ai.combat\_full.thinking] context < \[ai.combat\_full.instruct] context → E\_CFG. Thinking profile must have a larger context than Instruct.

\[ai.combat\_full.thinking] reasoning\_budget = 0 → E\_CFG. Thinking profile must have reasoning enabled (positive budget or -1 for unbounded).

\[ai.combat\_full.conversation] context < \[ai.combat\_full.thinking] context → E\_CFG. Conversation must have a larger context than Thinking.

\[ai.combat\_full.conversation] reasoning\_budget = 0 → E\_CFG. Conversation must have reasoning enabled (256 is the default).

\[ai.combat] profile = "instruct" | "thinking" | "conversation" | "coding" with destructive\_action\_always\_thinking = true is allowed but warns at startup — the user's fixed profile will be overridden for destructive actions. This is documented, not rejected. Overlay shows a warning chip on CombatProfileIndicator.

\[ai.combat] profile = "auto" requires \[ai.combat\_router] enabled = true (E\_CFG). "auto" without a router makes no sense.

\[ai.combat\_router] enabled = false requires \[ai.combat] profile to be a fixed value ("instruct", "thinking", "conversation", "coding", or "off"). profile = "auto" with router disabled is E\_CFG. profile = "off" with router enabled is also E\_CFG (no router to run).

\[ai.combat] profile = "conversation" requires \[net.search] backend != "disabled" (E\_CFG).

Both \[vision] retrace\_enabled and \[ai.combat\_full] retrace\_enabled must be true. Combat Full ships only with ReTrace. The config validator rejects any configuration where either is false while \[ai.combat\_full] is present.

net.search.verification\_packet must be true if net.search.backend != "disabled".

ai.combat\_full.instruct\_web\_search\_enabled must be true if net.search.backend != "disabled" (all Combat Full profiles depend on it for SimpleQA accuracy).

toolprm\_enabled = true with toolprm\_disabled\_on\_kernel\_ac = false and any per-game anti\_cheat.kernel\_level = true → rejected with E\_CFG. The ceiling is structural, not a preference.

\[ai.speculative.medusa\_temperature\_scaling] must be true → E\_MEDUSA\_TEMP\_SCALING\_MISSING otherwise.

Medusa heads must be shared-LM-head variant → E\_MEDUSA\_OWN\_HEAD\_VARIANT otherwise.

\[ai.optimization] quant = "sul\_quant" requires A.96 to have passed on the current hardware; otherwise sul-quant is hidden and llama.cpp Q4\_K\_S is used (warning, not error).

\[ai.kv\_tier] method must be a recognized value (auto, star\_kv, gaac, palquant, puzzlekv, jolt, turbo3, tcq, uncompressed) → E\_CFG otherwise.

\[ai.speculative] draft\_kv\_compress\_threshold\_mb must be in \[16, 64] → E\_CFG otherwise.

\[ai.speculative] draft\_refresh\_interval\_steps must be in \[8, 128] → E\_CFG otherwise.

\[ai.combat\_full] toolprm\_model must be "sul\_toolprm\_enc" (default) or "toolrm\_qwen3\_4b" (ED only). Validator rejects "toolrm\_qwen3\_4b" when anti\_cheat.kernel\_level = true for any game (E\_CFG).

Module-specific validator rules (audio routing, voice FX, STT, emulation, vault, auth, webview, music, broadcast, CSI, BCI, GEV, security, VoiceStudio) are documented verbatim in each module chapter's config section. The rule numbering above is the cross-cutting subset; the module chapters carry their own numbering starting from their section prefix (e.g., Ch. 4's audio rules are A-1 through A-42; Ch. 5's music rules are M-1 through M-4; Ch. 6's broadcast rules are B-1 through B-66).

Release-plan validation rules (cross-cutting rules 29–34):

Every \[features.\*] toggle must be assigned to exactly one release class in releases.md. Any unassigned toggle is E\_CFG at startup.

Every A.2 gate referenced by a releases.md component list must exist in SUL-LEDGER/gates.md. A dangling reference is E\_CFG at startup.

A release class listed in releases.md must have a matching reference-config block. Missing reference config is E\_CFG at cargo xtask config-check time.

The release that produced the running binary is recorded in %APPDATA%/SUL/release.toml at install time. The config validator reads it and refuses to enable any \[features.\*] toggle whose release class is later than the installed release class (E\_RELEASE\_FEATURE\_MISMATCH). This is the structural guarantee that "every release is a strict superset of the previous one."

Every Tier 1 event listed in releases.md must be classified as Tier 1-core (R0) or as belonging to a specific release class. A Tier 1 event whose class is not defined is E\_CFG at build time.

When cargo xtask config-check runs, the compat validator walks the §10 matrix against the enabled feature set for the installed release (drawn from releases.md \[release.R&lt;n&gt;].components) and emits a coverage metric — the fraction of the toggle space actually tested by the release's reference configuration. A coverage metric below the release's declared minimum is a warning, not an error. The coverage metric is written to \[compat] log and surfaced in Diagnostics.

#35 — Layered VRAM ceiling (general posture). At every launch, after resolving the enabled feature set and the current game state, the config validator compares the total SUL VRAM footprint against the layered ceiling (Brief §7.5). Above the idle ceiling with no game running: E_CFG. Above 2 GB with a game running and combat AI off: warning, not error. Above 3 GB with a game running and combat AI on: E_CFG. Deep / broadcast 4K / FG with a game running: requires the user to accept a Tier 1 confirmation (the launch proceeds only after the modal). The ceiling is a cap, not a target — the validator reports "headroom" but never consumes it. The "minimize, don't trade" rule is enforced by the individual feature gates (A.54, A.96, A.97, A.99, A.100); this validator rule enforces only the aggregate ceiling.

5\. Master Compatibility Matrix

Explicit conflicts, dependency chains, VRAM budget checks, DSP budget checks, and anti-cheat structural refusals. This is the authoritative matrix that §2.1, §2.8, and every module chapter reference.

Enforcement: cargo xtask config-check runs at every launch before model load. Load config, resolve toggles, walk compatibility matrix, auto-disable resolvable conflicts with warning dialog, E\_CFG for unresolvable conflicts, warn for missing dependencies, warn or refuse for VRAM over-budget against the layered ceiling (Brief §7.5): above the idle ceiling with no game → E_CFG; above 2 GB with a game and combat AI off → warning; above 3 GB with a game and combat AI on → E_CFG; Deep / broadcast 4K / FG with a game → Tier 1 confirmation. The 10% tolerance applies within each layer. Auto-resolutions logged to \[compat] and compat.log.

UI enforcement: Settings → Features shows every toggle with real-time compatibility check; Settings → Performance shows every optimization with "would this fit?" indicator; enabling an incompatible toggle triggers a confirmation modal; VRAM budget bar updates live.

5.2 Dependency chains

\[ai.combat\_full.conversation] requires \[ai.combat\_full.thinking] context to be defined first (Conversation extends Thinking's shared context).

\[ai.combat\_full.thinking] requires \[ai.combat\_full.instruct] context (Thinking > Instruct in context size).

\[ai.combat\_full.coding] requires \[ai.combat\_full.conversation] (Conversation 16K > Coding 8K/16K ceiling).

sul-fg requires VK\_LAYER\_PATH + VK\_INSTANCE\_LAYERS env at spawn — set only when FG is enabled for that game and anti\_cheat.kernel\_level == false.

sul-broadcast requires sul-broadcast-video + sul-broadcast-audio + encoder backend available.

sul-music-engine exclusive mode requires device-coordination check (Ch. 4 §4.3) to pass.

sul-voice-fx requires sul-dsp graph and sul-audio WASAPI layer.

sul-prosody runs on WASAPI buffer from sul-audio — requires sul-audio to be initialized.

sul-stt consumes sul-audio's dual-track ring — requires sul-audio to be initialized.

sul-toolprm runs inside sul-agent's beam search — requires sul-agent and Combat Full to be loaded.

sul-kv-compress runs inside sul-ai-native's KV layer — requires sul-ai-native.

sul-spec-draft runs inside sul-ai-native — requires sul-ai-native.

sul-quant is build-time/load-time — the runtime consumes the resulting GGUF.

sul-optimize disabled entirely when anti\_cheat.kernel\_level == true for the target game (structural).

sul-sandbox (Windows Sandbox) refuses to run kernel-level AC titles in the VM (hypervisor detection barrier — technical constraint, not policy).

sul-vfs not mounted on kernel-AC titles.

ETW per-process disabled on kernel-AC titles.

sul-csi requires ESP32 node reachable at startup.

sul-bci requires OpenBCI hardware connected and model loaded.

sul-gev requires wgpu-compatible GPU and feed reachability.

sul-security-toolkit requires Docker available; each tool additionally requires a signed consent file before running.

sul-voicestudio requires VoiceStudio model files present; clone\_voice only accepts character voice presets from licensed catalog.

sul-heretic is build-time only — no runtime dependency.

5.3 VRAM budget checks (reference rig: RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB)

#### Layered VRAM budget (applies to all games)

The general layered ceiling replaces HD2's old 2.5 GB special case. See Brief §7.5.

| State | Ceiling | What's loaded |
|---|---|---|
| Idle | ≤500 MB | UI, IPC, watchdog, telemetry |
| Game running, combat AI off | ≤2 GB (25% of 8 GB) | Substrate + OCR + prosody + state |
| Game running, combat AI on | ≤3 GB (37.5% of 8 GB) | Substrate + Combat Full stack |
| Deep / broadcast 4K / FG | Explicit exception | User-invoked with Tier 1 confirmation |

R0 case (no ReTrace, no ToolPRM): Combat Full Instruct ~1.65–1.75 GB + OCR ~21 MB = ~1.67–1.77 GB. Fits under 3 GB with ~1.23 GB headroom.

R0.1 case (ReTrace passed, ToolPRM not yet): Combat Full ~1.30–1.35 GB + OCR ~21 MB = ~1.32–1.37 GB. Fits under 3 GB with ~1.63 GB headroom.

R2+ case (ReTrace + ToolPRM + full spec chain): Combat Full ~1.3–1.45 GB + ToolPRM ~60–180 MB + OCR ~21 MB = ~1.53–1.65 GB. Fits under 3 GB with ~1.35 GB headroom.

Deep + game co-residence: explicitly refused under the general posture. Deep is for no-game coding. If the user invokes Deep with a game running, the compatibility validator raises a Tier 1 confirmation; accepting it records the exception.

5.4 DSP budget checks

DSP chain	p99	Verdict

sul-dsp baseline	≤8 ms at 512/48k on AVX2	Fits WASAPI period
\+ voice FX combined (pitch + formant + ring mod)	≤8 ms total	Fits
\+ HRTF loopback	risk of >8 ms	Auto-disable if >800 µs
Routing matrix hardware bus	within 5 ms of native WASAPI period	Fits
Routing matrix virtual bus	within 5 ms of cable native latency	Fits
Broadcast channel strip × 12 channels × 12 buses	<6% of one core	Fits

5.5 Anti-cheat structural refusals

Feature	kernel\_level: true	kernel\_level: false

Frame generation	Refused (E\_REFUSAL\_POLICY)	Allowed per per-game config
Flip-model overlay	Refused (external DComp only)	Opt-in per game
VFS	Not mounted	Per-module config
ETW per-process	Disabled	Opt-in per game
Game-hook capture	Refused (E\_REFUSAL\_POLICY)	Opt-in
sul-optimize	Disabled entirely	Enabled for ED only
Mod loading (mods\_allowed\_online: false)	N/A (mods blocked)	Allowed per per-game config
Broadcast game-hook capture	Refused	Opt-in
sul-sandbox hardware passthrough	Refused (bare-metal only)	Allowed for testing

A coverage metric below the release's declared minimum is a warning, not an error. The metric is written to \[compat] log and surfaced in Diagnostics.

Reference rig. RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB / Ryzen 5 5600X / 64 GB DDR4 / 970 EVO Plus. R3 optionally specifies a 12 GB+ baseline.

Profiling toolchain. flamegraph (CPU profiling, flamegraph-rs/flamegraph, R.8). cargo asm (SIMD/AVX2 codegen verification). criterion (micro-benchmarks, bheisler/criterion.rs). miri (UB detection, rust-lang/miri, R.8). loom (concurrency model checking, tokio-rs/loom, R.8). Kani (formal verification, model-checking/kani-github-action, R.10).

PGO workload: xtask pgo train runs scripted session (launch → load Combat Full → 10 inferences → open overlay → 10s capture → close).

Sustained benchmark: xtask bench-sustained runs 10-minute continuous inference, measures tok/s at end (catches thermal throttling). Run 10× to populate p99 for entries like \[ai.deep] tok\_per\_sec.

Kani in CI for sul-trust, sul-ring, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog, sul-vault-core, plus sul-ai-native ReTrace paths:

yaml

\- uses: model-checking/kani-github-action@v0.57

&#x20; with:

&#x20;   args: --tests -p sul-trust -p sul-ring -p sul-quarantine -p sul-watchdog -p sul-vault-core -p sul-ai-native

CI time increases \~4 minutes. Does not replace Miri. Both run.

Failure-injection test suite — every from-scratch crate gains --features=failure-injection. CI runs one invocation per failure class. The module-specific invocation lists are in each module chapter; the platform-level list:

bash

cargo test -p sul-vault-core --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=vt-1

cargo test -p sul-vault-core --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=vt-2

cargo test -p sul-vault-core --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=vt-3

cargo test -p sul-vault-core --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=vt-4

cargo test -p sul-vault-core --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=vt-5

cargo test -p sul-agent --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=mo-1

cargo test -p sul-agent --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=mo-2

cargo test -p sul-agent --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=mo-4

cargo test -p sul-ai-native --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=rt-4

Audio allocator instrumentation: sul-dsp and sul-voice use a custom #\[global\_allocator] in tests that panics on any allocation in the audio callback thread. sul-voice-fx inherits this instrumentation — the FX chain runs in the same callback thread, and a single allocation there is a p99 budget breach, not just a quality issue. sul-gb's APU mixing path is instrumented for per-frame allocation count = 0 (the whole audio and video hot loop); the AVX2 path is the only block exempt from the #\[deny(unsafe\_code)] policy and it is still required to be allocation-free. sul-music-engine's audio callback is instrumented the same way — zero allocations in the callback thread. sul-broadcast-audio's audio callback is instrumented the same way — zero allocations in the callback thread.

11\. Development workflow

11.1 Parallel agent development (four lanes, DAG-ordered waves)

Four lanes: Emulator Core, AI/Jarvis, UI/UX, IPC/Overlay. DAG-ordered waves:

Wave 1 (Emulator Foundation): Phase 1 libretro integration, crates/sul-emu adapter wrapper, CLI fallback.

Wave 1.5: sul-wire prototype (framing layer, ring view) — ships before Wave 2.

Wave 2a (AI core + overlay + prosody): sul-ai-native single llama.cpp build, sul-agent Think-Then-Act loop, Combat Full profile router (sul-agent::combat\_profile), sul-prosody classifier, DComp overlay (external).

Wave 2b (Audio + vision + coding tiers): WASAPI exclusive, sul-ocr INT8 pipeline, sul-vlm scene backends, Deep Q5/Q4 selector. Audio governor prototype + shipping (sul-audio-governor). Frame generation prototype + shipping (sul-fg) with emulator adapter. Combat Full multi-profile fine-tuning pipeline (Ch. 10 §10.8) — mode-tagged data + router-aware ToolPRM training — is a Wave 2b deliverable, because the Combat Full checkpoint is not shippable until the fine-tuned model demonstrates per-profile BFCL ≥65 and router accuracy ≥95% (A.63). sul-quant SPEED-Q wrap (A.96) is a Wave 2b deliverable, because without it the VRAM posture (Brief §7.5) is tighter than it needs to be. sul-toolprm cross-encoder distillation (A.100) is a Wave 2b deliverable, because without it ToolPRM is structurally disabled on HD2. sul-kv-compress trait and STAR-KV/GAAC backends are Wave 2b deliverables; alternative backends (PalQuant/PuzzleKV/JoLT/turbo3/TCQ) are Wave 3a.

Wave 2c: sul-dsp and sul-voice prototype + shipping (wave prototype follows core audio stability).

Wave 2d (Music player): sul-music process scaffold, sul-music-engine bit-perfect path, DSP chain, sul-music-tags, sul-music-lyrics, audio cutter, taskbar controls. Music player gates A.119–A.124.

Wave 2e (Broadcast engine): sul-broadcast process scaffold, sul-broadcast-video compositor + encoder admission, sul-broadcast-audio mixer + routing matrix + USB/IP virtual devices + VBAN, ISO recording, agent API. Broadcast gates A.126–A.134.

Wave 2f (Auth + toggles): sul-auth-app (app-level auth), sul-toggle (feature + performance toggle registry), sul-compat (compatibility matrix and resolution engine). Gates A.114–A.117.

Wave 3a (VFS + watchdog + KV tier): sul-vfs passthrough, process monitoring in sul-watchdog, sul-kv-tier (LRU + attention heuristic; ARGUS deferred, STAR-KV/GAAC/Lynx). sul-kv-compress alternative backends (PalQuant/PuzzleKV/JoLT/turbo3/TCQ) with A.97 gates. sul-spec-draft RIFT wrapper (dormant until draft cache >32 MB). sul-vault-core implementation starts here.

Wave 3b (Distillation research sprint): GAD/CADENCE training per Ch. 10 §10.6 three-gate procedure.

Wave 3c: Search pipeline + ReTrace integration + Combat Full fine-tuning (already in Wave 2b). RustXNG MCP integration; adblock-rust pre-fetch filter; readdown extractor; excerpt-select layer; verification packet builder (AFEV, SLED, Verideck, fallacy detection); ReTrace encoder (saliency from InternViT attention); dormant buffer on STAR-KV compressed paged format; backtracking injection layer; OODA-Tool scaffold (Ch. 10 §10.11); TSCG schema compilation (Ch. 10 §10.11). ReTrace is a shipping blocker — Combat Full does not ship without it. GitHub search tool + knowledge pack sulpack type + full-history KV reuse (sul-net and sul-agent) are Wave 3c deliverables for the Conversation profile.

Wave 4 (Optimize + native adapters + vault + WebView): sul-optimize (Elite Dangerous only), native emulator adapters. optimize + fg co-scheduling (A.76) is wired once both Wave 2b and Wave 4 have landed. sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, sul-voice-auth ship in Wave 4 (they are storage/auth subsystems, not inference subsystems — they depend on stable IPC, trust, and config). WebView hardening (\[webview] config, three CI gates) ships in Wave 4 as well.

Wave 5 (RIFT + spec-draft): sul-spec-draft RIFT wrapper is built in Wave 3a but stays dormant. When Deep context grows past 32K (research-gated) or a future tier grows an external drafter, it activates.

Wave 5a (Advanced sensing): sul-csi, sul-bci, sul-gev, sul-security-toolkit, sul-voicestudio. These build on the stable core (Wave 1–2) and the auth/vault layer (Wave 4). Each ships as a gated shipping component per its individual gate (A.136–A.143). sul-heretic build-time integration for uncensored models (A.144) ships alongside.

Worktree isolation, merge gates via cargo test. sccache shared cache (5–10× faster rebuilds). rust-lld linker. cargo nextest for test runs.

Developer workflow & xtask orchestration extensions (non-shipping dev tooling):
- Root `CLAUDE.md` fuses Karpathy coding discipline (minimal abstraction, test-first, surgical diffs) with §11.3's 13 AI-only rules.
- `DEV-WORKFLOW.md` (non-normative) maps gstack/CrewAI-style role gates (Release Manager, QA, Doc Engineer) onto the four parallel lanes.
- `xtask plan --wave <n>` reads `SUL-LEDGER/releases.md` to emit a dependency-aware JSON task DAG (claude-task-master pattern).
- `xtask learn-patterns` mines recent git diffs to propose candidate `SUL-LEDGER/guards.md` entries for human review.
- `xtask simulate-config --config <toml>` runs dry-run VRAM, latency, and fallback simulation against `baselines.md` without loading weights (enhances A.117).
- `xtask pipeline --release R<n>` emits and executes a node-based CI DAG (`config-check → electron-audit → tauri-capability-audit → webview-runtime-audit → bench → release`).
- Optional: Paperclip (MIT) may be used as a local agent-management UI in development; it is not a SUL dependency and is not shipped.

11.2 Test-first harness

Test-First (Ralph Loop) mandatory. Agents write failing test reproducing bug/feature before implementation. Harness: unit tests for sul-core, integration tests for IPC rings, mocked external APIs, Miri on every unsafe block (mandatory for sul-ring, sul-emu-libretro, sul-vfs, sul-arcade, sul-kv-tier, sul-kv-compress, sul-ocr, sul-vlm, sul-vision-sidecar, sul-optimize, sul-prosody, sul-dsp, sul-voice, sul-wire, sul-ai-native ReTrace paths, sul-agent OODA-Tool and Combat Full profile router, sul-net search pipeline unsafe paths, sul-fg layer entry point and command-forwarding paths, sul-gb AVX2 audio mixing path, sul-savestate libretro shim, sul-quant SPEED-Q FFI paths and APEX planner, sul-spec-draft RIFT selection/refresh, sul-toolprm cross-encoder FFI paths, sul-vault-core AEAD construction and IOCP pipeline, sul-face-auth RetinaFace/ArcFace FFI, sul-voice-auth sherpa-onnx FFI, sul-music-engine WASAPI exclusive path, sul-broadcast-video compositor and encoder paths, sul-broadcast-audio audio callback and routing matrix, sul-csi FFT processing, sul-bci neural decoding). CI rejects PRs without test file change unless #no-test tag. Miri documentation; loom documentation. Kani formal verification (§10) runs alongside Miri for sul-trust, sul-ring, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog. Router determinism is tested by proptest over synthetic signal sets — a given set of inputs must always produce the same profile decision (no nondeterministic classification).

Failure-injection is mandatory for every from-scratch crate. --features=failure-injection gate; each crate supports --force-failure=&lt;id&gt; for its failure classes. New failure classes from this handoff: qt-1 (sul-quant SPEED-Q A.96 fail → fall back to llama.cpp Q4\_K\_S), kc-1 (sul-kv-compress backend A.97 fail → fall back to STAR-KV/GAAC), sd-1 (sul-spec-draft dormant check), tp-1 (sul-toolprm A.100 fail → no-PRM baseline), vt-1/vt-2/vt-3 (vault unlock fail / tamper detected / hardware root unavailable), cp-1 (Coding profile A.101 fail → research only), mo-4 (profile routing ambiguity → small-LLM fallback), br-1 (broadcast admission controller refusal), br-2 (broadcast USB/IP device enumeration failure), br-3 (broadcast audio bus drift exceeded), mu-1 (music player exclusive mode refused by device coordination), mu-2 (music player bit-perfect path unavailable), csi-1 (CSI node disconnected), bci-1 (BCI calibration failure), gev-1 (geospatial feed unavailable), sec-1 (security tool container failure), vs-1 (VoiceStudio model unavailable).

11.3 AI-only code shape

Thirteen rules, zero shipped-binary cost:

Structured doc-comments: /// Inputs / Outputs / Errors / Complexity. Cached in codebase\_map.sulpack.

\#\[tracing::instrument] on every async boundary. <1% runtime.

Exhaustive matching, no wildcards. #\[non\_exhaustive] on error enums.

Function size ceiling: 60 lines.

Tests referenced by ID in doc-comments.

Error messages encode the fix. thiserror + #\[help("...")]. #\[cold] on every error constructor. (Diagnostic `#[help]` metadata is provided via `miette::Diagnostic` paired with `thiserror`; `#[likely]`/`#[unlikely]` use a stable Rust branch-hint helper, and Win32/C++ FFI calls sit behind thin OS adapter traits so Miri/Kani verify pure-Rust ring, nonce, and state-machine logic cleanly.)

\#\[inline] on every public fn under 20 lines in from-scratch crates.

\#\[likely] / #\[unlikely] on hot-loop branches.

\#\[cold] on error constructors and panic paths.

Collapse ternary/boolean patterns. Prefer (x >= y).then\_some(()) over if/else when compiler optimizes it away. \~60% token cost reduction per pattern, zero runtime change.

Positional tuple structs are permitted for wire/IPC types when field meaning is fixed by schema; named fields are required for domain types. §3.2's named-field IPC structs are compliant.

\#\[error] as short codes, #\[help] as prose. #\[error("E\_CFG")] + #\[help("check {path} exists and is valid JSON")]. Mode F classifies on enum variant, not string. Halves tokens per log line.

Test names ≤24 chars, t\_&lt;topic&gt;\_&lt;scope&gt;. t\_ring\_wrap\_10m not test\_ring\_buffer\_handles\_wraparound\_correctly\_under\_10m\_operations.

Effect: −20–30% wall-clock on agent development loop.

11.4 Contract template

Every from-scratch crate contract has these sections:

Purpose — one sentence.

Architecture — module structure, data flow.

Compatibility — how it interacts with the existing system (FA, speculation, audio pipeline, IPC, and for sul-agent: the Combat Full profile router).

Failure taxonomy — error codes this crate emits (with SUL-LEDGER/failures.md references).

Fallback chain — ordered array of fallbacks on failure.

Performance contract — measured targets with p50/p99.

Test requirements — Miri, integration tests, failure-injection tests, and for sul-agent: router determinism, destructive-action recall, and per-profile behavior tests.

Failure-injection section — which --force-failure flags this crate supports; what each one tests.

Fallback chain section — explicit enumeration of fallback order with success criteria per rung.

Failure-injection test suite: every from-scratch crate gains --features=failure-injection. CI runs one invocation per failure class. The platform-level list is in §10; each module chapter carries its module-specific list. Every failure in SUL-LEDGER/failures.md has at least one injection test. The router-specific failures (RT-4, MO-1, MO-2, MO-3, MO-4) are tested in sul-agent and sul-ai-native: mo-1 forces the router to select Thinking profile while Thinking is marked OOM; asserts Instruct fallback fires and CombatRouterFallback telemetry emits. mo-2 forces a destructive-action trigger while the user has overridden to Instruct; asserts the safety invariant overrides the user and E\_DESTRUCTIVE\_INSTRUCT\_OVERRIDE + CombatProfileDenied fire. rt-4 forces both pre-created contexts (Instruct 2K, Thinking 4K) to fail allocation; asserts E\_COMBAT\_PROFILE\_INVALID fires and Combat Full is dropped entirely. mo-4 forces ambiguous signals; asserts small-LLM fallback fires; if that fails, default to Instruct with E\_COMBAT\_PROFILE\_AMBIGUOUS.

New failure classes: qt-1/qt-2/qt-3 (sul-quant A.96 fail → fall back to llama.cpp Q4\_K\_S / SPEED-Q 4-bit / SPEED-Q 4-bit uniform), kc-1/kc-2 (sul-kv-compress A.97 fail → fall back to STAR-KV/GAAC / GAAC), sd-1/sd-2 (sul-spec-draft dormant check / refresh stall), tp-1/tp-2/tp-3 (sul-toolprm A.100 fail → no-PRM baseline), vt-1/vt-2/vt-3/vt-4/vt-5 (vault unlock / tamper / hardware root unavailable / decoy accessed / rate limited), cp-1 (Coding profile A.101 fail → research only), mu-1/mu-2 (music exclusive mode refused / bit-perfect unavailable), br-1/br-2/br-3 (broadcast admission refusal / USB-IP enumeration failure / bus drift), csi-1/csi-2 (CSI node disconnected / edge model load fail), bci-1/bci-2 (BCI calibration failure / model load fail), gev-1/gev-2 (geospatial feed unavailable / geolocation model unavailable), sec-1/sec-2 (security tool container failure / GPU unavailable), vs-1/vs-2 (VoiceStudio model unavailable / voice cloning attempt detected).
