2.24 Game registry (game_registry.json)
The per-game launch profile registry. This is the canonical source for [emu.gb] / [emu.savestate] / per-game overrides and for the anti-cheat block hash verification.

combat_exec_preload is not present (Hammer cut). combat_low_co_resident, combat_mid_co_resident, and combat_full_reload are not present — those flags belonged to the old three-combat-tier design, which is cut. Under the multi-profile design, Combat Full is the only combat checkpoint and all its profiles share the same weights; there is no co-residence to compute and no reload to configure.

Each launch profile carries a combat block (replacing the old co-residence flags), a frame_gen block, and an audio block.

Per-game combat block field semantics:

profile — "auto" | "instruct" | "thinking" | "conversation" | "coding" | "off". When "auto", the router decides per turn. When a fixed profile is set, the user has forced it; the router still enforces the destructive-action override (Ch. 10 §10.9 signal priority 1). When "off", Combat Full is not loaded for this game (unusual, but supported). Note: "off" is distinct from destructive_action_always_thinking = false below. "off" disables the entire model; destructive_action_always_thinking = false disables only the destructive-action override.

router_enabled — true | false. When false, the router is bypassed and the profile is fixed by profile (equivalent to force-selecting a specific profile). Rare; useful for diagnostic scenarios. Not recommended for normal use.

destructive_action_always_thinking — true | false. Default true. When true, destructive actions always route to Thinking profile regardless of user override — this is the safety invariant. When false, the safety invariant is disabled and the router respects user profile selection even for destructive actions. Setting this to false is a Tier 1 event (releases.md) and requires the OS-level approval modal. This flag exists for the specific scenario where a user has a legitimate reason to execute destructive actions without the Thinking-profile confirmation — for example, a scripted batch operation the user has already reviewed. It is not a general setting; it is a per-game escape hatch for a specific workflow. The global [ai.combat] destructive_action_always_thinking and the per-game combat.destructive_action_always_thinking are the same field at two scopes; per-game wins (base precedence, Ch. 1 §2.8). The "always" is not decorative — it marks this as a hard safety invariant rather than a routing preference, which is why disabling it is a Tier 1 event at either scope.

For Helldivers 2, the frame_gen block is structurally locked to "engine": "off" — the config validator (Ch. 1 §4.2) rejects any other value when anti_cheat.kernel_level == true. The combat block defaults to "profile": "auto" with router_enabled: true and destructive_action_always_thinking: true. HD2's combat profile allows all four profiles (Instruct for fast execution during gameplay, Thinking for destructive-action confirmation — e.g., "confirm use of a stratagem that will kill your teammate", Conversation for pre-game and post-game dialogue, Coding for between-mission work). All profiles fit within the 2.5 GB HD2 ceiling together (~1.3–1.45 GB total, single checkpoint).

For Elite Dangerous, the frame_gen block uses "engine": "auto" and "multiplier": "2x" as the shipped default. FG is safe on ED: single-player, no kernel AC, Vulkan presentable via DXVK. The combat block matches HD2's defaults — "profile": "auto", router_enabled: true, destructive_action_always_thinking: true.

HD2 Combat Full VRAM calculation (replaces the old co-residence calculation). Combat Full is a single checkpoint with four profiles. Instruct: ~1.65–1.75 GB base, ~1.30–1.35 GB with ReTrace. Thinking: ~1.70–1.80 GB base, ~1.35–1.45 GB with ReTrace. Conversation: ~1.25–1.30 GB with ReTrace (16K but no game — the extra KV is ~800 MB in q8_0, compressed to ~40–80 MB with STAR-KV). Coding: ~1.15–1.30 GB with ReTrace. All profiles share the same weights (~1.05 GB Q4_K_S) and differ only in KV cache. Under ReTrace (mandatory optimization per Phase 2), Combat Full in any profile fits comfortably under Phase 2's 3 GB general combat ceiling. In R0 (no ReTrace, no ToolPRM), Combat Full Instruct fits at ~1.67–1.77 GB. There is no co-residence calculation — Combat Full is the only combat model, and all profiles are the same model. The HD2 profile does not need co-residence flags. The 2.5 GB ceiling is satisfied by any profile alone, and the router flips profiles in <50 ms without a model reload. sul-toolprm cross-encoder (~60–180 MB Q4, A.100) also fits under 2.5 GB alongside Combat Full, restoring PRM rescoring that was previously disabled on HD2.

Elite Dangerous Combat Full VRAM calculation. ED has no kernel-level anti-cheat and allows co-residency with other tiers. On ED, Combat Full (~1.3–1.45 GB with ReTrace) can co-exist with Deep (~6.46 GB Q5_K_M Q5_K_M with STAR-KV fits at 4K) — but 1.45 + 6.46 = 7.91 GB > 8 GB, so co-residency requires offloading 2–4 layers of Deep (~7.1 GB total, tight but fits). The old three-tier ED co-residence calculation (~5.2 GB for Combat Low + Combat Mid + Combat Full) is obsolete; under the multi-profile design, Combat Full is ~1.3–1.45 GB, and Deep is the only other checkpoint.

Integrity requirement: anti_cheat blocks hash-verified against Ed25519-signed baseline in sul-trust at every launch (Ch. 16 §16.7). Mismatch → hardcoded safe-default.

Hot-reload: file watcher → reload on change.

[emu.gb] and [emu.savestate] module config (from §3.5.1 / §3.6) are in the module chapters; the registry carries per-game overrides. The combined config is:

toml
# Ch. 3, §3.5.1 — sul-gb core selection.
[emu.gb]
core = "auto"                              # "auto" | "sul_gb" | "libretro_gambatte"
accuracy_mode = "strict"                   # "strict" | "fast"
savestate_via_sul_savestate = true

# Ch. 3, §3.6 — save-state ring.
[emu.savestate]
ring_capacity = 4                          # slots; minimum 3 for run_ahead = 2, default 4
compression = "zstd"
compression_level = 1                      # 1 = fast, 3 = balanced, 6 = slow (not recommended for hot path)
worker_threads = 1
Validator rules for [emu.gb] / [emu.savestate] (in addition to ES-1..3 above):

ES-4: [emu.gb] core = "sul_gb" requires the A.90 accuracy gate to have passed on the current hardware; if the gate has not passed, E_GB_ACCURACY_GATE_FAILED at load and the core is forced to "libretro_gambatte" for the session (Mode B).

ES-5: [emu.gb] savestate_via_sul_savestate = false requires the A.91 gate to have failed (otherwise the Rust-native ring is the preferred path).

SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 04 — Audio Pipeline and Voice Stack.md
1. Purpose
The WASAPI backend, the dual-track ring, sul-audio, sul-audio-governor, sul-dsp, sul-voice, sul-voice-fx, sul-stt, and sul-tts. Provides the low-latency, allocation-free audio path that the broadcast mixer (Ch. 6 §6.4) and the music player (Ch. 5 §5.2) feed into and draw from. All three audio subsystems (sul-audio, sul-music, sul-broadcast-audio) coexist under the device-coordination rules in this chapter (§4.3) and the audio governor budget (§4.10).

2. Architecture
2.1 Overview
The audio pipeline is the WASAPI backend, the dual-track ring, sul-audio, sul-audio-governor, sul-dsp, sul-voice, sul-voice-fx, sul-stt, and sul-tts. The pipeline is built on WASAPI in both shared and exclusive modes, with a single governor (sul-audio-governor) as the sole arbiter over sample rate, buffer size, exclusive mode, DSP backend, voice isolation, ducking, and resampling decisions. Individual DSP components (sul-dsp, sul-voice, sul-voice-fx) never make device decisions; they consume the buffer the governor sizes.

2.2 Audio pipeline architecture
Backends:

WASAPI shared mode — cpal + rodio — the default for coexistence with other apps.

WASAPI exclusive mode — wasapi-rs — bit-perfect path for the music player (§4.3 / Ch. 5 §5.2).

Components:

Component	Role	Process
sul-audio	Pipeline host: WASAPI capture (loopback and mic), dual-track ring producer, DSP graph driver, STT/TTS integration point	In-process thread in sul.exe (or dedicated sul-audio process if compiled separately)
sul-audio-governor	Single arbiter: sample rate, buffer size, exclusive mode, DSP backend, voice isolation, ducking, resampling	In-process thread, same process as sul-audio
sul-dsp	Train-freeze-runtime audio DSP graph	In-process thread, same process as sul-audio
sul-voice	cIRM neural voice isolation (sub-3 ms, zero-alloc, zero-lock)	In-process thread, same process as sul-audio
sul-voice-fx	Voicemod-style voice transformation — pitch, formant, character presets, ring mod, bitcrush, EQ	In-process thread, part of sul-dsp graph
sul-prosody	Pitch / energy / speech rate extraction + intent gate	In-process thread in sul.exe (CPU thread pool)
sul-stt	whisper.cpp streaming wrapper	In-process thread, same process as sul-audio
sul-tts	Piper / Kokoro / Higgs Audio TTS synthesis	In-process thread, CPU-only
The dual-track ring is the central data structure. Two tracks, both written by sul-audio's WASAPI capture:

Track 1 — Mic track: raw microphone input (or sul-voice-isolated mic when [audio.voice] enabled = true).

Track 2 — Game loopback track: system audio loopback (all apps, or per-app when WASAPI process loopback is available — Ch. 6 §6.8).

sul-prosody reads from the mic track; sul-stt reads from both (mic for user speech, loopback for game/dialogue transcription); sul-voice-fx inserts into the mic track between isolation and STT when enabled.

Latency budget: WASAPI period is the floor; DSP p99 must fit within it. The governor sizes the buffer to accommodate the longest active FIR (Ch. 1 §5.4 DSP budget table). Default buffer sizes: 512 samples at 48 kHz (interactive), 1024 samples (background listening). The governor never escalates above 1024 samples silently — a longer buffer is a user-visible latency increase, not a silent escalation (validator rule A-8 in §4.17).

Allocation-free callback discipline: the WASAPI callback thread runs at THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL and is instrumented with a custom #[global_allocator] panic-on-alloc test (Ch. 1 §10). sul-dsp, sul-voice, sul-voice-fx, sul-stt's inference path (when reading from the ring), and sul-tts's output path all must satisfy zero-alloc-in-callback.

2.3 Audio device coordination
Three audio subsystems may contend for the same WASAPI device:

sul-audio (game loopback capture, voice isolation, DSP, STT, TTS).

sul-music.exe (music playback, optional WASAPI exclusive — Ch. 5 §5.2).

sul-broadcast-audio (broadcast mixer, virtual devices, VBAN — Ch. 6 §6.4).

Coordination rules:

sul-music.exe's exclusive mode is refused when its device matches sul-audio's device and sul-audio's loopback capture or voice loop is active. Exclusive mode is allowed on a different device.

sul-broadcast-audio monitoring uses shared mode. Exclusive mode is reserved for the music player.

The audio governor (§4.10) is the single arbiter over sul-audio's six decisions. The music player and broadcast mixer have their own budgets ([performance.music] in Ch. 5 §5.5 and [performance.broadcast] in Ch. 6 §6.6) and do not contend with sul-audio's DSP budget because they run in separate processes.

When the music player or broadcast mixer requests exclusive mode on the same device as sul-audio, the compatibility validator refuses the request with E_CFG and the device-coordination logic (Ch. 1 §5) surfaces the reason.

Device change handling: if the device is lost (AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED — AG-3 in §4.13), the governor re-queries the device list, re-runs its six decisions, and resumes on the new default device (or the last-used device if still present). The music player and broadcast mixer follow the same pattern via their own device-change handlers.

2.4 STT — speech to text
The STT path is whisper.cpp wrapped with a streaming pipeline. It consumes the dual-track ring (mic track for user speech, loopback track for game/dialogue) and produces transcripts that flow into the subtitle path, the TTS path (§4.5), and the prosody gate (§4.6).

Config:

toml
[stt]
backend = "whisper_cpp"
model = "tiny.en"
quant = "q5_1"
chunk_ms = 16
vad = "ring_aligned"
silence_removal = true
stereo_split = "auto"
flash_attn = true
audio_ctx = "auto"
thread_affinity = "auto"
hybrid_split = "auto"
language_hint = "auto"
voice_loop_enabled = true
Config semantics:

backend — "whisper_cpp" (shipping). A "streaming_native" alternative exists as A.83 rung 3 research; if that rung passes, a follow-up sul-stt crate is added.

model — tiny.en | base.en | small.en | medium.en. Baseline is tiny.en for combat callouts; small.en only when translation is active.

quant — fp16 | q8_0 | q5_1 | q4_0. q5_1 is the shipping default (~2.3× inference speedup vs fp16 with <2% precision loss).

chunk_ms — 16 ms chunks; matches the ring's slot cadence.

vad — "ring_aligned" coordinates the Silero VAD with the dual-track ring's existing VAD so the two do not double-gate. "none" is rejected during gameplay (validator rule A-38).

silence_removal = true — strip silence before inference (58% audio reduction measured in community deployment).

stereo_split = "auto" — auto-split mic and loopback into mono tracks for the recognizer.

flash_attn = true — must be explicitly set, not left to a default (validator rule A-39). Metal defaults it OFF in whisper-rs; the validator rejects a missing field.

audio_ctx = "auto" — auto-selects 1500 (full 30s window) or 768 (short clips, ~2× faster).

thread_affinity = "auto" — pins the whisper thread away from the game and the audio callback thread.

hybrid_split = "auto" — auto-selects gpu_encoder_cpu_decoder on GPU-present systems (16.5% faster than pure CPU, 21.0% faster than pure GPU, no thermal throttling on Snapdragon 8 Elite reference), falls back to cpu_both on GPU-less systems.

language_hint = "auto" — detects language from the first chunk; used for the STT↔sul-vlm language routing hint.

voice_loop_enabled = true — enables the A.85 voice loop wiring.

Pipeline stages (WhisperPipe pattern):

text
Mic / loopback (dual-track ring)
  → VAD gate (ring-aligned; silence stripped)
  → stereo split (auto)
  → overlapping context window (adaptive)
  → whisper.cpp inference (q5_1, flash_attn, hybrid split if GPU)
  → transcript
Measured baselines (from §4.14 and gate A.83):

Metric	Target	Test
End-to-end latency	< 150 ms median, p99 < 400 ms	stt-bench.py::end_to_end
WER	within 2% of offline Whisper on combat-speech eval set	stt-bench.py::end_to_end
Model size	tiny.en ~20 MB (q5_1), small.en ~150–500 MB	stt-bench.py::quant
Voice loop end-to-end	< 500 ms median, p99 < 900 ms (A.85)	stt-bench.py::voice_loop
Pipeline speedup vs stock whisper.cpp	~10× (measured on call-centre deployment)	stt-bench.py::pipeline_custom
Audio reduction before inference	58%	stt-bench.py::pipeline_custom
Short-clip latency (audio_ctx = 768)	~2× faster than default 1500	stt-bench.py::audio_ctx
flash_attn enabled	1 (binary gate)	stt-bench.py::flash_attn
Validator rules (STT-specific; rules #36–#42):

A-36: [stt] model must be one of {tiny.en, base.en, small.en, medium.en}; any other value is E_CFG at load.

A-37: [stt] quant must be one of {fp16, q8_0, q5_1, q4_0}; the combination (model, quant) must be present in the bundled model manifest; a missing model is E_STT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND (Mode C — fall back to bundled default).

A-38: [stt] vad must not be "none" during gameplay (E_CFG at load if it is, because STT without VAD would feed silence to the recognizer and breach the <150 ms end-to-end gate). Non-gameplay sessions may set vad = "none" only via a diagnostic flag, never config.

A-39: [stt] flash_attn must be explicitly set (not rely on a default). The validator rejects a missing flash_attn field with E_CFG.

A-40: [stt] audio_ctx may be "auto" or an integer in {0, 768, 1500}; any other value is E_STT_AUDIO_CTX_INVALID (Mode C — clamp to default and log).

A-41: [stt] hybrid_split = "gpu_encoder_cpu_decoder" requires [ai] device to be a CUDA or equivalent GPU-capable device (E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED otherwise, Mode C — fall back to gpu_both if GPU present, else cpu_both).

A-42: [stt] voice_loop_enabled = true requires [tts] engine to be a valid, loadable engine (Piper or Kokoro int8 per the manifest); missing TTS engine is E_CFG.

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_STT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND	Model not found	Bundled model missing	Fall back to bundled default (Mode C)
E_STT_WHISPER_INIT_FAILED	Whisper init failed	whisper.cpp fails to initialize	Retry once with CPU-only; if that fails, disable STT for session (Mode A); translation/subtitle path degrades to text-only; voice loop reports "STT unavailable" via overlay
E_STT_AUDIO_CTX_INVALID	audio_ctx invalid	Value not in {0, 768, 1500}	Clamp to default and log (Mode C)
E_STT_FLASH_ATTN_UNAVAILABLE	flash_attn unavailable	Backend doesn't support flash_attn	Fall back to non-flash path — still functional, slower (Mode C)
E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED	Hybrid split unsupported	GPU not present	Fall back to gpu_both if GPU present, else cpu_both (Mode C)
AST guards:

sul-stt (in sul-audio) must not import HTTP client.

sul-stt must read only from the dual-track ring or sul-voice output, never opening a new audio stream.

[stt] flash_attn must be explicitly true (a missing field is an error, not a default).

Tier 1 events (from releases.md): stt:change_model, stt:change_quant, stt:change_backend, stt:toggle_voice_loop. All R1.

STT history file (stt_history.json in the diagnostics bundle, Ch. 1 §3.6): per-session STT state. Records the active model + quant, chunk_ms, hybrid_split path, audio_ctx used on short clips, pipeline stage latencies from the WhisperPipe wrapper (VAD → inference → output), and any fallback events. Backs stt_bench.py post-hoc review and the [stt] baseline context. Contains no raw audio, no transcripts — only pipeline timings, model identifiers, and error codes.

Gate: A.83 (§4.16). Release: R1.

2.5 TTS — text to speech
The TTS path is CPU-only. It synthesizes the agent's spoken responses for the A.85 voice loop. Zero VRAM cost — the GPU belongs to Combat Full.

Config:

toml
[tts]
engine = "piper"                          # "piper" | "kokoro" | "higgs_audio"
voice = "en_GB_northern_english_male"
streaming = true
quant = "int8"
first_sentence_flush_ms = 300
Config semantics:

engine — "piper" (default, MIT license, ~150 ms on desktop CPU, ~1,220 ms on Raspberry Pi reference), "kokoro" (Apache 2.0, ~0.57 RTF int8 on CPU for English), or "higgs_audio" (gated A.162 — see below).

voice — Piper voice ID.

streaming = true — first-sentence streaming: begin TTS synthesis on the first completed sentence, flush at first_sentence_flush_ms max, for a 0.3–0.7 s perceived-latency reduction.

quant = "int8" — Piper int8 quantization; standard.

first_sentence_flush_ms = 300 — max time to wait for the first sentence before flushing.

Why CPU-only: GPU TTS (e.g., Breeze TTS 2 on RTX 4060: 220–472 ms first packet) is not faster than CPU Piper (~150 ms on M2-class), and the VRAM cost of GPU TTS competes with Combat Full. The measured gap does not justify the VRAM.

Baselines (from §4.14):

Metric	Target	Test
Latency	median 150 ms, p99 400 ms (Piper desktop CPU)	tts-bench.py::latency
RTF	median 0.15, p99 0.6 (Piper); Kokoro int8 CPU 0.57 English	tts-bench.py::latency
VRAM	0 MB (TTS never runs on the GPU in the shipping voice loop)	tts-bench.py::latency
#### Higgs Audio engine (A.162)

Higgs Audio (https://www.boson.ai/higgs-audio) is a third TTS engine option alongside Piper (default) and Kokoro. It is gated by A.162:

- Must meet A.88's voice-loop latency gate (<500 ms end-to-end with Combat Full Instruct as reasoning backend).
- Must meet A.85's TTS sub-gate (<150 ms Piper-equivalent latency).
- Must run without GPU offload, or with GPU offload that keeps the total SUL VRAM footprint within the idle ceiling (Brief §7.5) — GPU TTS is not permitted to crowd out Combat Full.

If A.162 fails, Higgs Audio remains a `[DEPRECATED]` evaluation and Piper/Kokoro stay the defaults. If it passes, it ships as a third `[tts] engine` option.

Reference: boson.ai/higgs-audio.

No validator rules for TTS beyond [stt] voice_loop_enabled = true requiring a valid TTS engine (validator A-42).

Failure taxonomy: none at the crate level. If the TTS engine fails to load, the voice loop is disabled with a warning (voice loop status indicator shows "TTS unavailable").

AST guards: none for TTS specifically. Tier 1 events: none for TTS specifically. Release: R1.

2.6 Prosody and intent gate
Contract: §2.6 defines the classifier; the sul-prosody crate row in Ch. 1 §11.5 is the build contract. Gates: none. Baselines: [prosody]. Boundary: Ch. 16 §16.1 (Prosody audio guard). Prosody feeds the Combat Full profile router (Ch. 10 §10.9 signal priority 3–5). Any change to prosody thresholds is a Tier 1 event (releases.md).

sul-prosody classifier runs on the same WASAPI buffer sul-index uses for STT. Prosody features (pitch, energy, speech rate) computed before STT completes; intent gate (EXECUTE / CLARIFY / ASSESS) decided before LLM sees transcript. Zero-token path from audio to intent.

Intent gate decision flow:

Prosody classifier outputs intent + confidence.

If confidence > threshold → intent is authoritative; ControlMsg::IntentClassified with source: ProsodyOnly or ProsodyWithText.

If confidence < threshold → the judgment profile decides (Combat Full Instruct when a game is running, Combat Full Conversation when no game is running). Source: JudgmentModel.

If both low → default_safe_intent = "assess" applied; source: DefaultSafe.

The prosody gate output feeds the Combat Full profile router directly (Ch. 10 §10.9). Its three outputs map as:

Prosody intent	Router profile
EXECUTE	Instruct (fast path)
CLARIFY	Thinking (needs context assessment)
ASSESS	Thinking (deliberate reasoning)
UNKNOWN	Router's own classifier decides
The "judgment profile" in the pre-consolidation design was Combat Low; in the current design it is Combat Full Instruct (fast path) with escalation to Combat Full Thinking if confidence is low. The escalation itself is a router decision, not a hard-coded fallback.

Combat-Confirm sub-role: When a destructive action is about to execute (file deletion, config overwrite, process launch, save-restore, mod install), Combat Full Thinking generates the user-facing warning: "About to overwrite config.toml — 47 changes will be lost. Confirm?" If Thinking mode is unavailable (OOM, model not loaded), Combat Full Instruct generates the same warning as a backup. Both use the same prompt template and the persona "warn before destructive operations" constraint. Zero new model. Under the router, destructive-action detection always routes to Thinking (per Ch. 10 §10.9 signal priority 1) — but the router's guarantee is that Thinking mode is selected for destructive actions, not that Thinking mode is guaranteed available. If Thinking mode is unusable (VRAM OOM during a spike), the router logs CombatRouterFallback and the fallback path (Instruct generating the warning) applies. This is documented, not silent.

Config:

toml
[ai.prosody]
enabled = true
default_safe_intent = "assess"
Baselines ([prosody] section, from Ch. 10):

Metric	Target	Test
Feature extraction latency	p99 <2 ms	bench_prosody.py
Classifier latency	p99 <5 ms	bench_prosody.py
Three-way intent accuracy	≥85%	eval_prosody.py
Gate: none (no gate; ships R1 per releases.md). Tier 1 events: none for the prosody classifier itself. The prosody gate feeds the router; router changes are Tier 1 (combat:change_profile, etc.).

AST guards: sul-prosody runs on WASAPI buffer from sul-audio — requires sul-audio initialized (dependency chain, Ch. 1 §5.2). No AST guard beyond that.

Data privacy: see §4.7. Release: R1.

2.7 Prosody data privacy
Prosody calibration file is local at %APPDATA%\SUL\voice-calibration.json, unsigned, aggregate-only. Raw audio never stored; per-utterance feature vectors not persisted; export and delete fully supported. Ch. 16 §16.1 covers the threat model.

Threat: attacker injects malicious audio to trigger a prosody classifier into an unwanted intent (EXECUTE instead of CLARIFY).

Defense: Prosody calibration is local, unsigned, aggregate-only. Raw audio is never stored; per-utterance features are not persisted. The prosody classifier is CPU-only (no VRAM). Voice isolation (sul-voice) intercepts mic before STT when enabled. The prosody gate is one of several signals — destructive actions always route to Thinking regardless of prosody. An attacker who compromises prosody cannot bypass the safety invariant.

2.8 Audio routing matrix (A.87)
Purpose: Voicemeeter-style N×M input-to-bus router with per-cell gain, per-bus limiter, and per-bus meter. Implemented in sul-audio's WASAPI layer. Inputs are the sources sul-audio already captures; buses are local, stream, monitor, record. Hardware buses bypass virtual cables at the smallest period that fits the FIR; virtual buses use the cable's native period. SUL depends on the user-installed virtual cable (VB-Audio Cable is the de-facto standard; VoiceMeeter's own cable and equivalents are detected) — SUL does not build a virtual audio driver.

Config:

toml
[audio.routing]
enabled = false
virtual_cable_name = "CABLE Input"
buses = ["local", "stream", "monitor", "record"]

[audio.routing.buses.local]
device = "auto"
latency_mode = "hardware"

[audio.routing.buses.stream]
device = "CABLE Input"
latency_mode = "virtual"

[audio.routing.buses.monitor]
device = "auto"
latency_mode = "hardware"

[audio.routing.buses.record]
device = "CABLE Output"
latency_mode = "virtual"

[audio.routing.gains]
# Per-input × per-bus gain (dB). Defaults are 0 dB for local, -6 dB for stream,
# 0 dB for monitor, 0 dB for record.
Validator rules (routing-specific; rules #29–#32):

A-29: [audio.routing] enabled = true requires the configured virtual_cable_name to be detected among the current WASAPI devices; otherwise E_ROUTING_VIRTUAL_CABLE_MISSING and the routing matrix is not enabled for the session (the §4.2 DSP pipeline still runs).

A-30: [audio.routing] buses must be a subset of {local, stream, monitor, record}; an empty list is valid and means "no routing"; a duplicate or unknown bus name is E_CFG.

A-31: Any bus with latency_mode = "hardware" must resolve to a real hardware endpoint; if it resolves to the same endpoint as a virtual bus, E_CFG (routing a hardware endpoint to itself would stack two cable hops).

A-32: [audio.routing] requires [audio] backend = "wasapi" (E_CFG otherwise — routing is a WASAPI-layer concept).

Performance baselines (from §4.14):

[audio.routing] matrix_mix_ms — { median = 0.5, p99 = 1.0, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 25, status = gated, note = "6 inputs × 4 buses, gain-only; four-bus with limiters is 3-5 ms (see limiter_p99_us); A.87 gate" }

[audio.routing] limiter_p99_us — { median = 3000, p99 = 5000, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 20, status = gated, note = "four limiters at 48 kHz / 512-sample buffer on AVX2; A.87 gate" }

[audio.routing] hardware_bus_roundtrip_ms — { median = 12, p99 = 20, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 25, status = gated, note = "within 5 ms of native WASAPI period at 512 samples" }

[audio.routing] virtual_bus_roundtrip_ms — { median = 20, p99 = 40, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 25, status = gated, note = "VB-Cable native; typically reported 10-30 ms per hop" }

[audio.routing] bus_drift_per_hour — { median = 0, p99 = 0, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 0, status = gated, note = "hard gate: zero sample-level drift across buses over 1 hour" }

Gate: A.87 (§4.16). Release: R1.

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_ROUTING_VIRTUAL_CABLE_MISSING	Virtual cable missing	Configured virtual_cable_name not detected	Routing matrix not enabled for session; base §4.2 DSP pipeline continues (Mode B)
E_ROUTING_DEVICE_IN_USE	Device in use	Another app using the device exclusively	Routing matrix not enabled for session (Mode B)
E_ROUTING_DRIFT_EXCEEDED	Drift exceeded	Sample-level drift across buses over 1 hour	Routing matrix disabled for session (Mode E); base DSP continues; persistent → Mode F
E_ROUTING_LIMITER_OVERFLOW	Limiter overflow	Limiter saturation detected	Governor reduces limiter aggressiveness (Mode C)
Tier 1 events: audio.routing:enable, audio.routing:change_virtual_cable, audio.routing:change_latency_mode. All R1.

AST guards: sul-audio must not import HTTP client. No voice-cloning entry point (see §4.9 AST guards). sul-voice-fx must not import wasapi directly (uses sul-audio's WASAPI layer).

Telemetry: RoutingMatrixActive, RoutingBusActive, RoutingRejected — see §4.13.

Release: R1.

2.9 Voice FX (A.88)
Purpose: Voicemod-style voice transformation implemented as a sul-dsp graph. Pitch shift, formant shift, character presets, ring mod, bitcrush, EQ. No GPU. Neural voice conversion (RVC, kNN-VC) is gated behind A.88's ≤30 ms CPU gate and remains research (A.89) until the gate passes. Voice cloning of a specific real person is a non-negotiable structural refusal — the API surface has no entry point, the config has no toggle, and the auto-updater has no path to introduce one.

Config:

toml
[audio.voice_fx]
enabled = false
pitch_semitones = 0                        # -12 to +12; 0 = off
formant_shift = 0.0                        # -1.0 to +1.0; 0.0 = off
character_preset = "none"                  # "none" | "chipmunk" | "demon" | "robot" | "phone" | custom
ring_mod_hz = 0                            # 0 = off; 20-500 Hz typical
bitcrush_bits = 16                         # 16 = off; 4-12 = degraded
eq_low_db = 0.0
eq_mid_db = 0.0
eq_high_db = 0.0
neural_vc = "off"                          # "off" | model id (gated on A.88 ≤30 ms CPU gate)
voice_clone = "refused"                    # always "refused"; voice cloning of a specific real person is a non-negotiable refusal
Validator rules (voice-FX-specific; rules #33–#35):

A-33: [audio.voice_fx] neural_vc != "off" requires the A.88 ≤30 ms CPU gate to have passed on the current hardware; otherwise E_VOICE_FX_NEURAL_VC_TOO_SLOW at load time and neural_vc forced to "off" for the session. Neural VC is research (A.89) until the gate passes.

A-34: [audio.voice_fx] voice_clone must remain "refused"; any other value is E_CFG and the field is forced back to "refused" at load time (the refusal is a policy invariant, not a runtime toggle). This is a Tier 1 event if a user attempts to change it.

A-35: [audio.voice_fx] combined feature set (pitch + formant + ring mod + EQ + bitcrush) is measured at load against the [audio.voice_fx] combined_p99_us baseline; if the baseline is exceeded by more than 50%, E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED fires and the governor disables the lowest-priority feature (§4.10) before the session starts.

Performance baselines (from §4.14):

[audio.voice_fx] combined_p99_us — { median = 6000, p99 = 8000, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 20, status = gated, note = "pitch + formant + ring mod at 48 kHz / 512-sample on AVX2; A.88 gate" }

[audio.voice_fx] stt_wer_delta_pct — { median = 0, p99 = 2, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 50, status = gated, note = "voice FX must not regress STT WER for the A.85 voice loop" }

[audio.voice_fx] voice_loop_delta_ms — { median = 0, p99 = 50, higher_is_better = false, tolerance_pct = 50, status = gated, note = "voice FX must not regress A.85 <500 ms end-to-end" }

[audio.voice_fx] preset_perceptual_agreement_pct — { median = 0.80, p99 = 0.90, higher_is_better = true, tolerance_pct = 10, status = gated, note = "10 listeners, ≥80% agreement that the preset matches its name" }

Gate: A.88 (§4.16). Release: R1.

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED	DSP budget exceeded	Combined FX DSP p99 exceeds baseline + 50%	Governor disables lowest-priority FX (ring mod → bitcrush → formant → pitch) until DSP p99 fits budget (Mode C)
E_VOICE_FX_NEURAL_VC_TOO_SLOW	Neural VC too slow	A.88 ≤30 ms CPU gate not passed	neural_vc forced to "off" (informational)
E_VOICE_CLONE_REFUSED	Voice clone refused	Attempt to clone a specific real person	Refused; the refusal is the intended behavior (informational)
Tier 1 events: audio.voice_fx:enable_neural_vc. R1.

AST guards:

sul-voice-fx must not import wasapi directly (uses sul-audio's WASAPI layer).

sul-voice-fx must not expose any voice-cloning entry point (the API surface is checked, not just the config).

[audio.voice_fx] voice_clone must remain "refused" in every shipped config.

Voice FX chain (Voicemod parity — signal order):

Stage	Effect	Implementation
1	Noise suppression	sul-voice cIRM when enabled; spectral subtraction otherwise
2	Pitch shift	Phase vocoder / PSOLA (existing sul-voice-fx implementation)
3	Formant shift	Spectral envelope manipulation (existing sul-voice-fx)
4	Auto-Voicetune	Pitch detection (rustfft + YIN/MPM) → target pitch quantise → PSOLA re-pitch
5	Ring mod / bitcrush	Existing sul-voice-fx
6	EQ (low / mid / high)	Existing sul-voice-fx
7	Character preset	Composite of stages 2–6 with preset parameters
8	Surroundings (reverb)	Convolution reverb with impulse responses (church, room, stadium, cave)
9	Device emulation	Band-limit + saturation + noise floor (telephone, radio, walkie-talkie, megaphone)
10	AI voice	Gated — see below
The first nine stages reuse sul-voice-fx entirely. sul-voice-fx already has pitch shift, formant shift, character presets, ring mod, bitcrush, and EQ, with a sul-dsp graph and a ≤8 ms p99 budget at 512-sample / 48 kHz on AVX2 (A.88). The broadcast module (Ch. 6) adds the reverb, device emulation, and Auto-Voicetune stages on top. Auto-Voicetune is the only genuinely new DSP: a pitch detector (YIN or McLeod Pitch Method on rustfft), a target-pitch quantiser (chromatic scale, or a user-selected key/scale), and a PSOLA re-pitch stage with a glide time. Latency budget: ≤5 ms at 256-sample buffers. It is a ground-up build (~600 lines), not a wrapper.

AI voices (from A.131, Ch. 6): research-gated. The user's non-negotiable — "voice cloning of a specific real person is refused" — applies unchanged. AI voices here are character voices (trained on licensed voice-actor data), not cloning. The gate requires: (a) the voice model is trained on data with explicit commercial-use rights; (b) the model has no zero-shot cloning capability — it can only produce the pre-trained character voices; (c) the API surface has no "upload a sample" path; (d) the refusal is structural, same as Ch. 16 §16.5.

Soundboard: a bank of short audio clips (user-supplied or from a licensed pack) that mix into the voice channel on demand. Clips are pre-loaded into RAM, played on a dedicated soundboard thread, and mixed with the live voice before the strip. Latency ≤10 ms from trigger to output.

Presets: 200+ presets, matching Voicemod's count. Each preset is a JSON document (versioned, signable, shareable) describing the parameter values for stages 2–9. Presets are signed by the maintainer when distributed through the hive; user-created presets are local and unsigned. A preset is not executable code — it is a parameter set, same discipline as the persona pack.

The sul-voice-fx crate contract (from Ch. 1 §11.5):

Purpose: Voicemod-style voice transformation — pitch shift, formant shift, character presets, ring mod / bitcrush / light EQ FX.

Why from-scratch: Voicemod and similar are proprietary, GPU-bound, or both. Classical DSP (phase vocoder / PSOLA, spectral envelope manipulation) runs at ~5–8 ms per 512-sample buffer on AVX2 — no GPU, fits inside the WASAPI period. Neural VC (RVC, kNN-VC) is gated separately behind A.88's ≤30 ms CPU gate; voice cloning is refused by policy.

Dependencies: uses the sul-dsp graph primitives (filter chain, mixer) but adds the pitch / formant / ring-mod / bitcrush / EQ voice-transformation algorithms. No new top-level deps — phase vocoder, PSOLA, and spectral-envelope manipulation are hand-implemented on the DSP primitives. The neural-VC research path (A.89) is behind a feature flag and is not part of the shipping binary.

Failure taxonomy: E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, E_VOICE_FX_NEURAL_VC_TOO_SLOW, E_VOICE_CLONE_REFUSED.

Fallback chain: stage-by-stage disable: ring mod → bitcrush → formant → pitch. At pitch-only, sul-voice-fx's minimal path is guaranteed to fit the WASAPI period.

Performance contract: combined DSP p99 under 8 ms at 512-sample / 48 kHz on AVX2. STT WER delta <2%. Voice loop latency delta ≤50 ms. Preset perceptual agreement ≥80%.

Test requirements: Miri clean on the DSP primitives. Zero allocations in the callback (custom #[global_allocator] test — sul-voice-fx runs in the same callback thread as sul-dsp and sul-voice, and a single allocation there is a p99 budget breach). Perceptual preset test (10 listeners, ≥80% agreement). STT WER test with FX active vs FX off. Voice-loop latency test with FX active vs FX off.

Failure-injection support: --force-failure=vfx-1 (voice FX budget exceeded).

Release: R1.

2.10 Audio governor (sul-audio-governor)
Purpose: Single arbiter over the §4.2 audio pipeline. Decides sample rate, buffer size, exclusive mode, DSP backend, voice isolation, ducking, and resampling per session, sized to actual load, without letting the individual primitives fight each other.

Architecture:

text
crates/sul-audio-governor/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                          # public API + decision loop
│   ├── decisions.rs                    # the six-decision table
│   ├── budget.rs                       # WASAPI period vs FIR length arithmetic
│   ├── exclusive.rs                    # device-usage history + seizure-event history
│   ├── dsp_select.rs                   # sul-dsp artifact load vs AVX2 fallback
│   ├── voice.rs                        # sul-voice model presence + SIMD path check
│   ├── ducking.rs                      # per-stem envelope + cap
│   ├── resample.rs                     # rubato filter-length selection
│   ├── fir_drop.rs                     # longest-FIR-drop policy on overrun
│   └── ipc_bridge.rs                   # AudioGovernorActive telemetry
└── tests/
    └── ...
Six decisions, all in one pass at session start:

Sample rate + buffer size — period query + longest FIR + underrun history.

Exclusive mode — recommend-only, never auto-enable.

DSP backend — frozen artifact vs AVX2.

Voice isolation — on / off / skip.

Ducking — envelope + cap.

Resampling — shortest filter that meets quality.

Decisions are re-evaluated on: session start, config change, device change, 30-second interval, any AudioUnderrun event.

Latency budget: the governor refuses any decision combination that cannot fit the WASAPI period. If the longest active FIR does not fit the buffer, the governor drops the longest FIR (with AudioFilterDropped) rather than raising the buffer above 1024 samples — buffer increases are visible to the user as latency and must be an explicit choice, not a silent escalation.

Config:

toml
[audio.governor]
budget = "balanced"                        # "latency_first" | "balanced" | "quality_first"
max_buffer_samples = 1024                  # governor never escalates above this silently
exclusive_mode = "recommend"               # "recommend" | "never"
hrtf_loopback = false
hrtf_p99_ceiling_us = 800
show_audio_debug = false                   # overlay AudioLatencyMeter
Config semantics:

budget — "latency_first" = 256-sample buffer, shorter FIRs; "balanced" = 512-sample buffer, standard FIRs; "quality_first" = 1024-sample buffer, longest FIRs.

max_buffer_samples — hard ceiling; the governor never exceeds this silently.

exclusive_mode — "recommend" (governor suggests exclusive when beneficial) or "never" (governor never recommends exclusive; used when the user has a specific reason to keep shared mode).

hrtf_loopback — HRTF processing on the loopback stem for spatial audio.

hrtf_p99_ceiling_us — if HRTF pushes DSP p99 above this, the governor auto-disables HRTF.

show_audio_debug — overlay AudioLatencyMeter visibility.

Baselines (from §4.14):

[audio.governor] decision_loop_ms — { median = 5, p99 = 15, tolerance_pct = 50, status = target }

[audio.governor] underrun_events_per_100_sessions — { median = 0, p99 = 0, status = target }

[audio.governor] fir_drop_events_per_100_sessions — { median = 0, p99 = 2, tolerance_pct = 50, status = target }

[audio.governor] exclusive_mode_recommendation_accuracy_pct — { median = 95, p99 = 100, status = target }

[audio.governor] hrtf_auto_disable_correct_pct — { median = 100, p99 = 100, status = target }

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW	FIR doesn't fit buffer	Longest active FIR exceeds 1024-sample buffer	Drop longest FIR, log AudioFilterDropped (Mode C)
E_AG_DEVICE_LOST	Audio device lost	WASAPI AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED	Re-query, re-decide, resume (Mode D)
E_AG_EXCLUSIVE_BLOCKED	Exclusive mode blocked	Another app using device	Refuse, surface reason (Mode B)
E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN	HRTF CPU overrun	DSP p99 > 800 µs with HRTF on	Disable HRTF, log (Mode C)
Validator rules: audio.governor.max_buffer_samples > 2048 → rejected (latency bug, not a feature) — cross-cutting rule #8 in Ch. 1 §4.2.

AST guards:

sul-audio-governor must not import wasapi directly (uses sul-audio).

sul-audio-governor must not raise max_buffer_samples above the config ceiling.

Tier 1 events: audio.governor:change_budget, audio.governor:override_exclusive_never, audio.governor:enable_hrtf_loopback. All R2.

Test requirements: Miri clean on decision loop. FIR/buffer arithmetic: every supported filter length × {256, 512, 1024} combinations either fit or produce the correct drop policy. Zero underruns across 100 scripted sessions on the reference rig. Exclusive mode recommendation: correct answer on 10 scripted device-usage histories. FG interaction: jitter metric rises correctly when FG is enabled on a scripted workload; recommendation fires. No silent buffer increases above 1024 samples.

Telemetry: AudioGovernorActive, AudioGovernorRejected, AudioUnderrunRiskFromFg — see §4.13.

Release: R1 (ships as sul-audio-governor per releases.md).

2.11 sul-dsp — train-freeze-runtime audio DSP graph
Purpose: Train-freeze-runtime audio DSP graph. Differentiable offline, stability-checked frozen artifacts, allocation-free CPU callback.

Architecture: Offline (Python/Rust): build DSP graph (filter chain, EQ, routing, ducking). Trainable parameters, differentiable end-to-end. Stability check: poles inside unit circle, no runaway feedback, no NaN/Inf over test signal sweep. Freeze: export a versioned artifact (.suldsp + .suldspsig). Artifact contains serialized graph IR, frozen parameters, stability certificate, build hash. Runtime (Rust, sul-dsp crate): load artifact, validate stability certificate, run allocation-free on the audio callback thread. No locks, no syscalls, no allocation in the callback.

Fluxion reference: arXiv:2610.24622 proves the train-freeze-runtime pattern. sul-dsp is SUL-specific.

Integration with sul-audio: the AVX2 hand-written chain is replaced by the frozen sul-dsp artifact. Same p99 target (10–12 ms). The AVX2 path remains the fallback.

Config:

toml
[audio.dsp]
backend = "fluxion"                        # fallback: "cpu_avx2"
artifact_path = "%APPDATA%/SUL/dsp/default.suldsp"
stability_check_on_load = true
Baselines (from §4.14):

[audio.dsp] callback_allocations — { median = 0, higher_is_better = false, status = target }

[audio.dsp] filter_chain_p99_us — { median = 800, p99 = 1000, tolerance_pct = 20, status = target }

[audio.dsp] artifact_load_ms — { median = 30, p99 = 50, tolerance_pct = 20, status = target }

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE	Artifact unstable	Stability check fails on load	Refuse to load, fall back to AVX2 hand-written chain (Mode E)
E_DSP_ARTIFACT_HASH	Artifact hash mismatch	Hash doesn't match signed manifest	Refuse to load, log (Mode D)
E_DSP_TRAIN_FAILED	Training failed	Offline training fails stability gate	Do not export artifact (offline-only)
Validator rules: audio.dsp.stability_check_on_load == true — cross-cutting rule #4 in Ch. 1 §4.2.

AST guards: sul-dsp must not import HTTP client. No wasapi import outside sul-audio (from Ch. 16 §16.15 base check list).

Tier 1 events: dsp:reload_artifact. R1.

Test requirements: Zero allocations in audio callback — custom #[global_allocator] in tests panics on any allocation in the callback thread. Stability check passes on all shipped artifacts. p99 filter chain <1000 µs (target 800 µs). Artifact load <50 ms (target 30 ms). Miri clean. Failure-injection: unstable artifact refuses to load.

Failure-injection support: --force-failure=rt-1 (DSP artifact reload fail).

Release: R1.

2.12 sul-voice — cIRM neural voice isolation
Purpose: cIRM neural voice isolation. Sub-3ms, zero-alloc, zero-lock, zero-syscall in audio callback. Phase-coherent, WASAPI driver-layer interception.

Architecture: Model: causal 32-band ERB filterbank → causal 1D convolution → recurrent GRUs. Trained offline (Python). Exported as INT8 or FP16 artifact. Runtime (Rust, sul-voice crate): loads model, runs allocation-free, zero-lock, zero-syscall on audio callback thread. SIMD: AVX2 / AVX-512 / NEON dispatch at load time. E_VOICE_SIMD_UNSUPPORTED if no supported path available. WASAPI driver-layer interception: intercepts mic stream before STT reaches it. When [audio.voice] enabled = true, the isolated stream feeds STT; raw mic is not used. SilentMic-RT reference proves the algorithm.

Config:

toml
[audio.voice]
enabled = false                            # gated shipping component
model_path = "%APPDATA%/SUL/voice/cirm.onnx"
sha256_required = true
simd_dispatch = "auto"                     # "auto" | "avx2" | "avx512" | "neon"
Baselines (from §4.14):

[audio.voice] isolation_roundtrip_us — { median = 2500, p99 = 3000, tolerance_pct = 20, status = target }

[audio.voice] isolation_allocations — { median = 0, higher_is_better = false, status = target }

[audio.voice] wer_improvement_pct — { median = 5, p99 = 10, tolerance_pct = 20, higher_is_better = true, status = target }

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING	Model missing	Model file not present at model_path	Disable voice isolation, log (Mode D)
E_VOICE_SIMD_UNSUPPORTED	SIMD unsupported	No supported SIMD path available	Disable voice isolation, log
AST guards: sul-voice must not import HTTP client. No wasapi import outside sul-audio (from Ch. 16 §16.15 base check list). sul-voice model file SHA-256 verified.

Tier 1 events: none for sul-voice directly; enabling [audio.voice] enabled = true is a config change, not a Tier 1 event.

Test requirements: Zero allocations in audio callback — custom #[global_allocator] panics on any allocation. Sub-3ms round-trip (target 2500 µs, p99 3000 µs). WER improvement 5–10% on isolated speech vs raw mic. Miri clean. Model file SHA-256 verified on load. Failure-injection: missing model disables cleanly.

Release: R1.

2.13 Audio telemetry and failure codes
Telemetry messages (from sul-audio, sul-audio-governor, sul-voice, sul-voice-fx, sul-dsp, sul-stt; defined in Ch. 1 §3.2 and here as audio-specific):

rust

E_ROUTING_LIMITER_OVERFLOW	Limiter overflow	Limiter saturation	Reduce limiter aggressiveness (Mode C)
E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED	Voice FX budget exceeded	Combined DSP p99 > baseline + 50%	Governor disables lowest-priority FX (Mode C)

Mode F classification (Ch. 1 §3.4):

E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE — Mode E (persistent across sessions escalates to Mode F for Coder review of the DSP artifact stability check).

E_DSP_ARTIFACT_HASH — Mode D (quarantine).

E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING — Mode D (quarantine).

E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW — Mode C (drop longest FIR). Persistent across sessions → Mode F for Coder review of the FIR/buffer arithmetic.

E_AG_DEVICE_LOST — Mode D (re-query).

E_AG_EXCLUSIVE_BLOCKED — Mode B (refuse).

E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN — Mode C (disable HRTF).

E_ROUTING_VIRTUAL_CABLE_MISSING, E_ROUTING_DEVICE_IN_USE — Mode B (refuse the routing matrix for the session; base DSP pipeline remains functional).

E_ROUTING_DRIFT_EXCEEDED — Mode E (routing disabled; if recurring across sessions, escalates to Mode F).

E_ROUTING_LIMITER_OVERFLOW, E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED — Mode C (degraded — governor reduces limiter aggressiveness / disables lowest-priority FX).

E_VOICE_FX_NEURAL_VC_TOO_SLOW — informational (no mode transition — the gate simply means neural VC stays in A.89 research; no shipping feature is degraded because neural VC was never a shipping feature).

E_VOICE_CLONE_REFUSED — informational (the refusal is the intended behavior — logging it is a record, not a failure; Ch. 16 §16.5 documents the refusal policy).

E_STT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND, E_STT_AUDIO_CTX_INVALID, E_STT_FLASH_ATTN_UNAVAILABLE, E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED — Mode C (degraded — STT still produces transcripts, just with the fallback parameter).

E_STT_WHISPER_INIT_FAILED — Mode A (retry once with CPU-only; if that fails, disable STT for session).

2.18 Audio threat model
Threat: attacker injects malicious audio to trigger a prosody classifier into an unwanted intent (EXECUTE instead of CLARIFY).

Defense: Prosody calibration is local, unsigned, aggregate-only (§4.7). Raw audio is never stored; per-utterance features are not persisted. The prosody classifier is CPU-only (no VRAM). Voice isolation (sul-voice) intercepts mic before STT when enabled. The prosody gate is one of several signals — destructive actions always route to Thinking regardless of prosody (Ch. 10 §10.9). An attacker who compromises prosody cannot bypass the safety invariant.

Threat: attacker disables or degrades the audio pipeline to hide evidence of a destructive action (e.g., by breaking STT so the confirmation prompt is not spoken).

Defense: Audio pipeline failure modes are all Mode A–E with documented fallbacks (§4.13). A degraded STT path still produces the confirmation prompt in text via the overlay. The destructive-action safety invariant does not depend on audio — it fires in the router regardless.

Threat: attacker uses voice isolation to mask an incriminating audio channel.

Defense: The dual-track ring records both raw mic and isolated mic — the isolated track feeds STT; the raw track is available to sul-watchdog for integrity verification. Voice isolation can be disabled (it's a config toggle, not a structural refusal), but the raw track remains.

2.19 Audio AST guards
Enforced by cargo xtask ac-regression on every PR:

sul-dsp must not import HTTP client.

No wasapi import in sul-dsp/sul-voice outside sul-audio (from Ch. 16 §16.15 base check list).

sul-voice model file SHA-256 verified.

sul-audio must not import HTTP client.

sul-voice-fx must not import wasapi directly (uses sul-audio's WASAPI layer).

sul-voice-fx must not expose any voice-cloning entry point (the API surface is checked, not just the config).

[audio.voice_fx] voice_clone must remain "refused" in every shipped config.

sul-audio-governor does not import wasapi directly (uses sul-audio).

sul-audio-governor does not raise max_buffer_samples above the config ceiling.

sul-stt (in sul-audio) must not import HTTP client.

sul-stt must read only from the dual-track ring or sul-voice output, never opening a new audio stream.

[stt] flash_attn must be explicitly true (a missing field is an error, not a default).

sul-net must not import wasapi.

SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 05 — Music Player.md
1. Purpose
A bit-perfect, low-latency, low-overhead local music player with feature parity to Musicolet. Runs as sul-music.exe (separate process) so its WASAPI exclusive session does not conflict with sul-audio's loopback capture. CPU-side only — no VRAM cost, no interference with Combat Full / Deep / emulator VRAM budgets. Quality-first: bit-perfect path when exclusive mode is enabled and no DSP is active; optional EQ/ReplayGain/resampling when the user wants them, each individually toggleable.

2. Architecture
2.1 Musicolet parity target
Musicolet's feature set is: multiple queues (up to 20, separate queue per folder/album/artist/playlist); folder browsing in linear and hierarchical modes; powerful equalizer with separate presets for speakers/headphones/Bluetooth; tag editor+ for batch tag and album-art editing; move/copy songs and rename folders in-app; synchronized lyrics (embedded + LRC); bookmarks and notes; add/remove a song to >1 playlist from notifications/widgets/lockscreen; sleep timers (close after hh:mm or after N songs); gapless playback; earphone controls; widgets; A-B repeat; playback speed control; audio cutter; 10-band frequency controller with presets. No ads, offline-only, lightweight (1.98 MB).

SUL's implementation adds bit-perfect WASAPI exclusive output (which Musicolet cannot do on Windows), ReplayGain (Musicolet's ReplayGain support is unverified), and OS media controls via SMTC.

2.2 Process model
sul-music.exe is spawned by sul.exe on first music-player open, kept alive while music is playing or the music UI is open, terminated when idle for 5 minutes (or when the user closes the music window and no audio is playing). Separate process because:

WASAPI exclusive mode blocks other apps from using the device — if the music player holds the device in exclusive mode, sul-audio's loopback capture on the same device fails. Isolation lets the player be suspended or use a different device without touching sul-audio.

A crash in the music player's decoder or audio callback does not take down sul.exe.

The audio callback can run at THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL without competing with the game's threads (SUL's normal priority discipline: game threads highest, launcher normal, inference below-normal; the music player's audio callback is a real-time audio thread that must not be preempted by inference).

sul-music.exe communicates with sul.exe via sul-ipc ring buffer:

MusicControlMsg — play/pause/next/prev/seek/volume/set-queue/set-eq (from sul.exe UI or overlay).

MusicTelemetryMsg — track-changed, position, playback-state, buffer-underrun, device-changed (from sul-music.exe).

2.4 Audio path
text
File → Symphonia decoder (integer samples if bit-perfect requested,
                         float otherwise)
→ [optional] ReplayGain (float, EBU R128)
→ [optional] EQ (float, biquad)
→ [optional] Resampler (float, only if device rate ≠ file rate
                       and rate-switching is off)
→ WASAPI output
    - exclusive mode: integer samples at file rate/bit-depth
                      (bit-perfect when no DSP active)
    - shared mode: float at device mix rate
                      (Windows mixer applies — not bit-perfect)
Bit-perfect definition (explicit): The integer samples leaving Symphonia are passed to WASAPI exclusive with no sample-rate conversion and no Windows mixer, at the file's native bit depth and sample rate. If ReplayGain, EQ, or resampling is active, the path is no longer bit-perfect (DSP modifies the samples) — the UI shows a "bit-perfect" badge only when all three are off and exclusive mode is on. Integer preservation: Symphonia decodes FLAC to i32 at the native bit depth (16/24); WAV to the native format; MP3/OGG/AAC to float (lossy formats have no "native integer" — the decoded float is the reference). For lossless files with exclusive mode and no DSP, the i32 samples go straight to WASAPI without float conversion. For lossy files, float is inherent; bit-perfect in that case means "no resampling and no mixer," not "no float."

WASAPI exclusive mode: wasapi-rs (HEnquist/wasapi-rs) provides safe Rust bindings with shared and exclusive modes; the playnoise_exclusive example demonstrates the exclusive path. Exclusive mode bypasses the Windows mixer (no sample-rate conversion, no Windows volume attenuation unless the device driver applies it). Requires the device to accept the file's exact format (WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE with matching sample rate, bit depth, channel count). If the device does not support the format, the player falls back to shared mode with a warning. Device is blocked for other apps while held. The UI shows "Exclusive — device held" and a warning if sul-audio or the voice loop is active. Rate-switching: in exclusive mode, the player can switch the device's sample rate to match the file (if the device supports it). This is what makes per-file bit-perfect possible for a mixed-rate library. Event-driven mode (not polling) for low latency: the audio callback is signaled by the device event, buffers 128–256 samples (2.9–5.8 ms at 48 kHz) for interactive playback; 512 samples for background listening. The callback is allocation-free (same discipline as sul-dsp / sul-voice).

Shared mode fallback: cpal + rodio for shared mode (the default when exclusive is off). rodio 0.22 has the f32 pipeline upstream; symphonia-all feature covers all decoders. Shared mode goes through the Windows mixer — not bit-perfect, but coexists with sul-audio, the voice loop, and other apps. This is the default posture; exclusive is opt-in.

Gapless playback: Symphonia supports gapless for FLAC, OGG, WAV, AIFF; AAC/MP4 gapless depends on container metadata; MP3 gapless uses the LAME enc_delay and enc_padding from the Xing/LAME header. AudioDecoderOptions::gapless is enabled by default in Symphonia 0.5.6+. The engine pre-loads the next track's decoder while the current track is playing (a dedicated preload thread), so the transition is seamless: at the end of track N, the decoder for track N+1 is already primed, and the audio callback switches sources without a gap. The preload is bounded (one track ahead) to keep memory usage predictable. Crossfade is mutually exclusive with gapless — crossfade overlaps the ends, gapless plays them end-to-end with no overlap. The validator refuses both being enabled (§5.12, rule M-1).

ReplayGain: ebur128 provides EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-5 loudness measurement and ReplayGain 2.0 track and album calculation. oximedia-normalize provides EBU R128, ATSC A/85, streaming-platform targets, and ReplayGain track/album with tagging support. Modes: Off (no gain applied, bit-perfect path preserved); Track (per-track gain from ReplayGain tags, or computed on first play if tags absent; computed gains cached in SQLite); Album (per-album gain, preserves inter-track dynamics within an album). Preamp: −12 to +12 dB, default 0 dB. ReplayGain is applied in float, after decode and before EQ. Applied at the decode stage (not post-mix) so the gain is consistent per track. Bit-perfect badge is hidden when ReplayGain is active.

EQ (10-band graphic + parametric): math_audio_iir_fir provides biquad filters and PEQ (parametric equalizer) with SPL response computation; biquad-rust is a Rust port of AutoEQ's parametric EQ optimizer; oxiaudio-dsp provides RBJ biquads (lowpass/highpass/bandpass/notch/allpass/peaking EQ/shelf), parametric EQ, and dynamics. Two modes, mutually exclusive:

Graphic 10-band — 31 Hz, 62 Hz, 125 Hz, 250 Hz, 500 Hz, 1 kHz, 2 kHz, 4 kHz, 8 kHz, 16 kHz; peaking biquads, ±12 dB per band; presets: Flat, Rock, Pop, Jazz, Classical, Electronic, Vocal, Bass Boost, Treble Boost, Custom.

Parametric — up to 10 bands, each with frequency, gain, Q, and filter type (peaking, low shelf, high shelf, lowpass, highpass, bandpass, notch); AutoEQ import — paste a parametric EQ profile from AutoEQ, which uses biquad-rust's optimizer format.

Per-device profiles: EQ settings are keyed by WASAPI device ID (speakers, headphones, Bluetooth, USB DAC each get their own profile), matching Musicolet's per-device presets.

Bypass when flat: [performance.music] eq_bypass_when_flat = true — if all bands are at 0 dB, the EQ chain is skipped entirely (zero CPU cost). Default on. Bit-perfect badge is hidden when EQ is active.

Resampling: Only used when the device sample rate does not match the file rate and rate-switching is off (shared mode, or exclusive mode on a device that doesn't support the file's rate). Three backends:

rubato — pure-Rust, FFT and Sinc fixed/async; "new_sinc matches the quality of the Fft resampler but is the most CPU-heavy option"; default for shared mode.

SoXR — native SoX VHQ via the soxr feature; when both rubato and soxr are enabled, SoXR wins on quality; optional backend.

ardftsrc — arbitrary-rate DFT SRC; "generally preferred over other resamplers when quality is paramount," more compute-intensive than rubato sinc; optional backend for users who prioritize quality over CPU.

Default: rubato_sinc (good quality, pure Rust, no native dependency). soxr and ardftsrc are opt-in per [performance.music] resampler. Bit-perfect badge is hidden when resampling is active. In exclusive mode with rate-switching on, no resampling is needed — the device switches to the file's rate.

Multiple queues: Musicolet supports up to 20 separate queues, one per folder/album/artist/playlist. SUL implements:

Named queues — each queue is a named list of tracks, persisted in SQLite (queues table, queue_tracks join table). Up to [music.library] queues_max = 20 (configurable).

Auto-queue — when the user plays a track from a folder/album/artist/playlist, a queue is auto-created or reused for that source. If a queue with the same name exists, the user is asked replace/merge (matching Musicolet's behaviour).

Active queue — one active queue at a time; switching active queue stops the current playback and starts the other queue's current track (or resumes its saved position).

Queue persistence — queues survive app restart; the active queue and its position are restored.

Folder browsing: Two modes, matching Musicolet: Linear (all folders at once, flat list) and Hierarchical (folders within folders, navigable tree). Default: hierarchical. The library scanner records the folder structure; the UI renders either view from the same index.

Tag editor: lofty — pure-Rust tag library, reads/writes FLAC (Vorbis Comments, ID3v2), MP3 (ID3v2, ID3v1, APE), MP4/M4A (iTunes atoms), OGG, WAV, AIFF, APE, WavPack. Batch edit: select N tracks, edit common fields (album, artist, genre, year) or per-track fields (title, track number). Album art: batch-replace or per-track. Save writes to the file via lofty and re-reads to verify. Tag writing is a Tier 1 event — it modifies user files. The first write per session prompts: "SUL will modify N files. Back up first? [Back up and write] [Write without backup] [Cancel]." Backups go to %APPDATA%\SUL\music-backups\<timestamp>\ (the original files are copied, not moved). Read-only mode: [features.music.tag_writing] can be turned off to make the tag editor read-only — useful if the user manages tags elsewhere and doesn't want SUL to touch files.

Synchronized lyrics: Embedded lyrics: ID3 USLT (MP3), FLAC LYRICS/UNSYNCEDLYRICS Vorbis comments, MP4 ©lyr atom. LRC sidecar: .lrc file next to the audio file (same basename). Both parsed into a timeline of (timestamp, text) pairs; the UI scrolls in sync with playback position. LRC parser supports: [mm:ss.xx] timestamps, multiple timestamps per line, metadata tags ([ti:], [ar:], [al:], [by:], [offset:]), and enhanced LRC word-level timing (ignored for display, preserved for future karaoke support). Lyrics display: overlay ticker (single line, follows [overlay] ticker_speed), full-screen lyrics view (multi-line, scrolls with playback), and "edit lyrics" (opens the tag editor with the lyrics field focused).

Sleep timers: Two modes, matching Musicolet: Time-based (close the app after hh:mm, configurable 1 min – 24 h; countdown shown in the UI) and Song-count-based (close after N songs, configurable 1–99; remaining count shown in the UI). "Close" means: stop playback, fade out over 2 s (configurable 0–10 s), then shut down sul-music.exe. sul.exe remains running.

A-B repeat: Set point A and point B in the current track; playback loops A→B. UI: click "Set A" at the current position, "Set B" at the current position, "Loop A-B" toggles. Clearing either point exits A-B mode. Points are per-track and not persisted (A-B is a transient practice tool, not a library feature).

Playback speed: 0.25× – 4.0×, in 0.05× steps. Implemented via resampler-based speed change (rubato's speed combinator, or a dedicated speed-adjusted resampler) — pitch is preserved (time-stretch, not pitch-shift). At 1.0× the speed chain is bypassed (zero CPU cost, bit-perfect path preserved). At non-1.0× speeds, the bit-perfect badge is hidden. Note: preserving pitch at non-1.0× speeds requires a time-stretch algorithm, not just resampling. rubato provides resampling (which changes pitch with speed); for pitch-preserved time-stretch, the player uses a phase-vocoder or WSOLA algorithm. This is a ground-up piece.

Audio cutter: Select a range (start/end) in the current track, export to a new file. Formats: FLAC (lossless, default), WAV (uncompressed), MP3 (lossy, requires an encoder). The export is lossless from the decoded samples — the range is decoded, trimmed, and re-encoded; for FLAC/WAV this is sample-exact, for MP3 it is a re-encode (quality loss). The UI warns: "MP3 export re-encodes; FLAC/WAV are lossless." Metadata: the exported file copies the source's tags (title gets " (cut)" appended by default, editable). Cover art copied. ReplayGain recomputed for the new file.

OS media controls: souvlaki — cross-platform OS media controls: SMTC on Windows, Now Playing on macOS, MPRIS on Linux; needs HWND on Windows. The player publishes: title, artist, album, cover art, playback state, position, and handles play/pause/next/prev/seek from the OS media keys and the Windows lock screen / volume flyout. This replaces Musicolet's "earphone controls" and "widgets" on Windows — SMTC is the OS-native equivalent that appears in the volume flyout, lock screen, and (on Windows 11) the media widget.

Overlay mini-player: When [features.music.overlay_mini_player] is on and the game overlay is active, a compact mini-player appears in the overlay corner: track title, artist, play/pause, next/prev, progress bar. Clicking expands to the full lyrics view. This is the Musicolet "widget" equivalent for SUL's overlay context.

Taskbar thumbnail toolbar: Windows taskbar thumbnail buttons for play/pause/next/prev, via the windows crate's ITaskbarList3::ThumbBarAddButtons. Same feature as Musicolet's notification controls, adapted to Windows.

Library index: SQLite (the same database engine SUL already uses for telemetry and config). Tables: tracks (id, path, title, artist, album, album_artist, track_no, disc_no, year, genre, duration_ms, bitrate, sample_rate, bit_depth, channels, codec, file_size, mtime, replaygain_track_db, replaygain_album_db, peak); albums (id, name, album_artist, year, cover_art_path); artists (id, name); folders (id, path, parent_id for hierarchical view); playlists (id, name, created_at, updated_at); playlist_tracks (playlist_id, track_id, position); queues (id, name, source_type, source_id, created_at); queue_tracks (queue_id, track_id, position); bookmarks (track_id, position_ms, note, created_at); lyrics (track_id, source, lrc_text). Scanner: walks [music.library_paths], reads tags via lofty, extracts cover art to %APPDATA%\SUL\music-covers\<hash>.jpg, inserts/updates rows. Incremental: mtime-based skip if unchanged. Full rescan on demand.

3. Contract
3.1 Config (consolidated)
This section merges the [music.*] config block, the [features.music.*] toggles, and the [performance.music] block. Authority rule: [features.music.*] is the release-gate view (which features are enabled in this release class); [performance.music] is the tuning view (performance optimizations); [music.*] is the runtime config (how the player behaves). Per-game override wins over all three if a per-game music block exists (currently none — the music player is global, not per-game, per Ch. 1 §2.8).

toml
[music]
enabled = true
library_paths = []                             # user adds via OS file picker
watch_library = true                           # filesystem watcher on library_paths
scan_on_startup = true

[music.playback]
output_device = "auto"                         # "auto" | device ID (WASAPI endpoint ID)
exclusive_mode = false                         # Tier 1 to enable — blocks other apps
buffer_size = 256                              # samples; 128-2048
sample_rate_follow_file = true                 # switch device rate to match file in exclusive mode
gapless = true
crossfade_ms = 0                               # 0 = off; 0-12000; mutually exclusive with gapless
replaygain_mode = "track"                      # "off" | "track" | "album"
replaygain_preamp_db = 0.0
playback_speed = 1.0                           # 0.25-4.0; 1.0 bypasses time-stretch
volume = 1.0                                   # linear 0.0-1.0; device volume separate

[music.dsp]
enabled = false                                # master DSP toggle; false = bit-perfect path preserved
eq_mode = "graphic_10band"                     # "graphic_10band" | "parametric"
eq_presets = {}                                # per-device; keyed by WASAPI device ID
resampler = "rubato_sinc"                      # "rubato_sinc" | "soxr" | "ardftsrc"
quality = "high"                               # "low" | "medium" | "high" | "maximum"

[music.library]
queues_max = 20
folder_view = "hierarchical"                   # "linear" | "hierarchical"
cover_art_size_px = 500
scan_threads = 2

[music.library.jellyfin]
server_url = ""                            # local Jellyfin server
api_key_from_vault = true                  # API key stored in the vault
enabled = false                            # gated A.164

[music.lyrics]
source = "auto"                                # "auto" | "embedded" | "lrc" | "off"
overlay_ticker = true
font_size = 16

[music.sleep_timer]
fade_out_ms = 2000                             # 0-10000

[music.cutter]
default_format = "flac"                        # "flac" | "wav" | "mp3"

[features]
# Music player features — release-gate view.
music.enabled = true
music.library_scanning = true
music.folder_browsing = true
music.multiple_queues = true
music.tag_reading = true
music.tag_writing = true
music.lyrics = true
music.bookmarks = true
music.playlist_multi_membership = true
music.sleep_timer = true
music.ab_repeat = true
music.playback_speed = true
music.audio_cutter = true
music.eq_graphic = true
music.eq_parametric = true
music.eq_per_device = true
music.replaygain = true
music.gapless = true
music.crossfade = false
music.exclusive_mode = false                   # opt-in Tier 1
music.bit_perfect = false                      # opt-in, requires exclusive
music.os_media_controls = true
music.overlay_mini_player = true
music.taskbar_controls = true

[performance.music]
# Music player optimization — tuning view.
bit_perfect_when_exclusive = true
allocation_free_callback = true
decoder_thread_priority = "above_normal"       # "normal" | "above_normal" | "highest"
gapless_preload = true
replaygain_at_decode = true
eq_bypass_when_flat = true
resampler = "rubato_sinc"                      # "rubato_sinc" | "soxr" | "ardftsrc"

cover_art_cache_mb = 64
Config semantics:

library_paths — user adds via OS file picker, not config edit.

watch_library — filesystem watcher on library_paths.

scan_on_startup — full rescan at startup (incremental scan is always on).

output_device = "auto" — uses the default WASAPI endpoint; a fixed device ID selects a specific endpoint.

exclusive_mode = false — opt-in, Tier 1 to enable, because it blocks other apps from using the device.

buffer_size = 256 — samples; 128–2048 (validator M-4).

sample_rate_follow_file = true — in exclusive mode, switches the device rate to match the file.

gapless = true — Symphonia gapless preload.

crossfade_ms = 0 — 0 = off; mutually exclusive with gapless = true (validator M-1).

replaygain_mode = "track" — Off / Track / Album.

replaygain_preamp_db = 0.0 — −12 to +12 dB.

playback_speed = 1.0 — 0.25–4.0; 1.0 bypasses time-stretch.

volume = 1.0 — linear 0.0–1.0; device volume separate.

[music.dsp] enabled = false — master DSP toggle; false preserves bit-perfect path.

eq_mode = "graphic_10band" — Graphic 10-band or Parametric (validator M-2).

eq_presets = {} — per-device, keyed by WASAPI device ID.

resampler = "rubato_sinc" — Rubato sinc / SoXR / ARDFTSRC.

quality = "high" — Low / Medium / High / Maximum.

queues_max = 20 — matches Musicolet's 20-queue limit.

folder_view = "hierarchical" — Linear or Hierarchical.

cover_art_size_px = 500 — cover art cache resolution.

scan_threads = 2 — library scan threads.

#### Jellyfin source (A.164)

Jellyfin (https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin) is a self-hosted media server. It is accepted as an **optional local library source** alongside `[music.library] library_paths`. This is a revision of the existing "streaming service integration" non-goal: Jellyfin is not a commercial streaming service — it is the user's own library. Commercial streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, etc.) remain rejected.

Config: `[music.library.jellyfin] enabled = false`, gated A.164. The API key is stored in the vault (Ch. 2 §2.4). The server URL is a user-configured local network surface, declared in Ch. 16 §16.15.14.

Gate A.164: Jellyfin library indexing, playback URL resolution, and search all work for a scripted 100-track library. If the gate fails, the feature stays off and `[music.library] library_paths` is the only source.

[music.lyrics] source = "auto" — Auto / Embedded / LRC / Off.

overlay_ticker = true — overlay ticker visibility.

font_size = 16 — lyrics font size.

[music.sleep_timer] fade_out_ms = 2000 — 0–10000 ms fade-out.

[music.cutter] default_format = "flac" — FLAC / WAV / MP3.

Validator rules (music-specific; rules #57–#60):

M-1: [music.playback] crossfade_ms > 0 and gapless = true are mutually exclusive (E_CFG). If crossfade > 0, gapless is auto-disabled with a warning.

M-2: [music.dsp] eq_mode must be "graphic_10band" or "parametric" (E_CFG otherwise).

M-3: [music.playback] exclusive_mode = true requires device coordination: if the music device matches sul-audio's device and sul-audio loopback or voice loop is active, exclusive is refused with E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT; the player falls back to shared mode.

M-4: [music.playback] buffer_size must be in [128, 2048] (E_CFG otherwise).

3.2 Device coordination (§2.4)
Three audio subsystems may contend for the same WASAPI device (Ch. 4 §4.3):

sul-audio (game loopback capture, voice isolation, DSP, STT, TTS).

sul-music.exe (music playback, optional WASAPI exclusive).

sul-broadcast-audio (broadcast mixer, virtual devices, VBAN).

Coordination rules (from Ch. 4 §4.3, as they apply to the music player):

sul-music.exe's exclusive mode is refused when its device matches sul-audio's device and sul-audio's loopback capture or voice loop is active. Exclusive mode is allowed on a different device.

sul-broadcast-audio monitoring uses shared mode. Exclusive mode is reserved for the music player.

The audio governor (Ch. 4 §4.10) is the single arbiter over sul-audio's six decisions. The music player has its own [performance.music] budget and does not contend with sul-audio's DSP budget because it runs in a separate process.

When the music player or broadcast mixer requests exclusive mode on the same device as sul-audio, the compatibility validator refuses the request with E_CFG and the device-coordination logic (Ch. 1 §5) surfaces the reason.

Threat model (from Ch. 17 §17.14): Threat: attacker (or a misconfiguration) enables WASAPI exclusive mode on the same device as sul-audio's loopback capture or voice loop, silently breaking game audio capture. Defense: The device-coordination logic refuses exclusive mode when it would conflict with sul-audio loopback or voice loop. E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT fires and the music player falls back to shared mode. The UI shows a warning ("Exclusive — device held") and the reason for the refusal. The compatibility validator (Ch. 1 §5) rejects the configuration at startup. The AST guard (§5.13) verifies that the exclusive-mode path does not bypass the device-coordination check. The loopback capture verification (A.119) is the end-to-end test that proves bit-perfect output and device coordination are both correct.

3.3 Process lifecycle
sul-music.exe is spawned by sul.exe when: the user opens the music player UI, OR the user resumes a previously-playing track, OR a sleep timer is pending. Terminated when: playback stopped and no music UI open for 5 minutes, AND no sleep timer pending. The process holds the WASAPI device only while playing. When paused or stopped, the device is released (so sul-audio can use it). Exclusive mode is re-acquired on resume. Crash recovery: if sul-music.exe crashes, sul.exe restarts it with the last known queue and position (read from the SQLite state). The audio device is re-acquired. The user sees a transient "Music player restarted" toast.

3.4 Library scanner
Walks [music.library_paths], reads tags via lofty, extracts cover art to %APPDATA%\SUL\music-covers\<hash>.jpg, inserts/updates rows in the SQLite library index. Incremental: mtime-based skip if unchanged. Full rescan on demand. [music.library] scan_threads = 2 controls parallelism (respects the process-level thread priority discipline — scanner threads run at below-normal so they don't compete with the audio callback or the game).

[music.library] watch_library = true installs a filesystem watcher on library_paths (via notify, already a workspace dependency) so new or modified files are picked up without a full rescan.

3.5 Audio cutter
crates/sul-music/src/audio_cutter.rs. Select a range (start/end) in the current track, export to a new file. Formats: FLAC (lossless, default), WAV (uncompressed), MP3 (lossy, requires an encoder). Pipeline: decode range → trim → re-encode. For FLAC/WAV this is sample-exact; for MP3 it is a re-encode (quality loss). The UI warns: "MP3 export re-encodes; FLAC/WAV are lossless." Metadata: exported file copies the source's tags (title gets " (cut)" appended by default, editable). Cover art copied. ReplayGain recomputed for the new file.

Encoder dependencies: flacenc (FLAC), hound (WAV), mp3lame-encoder (MP3, feature-gated — only enabled when the user selects MP3 export; the default FLAC/WAV path does not link it).

3.6 Startup: music player binary check (Step 4.16)
If [music] enabled = true, verify:

sul-music.exe present.

Library paths exist.

WASAPI device coordination (§3.2) passes.

sul-music-engine decoder initializes.

Failure modes:

Condition	Error	Behavior
sul-music.exe missing	E_CFG	Music player disabled; sul.exe continues.
Library paths missing	(warning)	Player starts with empty library; user is prompted to add paths.
Device coordination fails	E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT	Player falls back to shared mode; UI shows reason.
Decoder fails	E_MUSIC_BIT_PERFECT_UNAVAILABLE (if bit-perfect path unavailable)	Bit-perfect badge hidden; shared mode used.
UI: MusicStatusIndicator shows active track, playback state, bit-perfect status, exclusive mode status, device coordination state. Subscribes to MusicTelemetryMsg. Always visible in Settings → Music and in the overlay mini-player when [features.music.overlay_mini_player] is on.

Benchmarks (xtask music-bench):

music_bench.py::cpu_overhead — Music player CPU playing / EQ / EQ+RG+resampling. Produces [music] cpu_playing_pct, cpu_eq_pct, cpu_eq_replaygain_resampling_pct.

music_bench.py::bit_perfect_loopback — Bit-perfect path verification (input bytes vs output bytes). Produces [music] bit_perfect_loopback_verified.
