SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 10 — Local AI.md
1. Purpose
The single llama.cpp build, one combat checkpoint with four shipping profiles (Combat Full), one agentic coding checkpoint (Deep Coder), the Combat Full profile router, the OODA-Tool scaffold, TSCG schema compilation, the KV cache stack (STAR-KV primary, GAAC fallback, alternative compressors via sul-kv-compress), the speculation stack (Medusa + phrase + UniSpec + n-gram for Combat Full; ChainFlow + LiLiCorr + UniSpec + n-gram for Deep), quantization (sul-quant SPEED-Q + APEX), the distilled ToolPRM cross-encoder (sul-toolprm), ReTrace visual-token compression, and the sul-ai-native runtime. This chapter is the AI subsystem.

Contract: §10.4 (Combat Full profile router), §10.16 (ReTrace), §10.6 (fine-tuning), §10.13 (speculation), §10.14 (sul-quant), §10.11 (sul-kv-compress), §10.12 (sul-spec-draft), §10.15 (sul-toolprm) — authoritative. Gates: A.18 (STAR-KV PPL + KL@D), A.54 (ReTrace), A.63 (Combat Full per-profile BFCL + router accuracy), A.68 (design anchor), A.96 (sul-quant SPEED-Q), A.97 (sul-kv-compress backends), A.98 (sul-spec-draft RIFT), A.99 (Medusa + phrase head), A.100 (sul-toolprm cross-encoder), A.101 (Coding profile). Baselines: [ai.combat_full], [ai.combat_full_instruct], [ai.combat_full_thinking], [ai.combat_full_conversation], [ai.combat_full_coding], [ai.combat_full.toolprm], [ai.combat_router], [ai.deep_q4], [ai.deep_q5], [ai.speculative.*]. Boundary: Ch. 16 §16.1 (Model Boundary, Combat Mode Router Boundary).

2. Architecture
2.1 Tier models, Combat Full profiles, and single llama.cpp build
One combat checkpoint with four shipping profiles, plus one agentic coding checkpoint. Combat Full (InternVL3-2B + ReTrace) runs in one of four profiles — Instruct 2K (fast execution), Thinking 4K (deliberate planning/judgment), Conversation 16K (no-game open-ended dialogue), and Coding 8K (research-only, gated by A.101). Deep Coder (K2-Horizon-7B) is the actively-loaded agentic coder. There is no Butler, no Coding Low, no Deep Extended. Scene understanding is a capability layer (sul-vlm, Ch. 8 §8.4), not a tier.

Tier table:

Tier / Profile	Base Model	Quant	Context	VRAM (base)	VRAM (STAR-KV/ReTrace)	When Active
Combat Full — Instruct	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	Q4_K_S (SPEED-Q 4-bit)	2K	1.65–1.75 GB	1.30–1.35 GB	Game running, fast execution, tool formatting, simple judgment
Combat Full — Thinking	InternVL3-2B + ReTrace	Q4_K_S (SPEED-Q 4-bit)	4K	1.70–1.80 GB	1.35–1.45 GB	Game running, complex judgment, planning, destructive-action evaluation
Combat Full — Conversation	InternVL3-2B (shared weights) + ReTrace	Q4_K_S (SPEED-Q 4-bit)	16K	same base as Thinking	~1.25–1.30 GB	No-game open-ended conversation, web search, knowledge recall
Combat Full — Coding (research)	InternVL3-2B (shared weights) + ReTrace	Q4_K_S (SPEED-Q 4-bit)	8K (16K ceiling)	same base	~1.15–1.30 GB	No-game code work; ships only if A.101 passes (HumanEval ≥60)
Deep Coder	K2-Horizon-7B	Q5_K_M (quality-first; Q4_K_M available)	4K–8K (32K ceiling)	6.46 GB	~6.96 GB with q8_0 KV at 4K	Actively-loaded agentic coding
Notes below the table:

The Combat Full VRAM figures assume ReTrace is active (mandatory optimization per Phase 2 VRAM posture). Without ReTrace, Combat Full is ~1.65–1.75 GB in Instruct mode and ~1.70–1.80 GB in Thinking mode (larger context, larger KV). ReTrace compresses vision tokens to bring both modes to the 1.30–1.45 GB range. HD2's old 2.5 GB ceiling is retired in Phase 2 in favor of a general 3 GB combat ceiling for all games. R0 case (no ReTrace, no ToolPRM): Combat Full Instruct ~1.65–1.75 GB + PP-OCRv5 ~21 MB = ~1.67–1.77 GB. R0.1 case (ReTrace active, ToolPRM not yet): ~1.5 GB with ReTrace. R2+ case (ReTrace + ToolPRM + full spec chain): Combat Full ~1.3–1.45 GB + sul_toolprm_enc ~60–180 MB + PP-OCRv5 ~21 MB = ~1.53–1.65 GB. All fit under the 3 GB general combat ceiling with ≥1.2 GB headroom.

SPEED-Q 4-bit quantization (sul-quant, A.96) brings InternVL3-2B weights from 3,984.5 MB BF16 to 1,454.6 MB — ~63% reduction. The VRAM figures in the table assume SPEED-Q 4-bit is active after A.96 passes; until then, Q4_K_S via llama.cpp is the operative quantization. SPEED-Q 2-bit brings InternVL3-2B to 1,218.7 MB (~69% reduction, 6× higher accuracy than prior 2-bit methods); the 2-bit path is gated behind A.96's "holds within 2% absolute" clause. LiteRT independently confirms the modality split at 1.43 GB total (int8 vision encoder + int4 LLM + int8 embedding) with 34.4 tok/s decode / 573 tok/s prefill / 380 ms TTFT on Galaxy S26 GPU — the SPEED-Q 4-bit figure is the desktop CUDA equivalent.

The VRAM (base) column shows measured figures without STAR-KV or ReTrace active. The VRAM (STAR-KV/ReTrace) column shows what those tiers become once STAR-KV ships (A.18) or ReTrace ships (A.54). Once those gates pass, the deployed figures are the ones in the rightmost column; until then, the base figures are the operative ones for VRAM budget checks.

Deep Coder's 6.46 GB is Q5_K_M. Q5_K_M is 6.02 GiB, 94.14% top-1 agreement with BF16, +0.915% ΔPPL. Q4_K_M is 5.21 GiB but 92.12% top-1 and +2.04% ΔPPL. Q5_K_M fits at 4K with q8_0 KV (~6.96 GB total); Q4_K_M fits with ample headroom. Q6_K does not fit (7.40 GB before KV; no room for KV + runtime). Q8_0 exceeds 8 GB before KV. Q3_K_M fits with ample headroom but quality is too degraded (83.74% top-1, +9.3% ΔPPL). The full quantization table is in §10.19; the quality-first posture is Q5_K_M.

#### Model candidates (Phase 3)

DeepSeek models (https://github.com/deepseek-ai) are candidates for the Deep Coder checkpoint. Evaluate DeepSeek-V4 series against K2-Horizon-7B on the A.108 (post-training benchmark lift) and A.110 (PalQuant KV) gates. If a DeepSeek model wins by ≥3 points on the relevant gate, it replaces K2-Horizon as the Deep checkpoint. The eval harness structure takes reference from deepseek-harness (https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) and LM-Evaluation-Harness; A.63-Common ships the harness design.

Why each model:

Combat Full = InternVL3-2B + ReTrace, four profiles. InternVL3-2B is dialogue-optimized (better text performance than Qwen2.5 series), native vision, tool calling, GUI agents. ReTrace achieves 100% benchmark retention (MMB 80.8, MMBCN 79.0, POPE 89.9, SQAI 95.7, MME 2221) at 11.1% token retention, with ~90% KV reduction and 2.83× prefill speedup. max_dynamic_patch = 4 for HD2 alone-execution under the 3 GB general combat ceiling. Q4_K_S weights + q8_0 KV. Fine-tuned via LoRA + function masking + xLAM corpus + ToolPRM to replace Hammer (§10.6). Combat Full runs in one of four profiles, selected per turn by a router in sul-agent (§10.4). All four profiles share the same llama_context; the profile flip is a runtime parameter change, not a model reload.

Combat Full's web-search capability is load-bearing for its SimpleQA accuracy (78.3%). The config validator (Ch. 1 §4.2 rule #20) enforces that ai.combat_full.instruct_web_search_enabled remains true whenever net.search.backend is enabled. If the search backend is disabled for a session, Combat Full's judgment quality drops — this is not a silent failure, it is a documented dependency. The Conversation profile requires [net.search] backend != "disabled" (validator rule #17).

Combat Full is a separate tier from sul-vlm's no-game scene backends. sul-vlm's no-game backends (MiniCPM-V, LFM2.5-VL, jina-vlm, Qwen2.5-VL) are for no-game scenarios only (Ch. 8 §8.4). Combat Full's own InternViT encoder handles gameplay vision. These are two distinct vision paths, not one. The old Combat Mid tier, now cut, used to be a third path — packets-with-vision-fallback — but that workload class is absorbed into Combat Full Thinking's 4K context and Conversation's 16K context.

Deep Coder = K2-Horizon-7B Q5_K_M (quality-first). Actively-loaded agentic coding. SWE-bench Verified 70.6 — beats Qwen3.5-9B (50.8), Gemma 4-12B (63.1), Granite 4.2-8B (66.5) at a fraction of parameter count. (Qwen3.5-9B is a comparison baseline only — it is not in SUL's tier ladder.) Terminal-Bench 2.1 39.1 (agentic coding). Speculation chain ["chainflow", "lilicorr", "unispec", "ngram", "none"]; ChainFlow +39% over EAGLE-3, +11% over DFlash at matched drafter size on Qwen3.5 — these are Qwen3.5-specific published figures. The shipped Deep Coder is K2-Horizon-7B, where the shipped aggregate speedup is 1.6× median / 1.9× p99 — lower than DFlash's 2.5–4.9×. ChainFlow ships as Deep's first rung because its K2 workloads sit in the workload class where flow-matching wins. No fork required: K2-Horizon support is in llama.cpp mainline as of b11454 (PR #29535). Single mainline tree, no fork. Q5_K_M is the quality-first default; Q4_K_M available for headroom. Deep 8K context is plausible with STAR-KV; 32K is the practical ceiling; 512K remains a research target for 24 GB+ cards.

Why 13B+ not used: at SUL's 8 GB reference budget, 13B-parameter weights at any quant that preserves usable quality (Q4_K_M and up) exceed the available VRAM before KV cache or context. Lower quants (Q2_K ~5.3 GB) fit weights-only but collapse quality below the task thresholds this spec targets. CPU offload is 10–20× slower.

Why Qwen2.5-Coder is not the Combat model: code-specialized; on tool-use benchmarks code-tuned models consistently underperform general 7B-class models on tool-use (TaskBench and similar). See §10.6 for the Combat Full fine-tuning recipe that closes this gap.

2.2 Single llama.cpp build
sul-ai-native vendors one llama.cpp tree — mainline, pinned to b12207+ — as a git submodule, built as a static library via CMake. K2-Horizon support landed in mainline b11454 (PR #29535: dense and MoVA variants, HF-to-GGUF conversion, tokenizer, chat template, -sm tensor splitting). b12207 already satisfies b11454, so the pin remains b12207+. There is no llama.cpp-k2 fork, no PrismML cherry-picks, no dual-build complexity. arch.rs reads GGUF general.architecture and maps qwen2, qwen2.5, qwen2.5-coder, qwen3, qwen3.5, hammer2, internvl3, k2_horizon → mainline tree. Unknown → E_UNKNOWN_ARCH. The llama-cpp-2 fallback behind --features fallback-llama-cpp-2 does not support K2-Horizon; Deep is unavailable in fallback mode and the launcher logs E_K2_ARCH with a clear message. This remains a fallback-mode error only, not a shipping-path error. The b12207+ pin also includes the 35% Zamba2 throughput improvement, unified KV cache for multi-sequence, OCP FP8 support, and the Vec-LUT kernel — none of which regress on Qwen/InternVL3/K2. Submodule update cadence: quarterly, gated on full baselines regression (A.26).

Hardware kernel autotuning (`--backend-autotune`, R2, gated A.192): at Step 3.9, `sul-ai-native` can invoke Magnitude's kernel search on first launch to cache `%APPDATA%\SUL\bench\kernel_cache.json` alongside `%APPDATA%\SUL\bench\hardware_profile.json` (recording GPU, driver version, and passed A.96/A.97 backends so hardware/driver changes automatically invalidate stale gate caches).

R4 MoE tiered streaming (`[ai.deep] moe_backend = "llama" | "colibri" | "auto"`, R4 research, A.179): pure-C Colibri backend (hot experts on GPU, warm in RAM, cold streamed from NVMe) evaluated for R4 400B distillation on ≥25 GB RAM + NVMe systems.

crates/sul-ai-native/ layout:

text
crates/sul-ai-native/
├── build.rs                   # CMake invocation on the vendored mainline tree
├── vendor/
│   llama.cpp/               # mainline, pinned b12207+ (Qwen/InternVL3/K2)

2.3 LoRA adapters (distribution Option C — merged at build time; no .lora files at runtime)
Adapter	Base models	Purpose	Shipping
jarvis_persona_7b_k2.lora	K2-Horizon-7B	Deep voice/persona	Merged at build
jarvis_structured_k2.lora	K2-Horizon-7B	Deep tool/JSON shaping	Merged at build
jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora	InternVL3-2B	Function masking + xLAM corpus training (replaces Hammer); mode-tagged for instruct / thinking / conversation / coding	Merged at build
jarvis_deep_tools.lora	K2-Horizon-7B	Agentic-coding tool calls on SUL traces; mode-tagged for Deep	Merged at build
Each 50–200 MB. LoRAs merged into base GGUF via llama-export-lora at build time. CI job cargo xtask verify-lora-merge runs 10 prompts against merged GGUF vs base+adapter, asserts cosine similarity >0.998 and output-token equality >98%. If CI fails, build fails. Dev: [dev.lora] holds .lora paths; --dev-lora loads separate files per-request. Merge saves ~150 MB VRAM and ~100 ms per tier switch.

Note on jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora: the adapter is trained on mode-tagged data — every training example is labeled instruct, thinking, conversation, or coding, and the merged model responds differently based on a mode prefix in the system prompt (which is controlled by --reasoning-budget at inference time). This is what makes the multi-profile design work with a single merged GGUF. The training recipe (§10.6) covers profile-specific loss weighting, mode-tagged data, and router-aware ToolPRM training.

2.4 Distillation pipeline (§10.21)
GAD + CADENCE retained. The original assumption (7B Qwen teacher distills into 3B Qwen coder) does not apply to the current model ladder — Butler and Coding Low are cut, and the current ladder has no 3B-class coder to distill into. If distillation is attempted, it applies to whichever tier benefits, gated by the A.8 eval harness.

2.5 Speculative decoding — ordered chains
Tier	Chain
Combat Full (all profiles share one chain)	["medusa", "phrase", "unispec", "ngram", "none"]
Deep Coder	["chainflow", "lilicorr", "unispec", "ngram", "none"]
Every chain terminates in "none". The config validator (cargo xtask config-check) refuses to start if any chain does not terminate with "none" and raises E_SPEC_CHAIN_UNTERMINATED. Any tier with a draft model loaded but no --spec-type raises E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET at startup.

Combat Full has one chain, not per-profile. All four profiles share the same chain because the target is the same model — the speculation drafter predicts the target's next tokens regardless of profile. There is no per-profile chain. The chain is the same whether the current turn is routed to Instruct, Thinking, Conversation, or Coding. §10.13 has the full speculation implementation.

Speculative decoding rungs:

Medusa-1 (shared-LM-head, frozen backbone) is the first rung for Combat Full. Hard constraints: Medusa-1 only (heads trained on frozen backbone). Medusa-2 (joint fine-tune) is a Tier 1 event if ever offered, because it risks backbone quality. Shared-LM-head variant only. The own-LM-head variant (~1 GB for 5 heads on a 2B model with 151k vocab) is rejected by the config validator because it defeats the general combat ceiling. Temperature scaling applied to speculative logits — without it, acceptance drops 30–50% in practice. Head VRAM ≤50 MB at Q4 for the 5-head shared-LM-head variant. Expected median ~35 MB. Loader path: PyTorch .pt → Candle tensors; candidate tree builder; llama_batch construction with the tree attention mask (feeding llama.cpp's existing batch-verify path, not forking llama.cpp). Expected aggregate: acceptance rate 0.55 median / 0.70 p99; speedup 2.2× median / 2.8× p99. See [ai.speculative.medusa] baseline.

Phrase-level head is the second rung. A ~3.4M-param MLP reads the frozen target's hidden state, predicts a one-to-three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary, maps back via greedy longest-match expansion. Output identical to greedy decoding up to FP tie-breaking (arXiv:2611.12464). Head VRAM ~2–5 MB. Expected: acceptance rate 0.45 median / 0.60 p99; speedup 2.0× median / 2.4× p99. See [ai.speculative.phrase] baseline.

UniSpec stays as third rung (Combat Full) / third rung (Deep). Use the unispec crate with a thin adapter (sul-spec-draft::unispec_adapter) — feeds a SUL-tuned retrieval index (tool-call history, OODA state, Entity Ledger), calibrates confidence thresholds on the SUL tool-call eval set, writes candidates directly into the llama_batch tree-attention structure without an intermediate copy. Roughly 1–2 weeks. 2.6× p99 measured across Llama-3 and Qwen-3 on A100/A40/RTX A6000/RTX 3090; median is 2.0×.

ChainFlow is the first rung for Deep. Flow-matching drafter conditioned on target hidden states. +39% over EAGLE-3, +11% over DFlash at matched drafter size on Qwen3.5 (published Qwen3.5-specific figures, not K2 aggregate — see the Deep paragraph above for the shipped K2 aggregate of 1.6× median / 1.9× p99). Needs 1–2 flow steps instead of many denoising steps. Not yet in llama.cpp — vLLM plugin at Cosmos-YTU/chain-flow. sul-ai-native integrates flow-matching drafter loader + integrator. Draft model ~100–200 MB.

LiLiCorr replaces DFlash as Deep's second rung. LiLiCorr is mainline in llama.cpp v0.7.0 (PR #30506). Improves on DFlash with joint candidate scoring across the draft block, no additional backbone VRAM (only the small scorer transformer). The paper reports +9–19% acceptance length on every benchmark tested and the highest throughput in 70 of 72 settings. Expected: acceptance rate 0.60 median / 0.75 p99; speedup 2.7× median / 3.2× p99. See [ai.speculative.lilicorr] baseline.

DFlash and EAGLE-3 are orphaned by the Butler cut and the LiLiCorr replacement. Neither is in any shipping chain. DFlash is cut from [ai.speculative.*] baselines. EAGLE-3 is retained as a fallback rung name recognized by speculative.rs but is not in any shipping chain; its baseline is marked deprecated. Decision: cut both from shipping-chain consideration; retain only as recognized-but-unused rung names for future re-evaluation. If a future tier re-enables DFlash or EAGLE-3, the corresponding baseline entry is restored.

n-gram (final fallback all tiers): --spec-type ngram-mod — no draft model. 1.4–1.6× depending on workload.

The --spec-type refactor: -md no longer auto-enables speculation. Without --spec-type, draft model is loaded but never used. Config validator raises E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET if any tier has a draft model loaded and no --spec-type. The only silent failure mode; validator closes it at startup.

Startup benchmark (30s per tier, cached to %APPDATA%\\SUL\bench): for each tier, test every rung in chain except none; pick winner by effective decode tok/s; verify acceptance ≥ floor; cache result. On subsequent launches, read cache in <100 ms.

2.6 Scene understanding (sul-vlm)
sul-vlm (Ch. 8 §8.4) is a capability layer, not a tier. Four backends: MiniCPM-V 4.7 1B (0.64 GB, 1.3 s, 68.2% rubric, default no-game), LFM2.5-VL-3B (~2.5 GB, ~1–2 s, ScreenSpot-v2 80.7, no-game with free_vram ≥ 5 GB), jina-vlm 2.4B (~2.4 GB, ~1–2 s, SOTA multilingual VQA among 2B VLMs, no-game multilingual), Qwen2.5-VL-3B (~2 GB + CPU ViT, ~8 s, opt-in --enable-vlm only). Backend selected by sul-vlm governor based on language hint from query. Combat Full is a separate tier from sul-vlm.

2.7 YaRN context extension, gated and config-aware
YaRN extends context beyond the model's trained window. Factor 2.0 at 64K mandatory for K2 and Qwen when 64K is used — not the default 4.0. Double-applying YaRN garbles output. Read GGUF rope_scaling metadata before loading; if YaRN already baked into the GGUF, do not pass --rope-scaling, only --ctx-size. Combat Full uses native contexts (2K/4K/16K/8K) — no YaRN. Deep uses native 32K ceiling — no YaRN. The double-scale check in Ch. 1 §2.7 step 2.5 prevents accidental YaRN.

2.8 Prompt strategy
Reason-free, constrain-late. No chain-of-thought tokens in output — the model answers directly, and the Verifier (§10.4) constrains structure. IFFC (instruction-following formatting constraint) for small-model tool calling — explicit JSON schema in the prompt forces correct tool-call shape. Two-tier prompt caching: (1) persistent prompt prefix cache in KV (reused across turns), (2) persistent prompt cache to disk (%APPDATA%\\SUL\cache\prompt-prefix) saving 2–3 s at session start. A.4 gate.

2.9 Game-state machine and screenshot ring (refined RDP handling)
sul-governor game-state machine reads OCR text and maintains rolling state summary. Publishes GameStateUpdated on telemetry. On RDP (SM_REMOTESESSION true), screenshot ring becomes request-scoped at 2s / 5 Hz instead of 10s / 30 Hz, because persistent WGC on RDP causes 3.2× higher capture latency and 14.5× more callbacks (screenpipe PR #5226 measurement). Ring disabled entirely if user sets [vision] rdp_screenshot_ring = false. Ring size and RDP behavior configurable via [vision] screenshot_buffer_seconds = 10, [vision] rdp_screenshot_ring = true.

2.10 Combat Full profile VRAM (HD2 and ED)
HD2 Combat Full VRAM calculation: Combat Full is a single checkpoint with four profiles. R0 ships Instruct without ReTrace (~1.65–1.75 GB). R2+ ships with ReTrace active (Instruct ~1.30–1.35 GB, Thinking ~1.35–1.45 GB, Conversation ~1.25–1.30 GB, Coding ~1.15–1.30 GB). All profiles share the same weights (~1.05 GB Q4_K_S) and differ only in KV cache. Under ReTrace (mandatory optimization per Phase 2), Combat Full in any profile fits comfortably under Phase 2's 3 GB general combat ceiling. There is no co-residence calculation — Combat Full is the only combat model, and all profiles are the same model. The HD2 profile does not need co-residence flags. The 3 GB ceiling is satisfied by any profile alone, and the router flips profiles in <50 ms without a model reload. sul-toolprm cross-encoder (~60–180 MB Q4, A.100) also fits under 3 GB alongside Combat Full, restoring PRM rescoring that was previously disabled on HD2.

ED Combat Full VRAM calculation. ED has no kernel-level anti-cheat and allows co-residency with other tiers. On ED, Combat Full (~1.3–1.45 GB with ReTrace) can co-exist with Deep (~6.46 GB Q5_K_M; Q5_K_M with STAR-KV fits at 4K) — but 1.45 + 6.46 = 7.91 GB > 8 GB, so co-residency requires offloading 2–4 layers of Deep (~7.1 GB total, tight but fits). The old three-tier ED co-residence calculation (~5.2 GB for Combat Low + Combat Mid + Combat Full) is obsolete; under the multi-profile design, Combat Full is ~1.3–1.45 GB, and Deep is the only other checkpoint.

2.11 Pre-created contexts and profile lifecycle (Startup Step 3.7)
Pre-created contexts (from Ch. 1 §2.7 step 3.7):

Verify all pre-created contexts exist on the loaded llama_context: Instruct (2K), Thinking (4K), Conversation (16K, lazy no-game), Coding (8K, research). Verify --reasoning-budget toggles correctly between 0 (Instruct/Coding), 256 (Conversation), and the configured Thinking budget.

If Instruct context is available but Thinking context fails, log E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID and disable Thinking profile for the session (all turns Instruct — router bypassed with a warning). If Conversation context fails, disable Conversation profile for the session (all no-game turns Instruct). If Coding context fails, Coding profile stays research (already gated A.101). If no context is available, Combat Full is dropped entirely for the session and the user is notified (E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID at the fatal severity). This check runs before Step 4.5 (DSP artifact load), because Combat Full is the highest-priority tier and its failure is more user-impactful than DSP artifact failure.

Combat profile fallback chain (from Ch. 1 §3.4 / §10.24):

Thinking OOM or unavailable when selected → Instruct takes over (CombatRouterFallback logged) → drop Combat Full entirely (E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID fatal).

Instruct-only fallback is documented, not silent — the overlay shows the fixed profile with a warning chip on CombatProfileIndicator.

2.12 Combat Full profile router (sul-agent::combat_profile)
Purpose: Select Combat Full's inference profile (Instruct / Thinking / Conversation / Coding) per turn. One model, four profiles, one checkpoint, one VRAM budget.

Location: sul-agent::combat_profile. Runs in sul.exe's agent thread. Sends ControlMsg::SetCombatProfile { profile } to sul-ai.exe before each turn.

Decision: Instruct, Thinking, Conversation, Coding, or off.

"off" mode: If [ai.combat] profile = "off", the router is not invoked and SetCombatProfile is never emitted. Combat Full is not loaded for that session (the checkpoint may remain loaded for other reasons, but no combat-tier turn is dispatched to it). The user sees a persistent overlay chip: "Combat Full disabled for this game." This is an unusual configuration — typically only chosen when a game's anti-cheat profile makes combat-tier assistance undesirable — and it is a Tier 1 event when toggled.

Signals (evaluated in order):

Priority	Signal	Decision	Notes
1	Destructive action detected	Thinking	File deletion, config overwrite, process launch, save-restore, mod install. This is the safety invariant — it overrides user override if destructive_action_always_thinking = true (default). This is evaluated first because it is a hard safety invariant, not a preference.
2	User profile override	As specified	[ai.combat] profile = "instruct" | "thinking" | "conversation" | "coding" | "auto". Applied only when priority 1 does not fire.
3	Prosody intent = EXECUTE (confidence > threshold)	Instruct	Fast path from Ch. 4 §4.6.
4	Prosody intent = CLARIFY	Thinking	Needs context assessment.
5	Prosody intent = ASSESS	Thinking	Deliberate reasoning mode.
6	Task-type classifier = multi-step plan	Thinking	Planner-type tasks.
7	Tool call formatting for a verified plan	Instruct	Execution of a decided action.
8	Prior tool call failed verification	Thinking	Escalation to reasoning.
9	No game running + no destructive action + no tool-verification failure + non-command turn	Conversation	Open-ended no-game dialogue.
10	Default (game running, no other signal)	Instruct	Fast path.
Destructive-action detection. The router intercepts every turn before tool emission and scans for destructive-action indicators: the target tool is write_file, edit_file, or process_launch; the parameters reference paths under %APPDATA%\\SUL\config.toml, %APPDATA%\\SUL\sulpack\, %APPDATA%\\SUL\dsp\, or any file already in session_working.artifacts with prior state; the target is a process launch of a game or SUL component; the target is a mod install path. The detection is deterministic (regex + schema-match) — no LLM involvement.

Safety invariant. If the user manually selects Instruct profile and a destructive action is detected, the router overrides to Thinking. The user sees "Profile overridden to Thinking for destructive action — Instruct profile ignored" in the overlay (CombatProfileIndicator shows a lock icon with this reason). This cannot be disabled by user profile selection, by the router's default, or by any priority-5+ signal. The only way to disable it is the per-game destructive_action_always_thinking = false flag, which is a Tier 1 event and requires the OS-level approval modal. This is a hard safety invariant — the user can disable it, but not silently.

Fallback. If the deterministic signals conflict or are ambiguous, the router invokes a small classifier prompt on Combat Full Instruct itself (fast path) to make the choice. This is a single-pass LLM call, not a loop. Target latency for the two-call case: <600 ms cold / <150 ms warm.

Logging. Every router decision publishes CombatProfileSelected { profile, source, confidence, at } on telemetry. source ∈ { user_override, destructive_action, prosody, task_classifier, tool_verification, no_game_conversation, default }. Backs CombatFullStatusIndicator UI (overlay shows "Combat Full · Instruct" / "· Thinking" / "· Conversation" / "· Coding") and the CombatProfileIndicator chip (Ch. 7 §2.6). Also backs combat_profile_history.json (§10.24) for post-hoc router behavior analysis.

User override. The Settings UI exposes a manual profile override. Override is per-session, not persistent. A Tier 1 event when toggled. [ai.combat] profile_override_scope = "session" (default) or "task" controls whether the override resets on session start or on task completion. destructive_action_always_thinking still applies (see safety invariant).

Failure handling. If Thinking profile OOMs (transient VRAM spike) or fails to load its 4K context, the router falls back to Instruct for that turn and logs CombatRouterFallback. The rate is tracked in [ai.combat_router] instruct_fallback_rate_pct. If the checkpoint itself fails to load, all profiles are unavailable and Combat Full is dropped entirely — there is no combat model for the session (the user is notified via overlay). If the router is itself disabled (router_enabled: false in game_registry.json), the session runs in a fixed profile selected by [ai.combat] profile — Instruct is the recommended fixed profile because it cannot silently mis-route a destructive action to Instruct (the safety invariant still applies even with the router disabled).

2.12.1 Zero-allocation critical path & temporal hysteresis (D-147)
- **Zero-allocation decision matrix**: Signal ingestion (token length, complexity markers, VRAM pressure telemetry, prosody intent, and regex/schema destructive-action flags) evaluates over fixed stack-allocated structs on `sul.exe`'s agent thread without heap allocations on the turn hot path.
- **Temporal hysteresis**: Non-safety profile transitions (`Instruct` ↔ `Thinking` ↔ `Conversation`) apply a configurable turn/millisecond cooldown window (`hysteresis_ms`) to prevent rapid profile thrashing near decision boundaries; Priority 1 (destructive-action → `Thinking`) and VRAM-pressure fallback (`Thinking` → `Instruct`) bypass hysteresis immediately.


Combat-Confirm sub-role (from Ch. 4 §4.6): When a destructive action is about to execute (file deletion, config overwrite, process launch, save-restore, mod install), Combat Full Thinking generates the user-facing warning: "About to overwrite config.toml — 47 changes will be lost. Confirm?" If Thinking mode is unavailable (OOM, model not loaded), Combat Full Instruct generates the same warning as a backup. Both use the same prompt template and the persona "warn before destructive operations" constraint. Zero new model. Under the router, destructive-action detection always routes to Thinking (per signal priority 1) — but the router's guarantee is that Thinking mode is selected for destructive actions, not that Thinking mode is guaranteed available. If Thinking mode is unusable (VRAM OOM during a spike), the router logs CombatRouterFallback and the fallback path (Instruct generating the warning) applies. This is documented, not silent.

Capability scaling under the profile design: Combat Full Instruct handles 2–3-step execution; Combat Full Thinking handles 4–5-step planning; Combat Full Conversation handles 3–4-step dialogue-with-tools; Combat Full Coding (research) handles 3–4-step code. No VRAM increase from profile choice — same checkpoint, same weights, same ReTrace, only KV cache differs (Instruct 2K vs Thinking 4K vs Conversation 16K vs Coding 8K). The router's decision is orthogonal to planner/verifier/solver — those run in whichever profile is active for the turn.

Verification escalation path (from §11.11g):

Attempt 1 — Combat Full Instruct formats call; Verifier checks. Fail → retry with error-in-prompt.

Attempt 2 — Combat Full Instruct retries. Fail → escalate to Thinking profile (this is router signal priority 8: prior tool call failed verification).

Combat Full Thinking reasons through the failure: "the call failed twice; worth a third try, or decline?" Decides retry / decline / surface E_TOOL_UNFORMABLE.

If Thinking also fails to format the call after a retry, E_TOOL_UNFORMABLE — user sees: "I can't format this call reliably. Here's what I have — {partial}. You may want to do this manually."

Query decomposition: Compound queries split into single-purpose calls. "Read the mission text, check the shop price, and tell me if the reward is enough" becomes: vision_ocr (mission text), vision_ocr (shop price), Combat Full Instruct reasoning. Neutralizes MiniCPM-V's documented multi-step weakness (Ch. 8 §8.4) — each model does one job.

Task-type classifier (from §11.11g):

Task class	Route
Chat, extraction, short code (<40 lines), config diff	Combat Full — Conversation profile
Code >40 lines, multi-file refactor, agentic task	Deep Q5 (if VRAM ≥ 7.5 GB)
Whole-session analysis, >16K context	Deep at 32K ceiling with STAR-KV (if VRAM ≥ 7.5 GB)
Lite coding, tight VRAM (<3 GB)	Combat Full — Coding profile if A.101 passes; otherwise Deep (may require offload)
Escalation is user-visible: a banner shows "Escalating to Deep: this task exceeds Combat Full Conversation's capability." User can interrupt. Silent escalation is worse than no escalation.

Planner tier selection under the profile design (from §11.11g):

Loaded profile	Mode	Plan depth	When planner routes here
Combat Full Instruct	Execution	2–3 steps	Execution intent, fast path (game running)
Combat Full Thinking	Planning	4–5 steps	Planning, judgment, destructive-action evaluation (game running)
Combat Full Conversation	Dialogue	3–4 steps	No game, chat + lite coding
Combat Full Coding (research)	Code	3–4 steps	No game, code work (A.101 gated)
Deep Q5	Agentic	5+ steps	Explicit coding request, agentic tasks
The routing-first principle: every tier is more capable than earlier revisions asked it to be. Combat Full Thinking can plan 4–5 steps; Combat Full Conversation can plan 3–4 steps; the routing layer lets each profile do what it can when it's loaded, and routes only what genuinely exceeds it.

Router tests (from §11.11g):

Router profile-selection accuracy ≥95% on 200 SUL-shaped turns.

Router destructive-action detection recall = 100% on the router's 100-trigger destructive-action test set — any miss is a hard fail.

Profile-switch latency <50 ms p99.

Instruct never emits thinking tokens (200-prompt negative-example test, zero leaks).

Thinking never skips reasoning for complex calls (200-prompt test, all four scaffold fields populated with reasoning traces).

Conversation does not emit tool-call-shaped output for non-tool turns (200-prompt test).

Coding does not emit conversational fluff (200-prompt test).

Router deterministic given fixed inputs (proptest 1000 iterations, no nondeterministic classification).

User override respected (manual profile = "instruct" honored unless destructive action detected; CombatProfileDenied + E_DESTRUCTIVE_INSTRUCT_OVERRIDE emitted if safety invariant overrides).

Router fallback (Thinking OOM → Instruct) fires correctly with scripted VRAM-spike workload; CombatRouterFallback telemetry emitted.

Two-call case latency: <600 ms cold / <150 ms warm on the router LLM fallback path.

Router disabled (router_enabled: false) → session runs fixed profile; safety invariant still applies (destructive actions still escalate to Thinking if destructive_action_always_thinking = true).

destructive_action_always_thinking = false (Tier 1 event) → safety invariant disabled, user override respected even for destructive actions, logged with E_DESTRUCTIVE_PROTECTION_DISABLED in a warning (not error) state. E_DESTRUCTIVE_INSTRUCT_OVERRIDE is not emitted in this case — no override occurred.

Router benchmarks (xtask router-bench, mode-switch-bench, router-determinism-bench):

router_bench.py::mode_selection — 200 scripted turns through the router; per-turn accuracy. Produces [ai.combat_router] mode_selection_accuracy_pct.

router_bench.py::destructive_action — 100 destructive-action triggers through the router; recall. Produces [ai.combat_router] destructive_action_detection_recall.

router_bench.py::determinism — 1000 identical-input iterations; same profile each time. Binary gate (no baseline entry).

mode_switch_bench.py::reasoning_budget_flip — --reasoning-budget flip latency on same llama_context. Produces [ai.combat_router] mode_switch_latency_ms.

mode_switch_bench.py::context_swap — 2K ↔ 4K ↔ 16K ↔ 8K context switch latency (informational; mode_switch_latency_ms is the gate).

2.13 sul-agent — REWOO/ReAct, OODA-Tool, TSCG, planner_split
Routing flow (from §11.11g):

text
User prompt (with optional prosody features from Ch. 4 §4.6)
  ↓
Combat Full profile router (if a game is running, or no-game):
  ├── Instruct (fast path, game running)
  ├── Thinking (deliberate path, game running)
  ├── Conversation (no game, open-ended)
  └── Coding (no game, code work, research-gated)
  ↓
Prosody intent gate: EXECUTE | CLARIFY | ASSESS | UNKNOWN
  ↓
  ├─ ASSESS → direct conversational answer, no tool path
  ├─ CLARIFY → one clarification question, then proceed
  └─ EXECUTE / UNKNOWN → Router (DIRECT / REWOO / REACT)
  ↓
  [DIRECT] → single-turn answer, no tools
  [REWOO] → OODA-Tool scaffold → Planner → Verifier → Executor → Solver
  [REACT] → Thought → Action → Observation loop (fallback)
  Each tool call within REWOO/REACT passes through OODA-Tool scaffold before execution
  Each tool schema is TSCG-compiled before reaching the model
Prosody gate: If classifier is confident (EXECUTE/ASSESS), LLM bypassed for the intent decision. If UNKNOWN, the loaded judgment profile (Ch. 4 §4.6 fallback table) provides judgment. Zero-token fast path. The prosody gate output feeds the Combat Full profile router directly (§10.4).

Router: small classifier prompt on the currently loaded tier. Most config-help questions are DIRECT; diagnostics are REWOO; recovery-from-failed-plan is REACT.

Planner: emits a step-by-step plan as a DAG of tool calls. Uses only tool schemas already in the loaded packet (Ch. 11 §11.4), and those schemas are delivered as TSCG-compiled structured text, not raw JSON. The planner prompt includes the exact available_tools list — no hallucinated tools.

Verifier: deterministic check (not an LLM call) that every tool in the plan exists in the current schema and argument types match. Rejects invalid plans before execution.

Executor: runs the plan DAG in dependency order. Before each tool call, the OODA-Tool scaffold is applied: Observed state → Orientation → Decided action → Act. The scaffold fields are written into a temporary scratchpad that is not carried into the next turn — only the emitted tool call survives. Observations from the tool call are stored

Durable execution & Coder context selection: `sul-agent::ooda_tool` uses a lightweight checkpointed state machine (LangGraph pattern, no Python dep) persisting OODA node state to `sulpack`'s `agent_state` section for Mode E/F recovery. For Coder sessions, `repo_map` runs tree-sitter + PageRank (Aider pattern) to select top-k relevant files + imports. For Conversation, `[features.reading_mode]` (R2, gated A.189) parses local EPUB/MOBI via `epub` and injects chapter/selection context + address pointers in <100 ms. but not re-fed to the model between steps — the REWOO token-efficiency win (5× fewer tokens than interleaved ReAct). For Combat Full, the executor delegates to whichever profile the router selected for this turn — Instruct formats function calls quickly, Thinking reasons through destructive-action chains before formatting, Conversation applies dialogue-shaped reasoning, Coding applies code-shaped reasoning.

Solver: composes the final answer from the evidence. If execution failed at any node, the Router falls back to REACT for that specific node, then resumes.

OODA-Tool state scaffold: Before emitting any tool call, the model must populate four fields in sequence:

Observed state — what the packet currently says is true (mission ID, shield %, current target, active contract), read from session_working.threads.current_encounter and session_working.entities.

Orientation — is execution warranted? Does the packet need a search? If a search is needed, the model emits web_search first; the search pipeline returns a verification packet; then orientation re-runs with the packet as evidence.

Decided action — function name and parameter structure, checked against the TSCG-compiled schema.

Act — final call.

Not a reasoning loop; a structured pre-call scaffold. Mitigates state-action competition. Evidence: OODA-Tool improves task success on smaller models most, especially for tasks depending on accumulated information across turns.

All Combat Full profiles apply OODA-Tool. Instruct applies it compactly (same four fields, minimal elaboration). Thinking applies it with full reasoning traces (same four fields, expanded orientation reasoning). Conversation applies it compactly for tool-use turns; skips it for pure-dialogue turns. Coding applies it compactly with code-shaped scratchpad. The scaffold is profile-agnostic; the profile determines depth of reasoning inside the scaffold, not whether the scaffold runs.

Failure mode: If scaffold fields are incomplete (fields_populated < 4), retry once; then skip scaffold for that call and log E_OODA_INCOMPLETE. Test cases assert retry-then-skip behavior.

TSCG schema compilation: Tool schemas delivered to the model are not raw JSON. The MCP server compiles them to token-efficient structured text (≥51% compression). This addresses the protocol mismatch that Constraint Tax identifies as the dominant failure mode (Qwen2.5-1.5B: 91.5% executable accuracy with prompt-only JSON vs 48.0% under hard tool-call schema). TSCG is profile-agnostic — same compiled schemas for all Combat Full profiles.

Where it lives: sul-agent::ooda_tool (prompt scaffold) and sul-agent::tscg (schema compiler). Not new models. Not reasoning loops. The compiled schema is cached per-session per-profile (schemas don't change mid-session). TSCG is profile-agnostic — all Combat Full profiles receive the same compiled schemas.

Failure modes: E_OODA_INCOMPLETE (scaffold fields not populated before tool call → retry once, then skip scaffold for this call). E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED (schema compilation failed → fall back to raw JSON for this call).

planner_split module (gated shipping component, A.47): small-planner / big-executor for Deep. Measured ~30% token reduction on agentic tasks. The planner runs on Combat Full Instruct (if a game is running) or Combat Full Conversation (if no game); the executor runs on Deep. Test requirements gain: "Planner_split uses ≥25% fewer tokens than same-tier planning with no quality loss."

OODA-Tool tests (from §11.11g): Scaffold does not increase token cost >5% vs unstructured planning. Multi-step reliability: BFCL multi-turn accuracy improves ≥10% with scaffold vs baseline. State-action competition: scripted tests with stale packet state produce correct calls ≥95% of the time with scaffold vs baseline. Failure-injection: incomplete scaffold fields retry once then skip; E_OODA_INCOMPLETE logged. Scaffold runs in all profiles (Instruct compact, Thinking verbose, Conversation compact, Coding compact); fields_populated = 4 in all profiles.

TSCG tests (from §11.11g): TSCG compilation achieves ≥51% schema compression on reference schema set. Tool-call accuracy retention ≥95% with TSCG vs raw JSON on BFCL subset. Per-session per-profile caching correct (schemas don't change mid-session). Failure-injection: compilation failure falls back to raw JSON; E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED logged. Miri clean.

sul-agent test requirements (from §11.11g): Planner never emits a tool not in the current schema (property test over 1000 prompts). Verifier rejects hallucinated tools deterministically. REWOO uses <25% of ReAct's tokens on the same task. ReAct fallback recovers from a failed plan within 3 iterations. Prosody gate respects the one-question cap (≤1 clarification per task). Task-type classifier routes correctly on 200 SUL-shaped prompts (≥95% accuracy). planner_split uses ≥25% fewer tokens than same-tier planning with no quality loss. Router tests (see §10.4).

Benchmarks (xtask ooda-bench, tscg-bench):

ooda_bench.py::scaffold_overhead — Scaffold token overhead. Produces [agent.ooda_tool] scaffold_overhead_pct.

ooda_bench.py::multi_turn_gain — Multi-turn accuracy gain. Produces [agent.ooda_tool] multi_turn_accuracy_gain_pct.

tscg_bench.py::compression — Schema compression ratio. Produces [agent.tscg] schema_compression_pct.

tscg_bench.py::accuracy_retention — Tool accuracy retention. Produces [agent.tscg] tool_accuracy_retention_pct.

#### Comparison to OpenHands (reference)

OpenHands (https://github.com/OpenHands/openhands) provides a reference for planner/executor decomposition, tool registry design, and multi-turn memory. sul-agent adopts the *lessons* (planner/executor split, deterministic verification) but not the architecture — sul-agent is deterministic-first with a small-LLM fallback, per D-056. OpenHands is a reference, not a dependency.

2.14 Combat Full + Deep fine-tuning pipeline
Purpose: Replace Hammer2.1-3B's execution capability with a LoRA-tuned Combat Full (InternVL3-2B) that approaches — but does not match — Hammer's BFCL 81.42 non-live / 95.00 live ceiling. Under the multi-profile design, the fine-tuning must train the model to be competent at four profiles (Instruct / Thinking / Conversation / Coding) with router-aware signals. Deep (K2-Horizon-7B) gets its own LoRA for agentic-coding tool calls. Measurement-driven decision gate: per-profile BFCL ≥65 non-live (Instruct and Thinking) + Conversation quality + Coding HumanEval ≥60 (A.101) + router accuracy ≥95% + destructive-action recall 100% keeps the Hammer cut final; any failure re-evaluates whether Hammer returns as a swap-in.

Recipe (Combat Full):

Training data: Salesforce/xlam-function-calling-60k + MadeAgents/xlam-irrelevance-7.5k. These are the exact datasets used to fine-tune Hammer. Include BFCL train split + ToolSandbox subsets (7:3 train/test). License note: xlam-function-calling-60k is CC-BY-NC-4.0 (commercial use prohibited, research-only access form). It cannot ship as the primary training dataset for a commercial product. Two paths, gated independently:

(a) Synthetic replacement (recommended): generate function-calling data from SUL's own tool schemas (the 30+ tools in Ch. 11 §11.11 + §11.20) using the APIGen pipeline (apigen-pipeline.github.io — verify current repository license against the tag before shipping; the public release is CC-BY-4.0) or the ToolOrchestrationReward constrained-synthesis pipeline (horizon-llm/ToolOrchestrationReward, BFCL-compatible). If the generated dataset reaches ≥90% of xLAM-trained BFCL performance on the held-out SUL tool set, ship this path.

(b) Licensed-subset path: keep xLAM but filter to any explicitly CC-BY-4.0 or Apache-2.0 splits. Note: the 60k dataset as published is uniformly CC-BY-NC-4.0; subsets must be verified individually. If none qualify, this path is closed.

Either path must additionally use ToolPref-Pairwise-30K (RioLee — verify license before shipping) for the ToolPRM reward-model SFT stage.

Mode-tagged data (multi-profile extension). Every training example is tagged with a profile: instruct, thinking, conversation, coding. The profile is controlled at inference time by --reasoning-budget (Instruct = 0, Thinking = positive, Conversation = 256, Coding = 0) and during training by a profile prefix in the system prompt. The model learns to respond differently based on the prefix: instruct examples emphasize fast, direct tool formatting with minimal internal reasoning; thinking examples include full reasoning traces (CacheRL hybrid thinking trajectories) before the tool call; conversation examples are dialogue-shaped: no tool-call structure unless the turn requires a tool, longer-form answers, web-search citations; coding examples are code-shaped: multi-line code blocks, code-shaped reasoning traces, tool-call formatting for write_file / edit_file / run_cargo_test.

Method: LoRA SFT (not full fine-tune). LoRA preserves pretrained behavior and is the strongest in-distribution method — a controlled study across six Qwen3 models (0.6B–32B) found LoRA won 15 of 18 settings vs full parameter tuning. Full fine-tune is rejected: it degrades the model's pretrained agentic behavior.

Profile-specific loss weighting. Thinking examples get 1.5× weight (reasoning quality is the harder target). Instruct examples get 1.0× weight (execution correctness is the goal, not reasoning depth). Conversation examples get 1.2× weight (dialogue quality and citation accuracy are hard targets). Coding examples get 1.0× weight (execution correctness again). The ratios were chosen so that Thinking-mode planning quality improves without regressing Instruct-mode execution speed, and Conversation-mode dialogue quality improves without regressing any tool-use capability. The first training run must record per-profile BFCL after fine-tuning; if Instruct BFCL regresses, the weight ratio is reduced.

Function masking: Randomly replace function names, parameter names, and default values with random alphanumeric strings during training. Forces the model to prioritize semantic descriptions over brittle naming conventions. This is Hammer's core technique. The masking schedule is the non-trivial part of the recipe; it is implemented in crates/sul-lora/combat_full_tools/masking.py. Function masking applies to all profiles — the model must be robust to name masking in all of them.

Hybrid thinking trajectories (CacheRL recipe): Teach the model why to call a tool, not just what. Include reasoning traces in the training data. CacheRL finds that reinforcement learning yields limited gains beyond strong SFT, and that data quality and reward design matter more than complex optimization — so the LoRA run prioritizes high-quality function-masking data plus reasoning traces, not a complicated RL pipeline. Thinking-mode examples get the full hybrid trajectories; Instruct-mode examples get abbreviated trajectories (one to two sentences of intent, not multi-paragraph reasoning); Conversation-mode examples get dialogue-shaped traces (why the model chose to search, what it did with the search results); Coding-mode examples get code-shaped traces (why a function shape, why a specific tool).

ToolPRM: Backbone is now sul_toolprm_enc (distilled cross-encoder, A.100). Teacher model for training is ToolRM-4B (Apache-2.0, see R.4). Scores each intra-call decision (function name, param name, param value) and guides beam search at inference time. Loads only during function-calling turns. The 4B teacher is retained for ED (no HD2 ceiling), but the shipping runtime uses the cross-encoder everywhere, including HD2. This restores PRM rescoring on HD2 that was previously structurally disabled.

ToolPRM VRAM on HD2. Cross-encoder at ~60–180 MB Q4. Combined with Combat Full's ~1.3–1.45 GB (ReTrace-on) + SPEED-Q 4-bit's ~1.45 GB, total ~1.53–1.65 GB — comfortably inside the 3 GB general combat ceiling with ~1.35 GB headroom. The 4B teacher (~2.3–2.5 GB Q4) does not fit alongside Combat Full and remains ED-only.

Router-aware ToolPRM (multi-profile extension). The cross-encoder reward head is trained with an auxiliary objective that scores not just intra-call decisions but also the profile-conditional quality of the call — i.e., "is this the right shape for the profile this turn was routed in?" This is a training-time signal only: it teaches the merged model to behave better in all profiles. It is not a runtime router input. The router in §10.4 uses deterministic signals exclusively; adding an LLM-scored signal to the router would reintroduce the two-call latency and nondeterminism that §10.4 explicitly avoids. The value of router-aware PRM training is that a turn routed to Instruct gets an execution-shaped response and a turn routed to Thinking gets a planning-shaped response — because the fine-tune trained on that distinction — not because the router consults a reward model at runtime.

No profile bleeding (multi-profile invariant). The fine-tuning must prevent four failure modes: Instruct mode accidentally emitting thinking tokens (bad: wastes context, breaks latency budget); Thinking mode skipping reasoning for simple calls (bad: misses complex cases); Conversation mode emitting tool-call-shaped output for non-tool turns (bad: users see JSON where they wanted prose); Coding mode emitting conversational fluff (bad: code tasks need code, not chit-chat). The CacheRL recipe already addresses the second; the fine-tuning must add explicit negative examples for the others. Training data includes: 500 (prompt, Instruct-mode-response-with-thinking-tokens) pairs labeled as negative examples — the model learns to suppress thinking tokens under --reasoning-budget 0; 500 (prompt, Thinking-mode-response-without-reasoning) pairs labeled as negative examples — the model learns to emit reasoning traces under Thinking mode; 500 (prompt, Conversation-mode-response-with-tool-call-JSON) pairs labeled as negative examples — the model learns to keep conversation turns in prose unless the turn genuinely requires a tool call; 500 (prompt, Coding-mode-response-with-conversational-fluff) pairs labeled as negative examples — the model learns to produce code-shaped output for code tasks.

Target:

Metric	Hammer (specialist)	Combat Full target (multi-profile)	Combat Full + ToolPRM
BFCL non-live (Instruct)	81.42	high 60s – low 70s	low-to-mid 70s
BFCL non-live (Thinking)	81.42	high 60s – low 70s	low-to-mid 70s
BFCL non-live (Conversation)	n/a	high 60s – low 70s	low-to-mid 70s
BFCL live (Instruct)	95.00	mid 80s – low 90s	low 90s
BFCL live (Thinking)	95.00	mid 80s – low 90s	low 90s
Conversation turn quality	n/a	≥75% mean rubric	same
Coding HumanEval	n/a	≥60 (A.101)	same
Multi-turn	16.5	improved over base	improved
Destructive reliability (Thinking)	validated	improved	closer to specialist
Router accuracy	n/a	≥95% on 200 SUL-shaped turns	same
Destructive-action detection recall	n/a	100% (hard gate)	same
Caveat: The 2B parameter count and generalist VLM lineage create a hard ceiling. The net gain is real but it is not Hammer-grade specialist precision. If the requirement is Hammer-grade destructive-chain precision, Hammer must return as a swap-in.

The pre-fine-tuning InternVL3-2B BFCL non-live score is not currently measured. The A.63 gate (≥65) is only a meaningful validation if pre-fine-tuning is at or below 65. If pre-fine-tuning is already above 65, the fine-tuning cannot demonstrate added value against the gate, and A.63 should be re-read as "confirm the fine-tuned model does not regress below 65" rather than "the fine-tuned model must reach 65." The first A.63 run must record both pre- and post-fine-tuning BFCL non-live, per profile (Instruct and Thinking at minimum; Conversation and Coding if the corresponding gates have not yet been measured).

Cost: LoRA training ~$36 (Vast.ai / RunPod A100 40GB at ~$1.50/hr, same xLAM data, function masking script, a few hours of training). Function masking script ~2–3 days engineering. ToolPRM distillation training ~$20 (teacher inference + distillation). Profile-tagged data preparation ~1.5 days (relabeling the existing xLAM examples, plus generating the negative-example suites). **Total ~$56 + ~4.5 days engineering time.**

Measurement-driven decision: Run the LoRA training. Measure BFCL on the reference rig (per profile). Measure Conversation turn quality. Measure Coding HumanEval. Measure router accuracy on 200 SUL-shaped turns. Measure destructive-action recall on 100 scripted destructive triggers. If all gates pass (Instruct BFCL ≥65, Thinking BFCL ≥65, Conversation quality ≥ threshold, Coding HumanEval ≥60, router ≥95%, destructive recall 100%), the Hammer cut is final. If any fail, re-evaluate — options are (a) keep Hammer as swap-in, (b) re-run training with more data, (c) accept the lower ceiling if destructive-chain scenarios are rare enough.

Failure handling: E_LORA_MERGE_MISMATCH if cargo xtask verify-lora-merge fails cosine similarity >0.998 or output-token equality >98% assertions.

Test requirements: CI job cargo xtask verify-lora-merge runs 10 prompts against merged GGUF vs base+adapter; asserts cosine similarity >0.998 and output-token equality >98%. Additional CI tests for the profile design: merged GGUF respects --reasoning-budget 0 (no thinking tokens emitted under Instruct/Coding), emits thinking tokens under Thinking profile prefix, respects Conversation profile prefix (no tool-call shape unless prompted), respects Coding profile prefix (code-shaped output). If CI fails, build fails. BFCL measurement on the reference rig is the shipping gate (A.63).

Deep LoRA recipe: Reference: K2-Horizon-7B supports LoRA fine-tuning through Axolotl with trust_remote_code: true, lora_target_linear: true. Purpose: specialize K2's 32K-reasoning default to SUL-shaped outputs, so the model produces SUL-shaped tool calls without spending 32K reasoning tokens to reach them. Same "function masking + xLAM + profile-tagged data" recipe as Combat Full, applied to Deep. Profile tags for Deep: instruct, thinking, conversation, agentic_coding. The agentic_coding tag is Deep's workload. instruct and thinking are preserved for cases where Deep is used for non-coding conversational turns (rare, but supported). conversation for Deep's dialogue-shaped answers when used as a fallback reasoning backend. Adapter: jarvis_deep_tools.lora. Same distribution model (merged at build). Same CI verification (verify-lora-merge). Same negative-example suites (500 per failure mode). Training data for Deep: SUL's own agentic-coding traces (the sul-ai-native tool-call history), SUL's git history (public repo commits), and the ToolOrchestrationReward constrained-synthesis pipeline for multi-step tool orchestration. License: SUL's own traces are owned by SUL; ToolOrchestrationReward is verify-before-shipping.

2.15 Runtime configuration and soft degradation
Universal flags: -fa (Flash Attention, on every tier), -sm row, -ngl 99, -b 1024 (8 GB) / -b 512 (4 GB), -ub 512 (8 GB) / -ub 256 (4 GB), --reasoning-budget 0 (Instruct / Coding), --jinja (required for role separation), --no-context-shift (Qwen best practice). These flags are applied at the loader level for every tier; fa = true is implicit for every tier and validated by the config validator (Ch. 1 §4.2).

--reasoning-budget is profile-dependent for Combat Full. Instruct and Coding use 0 (no thinking tokens — execution fast path). Thinking uses a bounded positive budget. The exact budget is subject to the open question in the multi-profile handoff: likely 512–1024 tokens bounded, not unbounded, to preserve latency. Until that decision is finalized, Thinking mode's budget is specified as reasoning_budget = -1 (unbounded) in Ch. 1 §4.1's [ai.combat_full.thinking] block, with the note that the first A.63 run records the chosen budget based on measured latency. Conversation uses 256 — bounded positive, enough for conversational judgment, not full planning.

Sampling per profile:

Combat Full — Instruct: temp 0.2, top-p 0.9, top-k 40, min-p 0.05

Combat Full — Thinking: temp 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 40, min-p 0.05

Combat Full — Conversation: temp 0.7, top-p 0.95, top-k 40, min-p 0.05

Combat Full — Coding: temp 0.2, top-p 0.9, top-k 40, min-p 0.05

Deep: temp 0.1 structured / 0.2 code / 0.7 chat

Pre-created contexts per profile: Combat Full Instruct (2K), Thinking (4K), Conversation (16K, lazy-allocated no-game only), Coding (8K, research-gated); Deep Q5/Q4 (4K). Deep 8K on demand with asymmetric KV (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_1).

Persistent CUDA streams: Created at init, reused across llama_decode. ~200–500 µs per inference.

Batch tuning: -b 1024 -ub 512 at 8 GB (tighter batch saves ~50–100 MB per tier with no measurable throughput cost).

SubSpec integration (gated shipping component): For disk-backed Deep, construct a quantized substitute draft model from the offloaded layers. Lossless, training-free. 9.1× speedup for Qwen2.5-7B at 8 GB VRAM. SubSpec paper (arXiv:2509.18344). Theoretical ceiling on offloaded layers, not end-to-end shipping.

Qwen VL CPU offload: When --enable-vlm, vision encoder (mmproj) offloaded to CPU via --no-mmproj-offload. Reduces peak VRAM by 600–800 MB.

Two distinct mmproj flags, do not conflate: --no-mmproj disables multimodal projector loading entirely — Combat Mid (now cut) used this because its vision fallback was optional and the projector was loaded on demand. --no-mmproj-offload loads the projector but offloads it to CPU — the opt-in Qwen2.5-VL-3B path uses this to reduce peak VRAM. Combat Full uses neither: InternVL3-2B's InternViT encoder is bundled with the InternVL3 GGUF and loaded as part of the vision path (Ch. 8 §8.4).

Tiered soft degradation: context reduction → KV precision → batch → (variant swap removed — no variants exist to swap between). STAR-KV quality failure → GAAC fallback (§10.11) is a fourth degradation rung before refusal. Combat Full profile degradation — Thinking mode OOMing and Instruct mode taking over — is a router decision (§10.4), not a config-driven degradation, because Thinking OOM is transient (per-turn) rather than persistent. The router logs instruct_fallback_rate_pct (§10.20 / [ai.combat_router]) when this happens.

Thread count: Combat 4 (all profiles); Deep 6.

2.16 KV cache stack: sul-kv-compress trait, STAR-KV primary, GAAC fallback, Lynx promotion
Contract: §10.9 (STAR-KV), §10.10 (tiered KV cache), §10.11 (sul-kv-compress) — authoritative. Gates: A.18 (STAR-KV PPL + KL@D), A.97 (sul-kv-compress backends). Baselines: [kv_tier.star_kv], [kv_tier.gaac], [kv_tier.fallback], [kv_tier.palquant], [kv_tier.puzzlekv], [kv_tier.jolt], [kv_tier.turbo3], [kv_tier.tcq]. Boundary: Ch. 16 §16.1 (KV Boundary).

The practical floor was symmetric q8_0/q8_0 KV. The current stack is a trait-based compressor layer with three-tier caching:

Layer	Method	Compression	Quality	When active
Primary	STAR-KV low-rank + 3.2-bit quantized codes	up to 20×	Near-lossless (low-rank-aware mixed precision)	All tiers, all contexts
Lossless fallback	GAAC exponent-redundancy codec	1.405×	Bit-for-bit lossless	When STAR-KV quality fails the A.18 gate
Alternative compressors	PalQuant, PuzzleKV, JoLT, TurboQuant+ turbo3, TCQ	2–7.42×	Varies (see below)	Per-tier selection behind sul-kv-compress trait (A.97)
Tier promotion	Lynx split-stream transfer	N/A (bandwidth)	N/A (lossless transfer)	Cold → hot promotion in disk-backed mode
Compatibility with FA: STAR-KV and all compressors reconstruct to f16/BF16 before the FA kernel sees it. The FA–KV rule still applies to the reconstructed KV — both K and V are f16, which is symmetric. Compression precedes FA. GAAC is also compatible with FA — it round-trips BF16 without loss. Lynx is a transfer optimisation, not a compression; it does not interact with FA.

Throughput caveat (critical): STAR-KV's current design reconstructs to f16 before FA — exactly the "converting the whole cache to f16 per call" that llama.cpp's new SYCL DPAS kernel (b11980, PR #31125) eliminates for q4_0/q8_0 KV. The DPAS kernel runs FA directly on quantized KV blocks and measured 31.3 → 54.2 t/s (+73%) on B580, Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M, q4_0 KV, 16K. A ground-up CUDA kernel that dequantizes STAR-KV's low-rank + 3.2-bit codes inside the attention computation — same shape as DPAS but for STAR-KV's format — is an A.4 research entry (§10.26, A.105). This turns STAR-KV from "compression that costs throughput" into "compression that is throughput-neutral or better." It is the single highest-value ground-up performance change available for the STAR-KV path.

A.18 quality gate measures both PPL delta AND KL divergence at the logit level (KL@D). PPL alone can pass while attention logits are distorted in ways that matter for the Entity Ledger, tool-call structure, and OODA scaffold fields. TurboQuant+ documentation is explicit: "Methods that are strictly better under MSE are systematically worse under KL@D in deployment. MSE is a broken proxy for KV cache compression quality. Attention is not [linear]." A.97 extends the same gate to every sul-kv-compress backend.

STAR-KV model surgery is irreversible. STAR-KV models ship with an uncompressed sibling (§10.14) so a decompression failure is recoverable. The pair_verified_at timestamp gates the sibling's retention.

Deep KV choice under the 8 GB hardcap:

KV cache type	PPL	KL vs f16	Top-1 token agreement
f16	5.7438 ± 0.0355	baseline	n/a
q8_0	5.7433 ± 0.0355	0.0016 ± 0.0001	98.64% ± 0.03
turbo3 (~4.9×)	5.8092 ± 0.0360	0.0199 ± 0.0002	93.93% ± 0.06
turbo4 (~3.8×)	5.7810 ± 0.0359	0.0131 ± 0.0003	95.28% ± 0.06
Decisions:

4K context: -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 (KL 0.0016, top-1 98.64%, essentially free).

8K context: -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_1 asymmetric (K needs more precision than V; 45.3% of BF16 size at 94.2% p99 precision).

32K ceiling: -ctk q8_0 -ctv turbo4 if the context is ever raised that far.

Trellis-coded KV — the quality-first future lever. TCQ combines Fast Walsh-Hadamard rotation with Viterbi-optimal trellis encoding. Measured results: 3.25 bits per value produces lower perplexity than uncompressed FP16 KV (5.802 vs 5.805 at 2K) due to a norm-scaling regularisation effect; 4.25 bpv matches FP16 quality at half the VRAM of q8_0; 10–44% KL-divergence reduction over scalar quantization at 2–3 bits. Blocker: buun-llama-cpp fork, ~15% Viterbi encode tax, not in mainline. sul-kv-compress implements TCQ as a research backend. Gate A.97 covers it. This is the lever to pull when VRAM-reduction work begins — it is the only known method that can shrink the KV cache while improving its quality.

2.17 sul-kv-tier — tiered KV cache for disk-backed mode
Purpose: Implements three-tier KV cache: Hot (VRAM) — active attention window, full-speed attention. Warm (RAM) — recently used KV blocks, ~200 µs access. Cold (SSD) — inactive history, ~5 ms access, rarely touched.

Eviction: LRU combined with attention-score weighting.

Prefetch: predictive preloading overlaps disk I/O with compute. KVSwap reports 1.8× NVMe throughput improvement at 32K vs strongest baseline. KVSwap paper (R.4).

I/O path: non-mapped async on Windows (pread + FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, or DirectStorage for KV pages), not mmap. Benchmarks show 7.9 GB/s async vs 2.5 GB/s mmap on Windows.

Quantize before write: KV is already q8_0 (or q8_0/q5_1 asymmetric for Deep 8K); 2–4× smaller than f16, 2–4× less disk I/O per eviction, 2–4× more blocks fit in warm RAM.

Symmetric K/V rule: symmetric q8_0/q8_0 for all tiers at 4K; asymmetric q8_0/q5_1 permitted for Deep 8K. Asymmetric forbidden when FA on unless the storage format is STAR-KV/GAAC which reconstruct to uniform f16/BF16 before FA. STAR-KV and GAAC both reconstruct to symmetric f16/BF16 before FA sees them — STAR-KV/GAAC active does not violate this rule. The asymmetric q8_0/q5_1 path is safe because the FA kernel sees a uniform f16 reconstruction (it's a mixed storage format that reconstructs to uniform f16).

STAR-KV integration: The three-layer KV stack (§10.8) is implemented here. STAR-KV is primary; GAAC is lossless fallback; Lynx is split-stream promotion; alternative compressors (PalQuant/PuzzleKV/JoLT/turbo3/TCQ) are plugins behind sul-kv-compress. KV blocks are compressed before they are tiered (see §10.10 and §10.11).

method = "auto" vs method = "star_kv": STAR-KV replaces the symmetric q8_0 default when [ai.kv_tier] method = "star_kv". Under method = "auto" (the default), the loader consults the A.18 gate outcome: if A.18 passed, STAR-KV activates; if A.18 failed, GAAC is used. "auto" never silently falls back to symmetric q8_0 — it always resolves to STAR-KV or GAAC. The symmetric q8_0 default only applies when method = "uncompressed" is explicitly set.

GAAC fallback: When STAR-KV quality gate fails (A.18), tier falls back to GAAC (bit-for-bit lossless, 1.405×). GAAC round-trips BF16 without loss, so FA kernel sees symmetric BF16.

Lynx promotion: Cold → warm → hot uses Lynx split-stream transfer. Hot → warm → cold uses Lynx with anchor-first decode.

ReTrace dormant buffer integration: The ReTrace dormant token buffer is a new consumer of the STAR-KV compressed paged format. It does not need a new compression method — it reuses the existing STAR-KV/GAAC/Lynx stack, with the backtracking injection layer acting as the trigger for Lynx promotion. When ReTrace needs to restore dormant tokens at the backtracking layer, sul-kv-tier promotes those tokens from cold to hot via Lynx split-stream transfer. When ReTrace prunes redundant enriched pivots after context injection, the pruned pages are returned to the tier pool (evicted from hot, retained in warm for potential future access). The dormant buffer is sized to hold the full token set before pruning; for Combat Full (InternVL3-2B, Conversation profile's 16K context, max_dynamic_patch = 4), the dormant buffer is ~30–40 MB. For Thinking's 4K context, ~20 MB. For Instruct's 2K context, ~10 MB. The operational maximum is Conversation's 16K, so that's the size the buffer is allocated to; lower profiles fit with headroom.

Research references (not shipping path): OScaR INT2 (A.1 only); Palu low-rank projection; HARD-KV head-adaptive cascade. None in shipping path.

Placement policy: LRU + attention heuristic (ARGUS-compatible). ARGUS is a real llama.cpp KV-page placement policy. The initial release implements attention heuristic; kv_eviction_policy = "argus" resolves to lru_attention behavior and upgrades to attention-score-gated placement in a later gate.

Test requirements: Miri clean under concurrent read/prefetch/evict. No torn reads. Write-amplification counter increments correctly. Prefetch hit-rate >70% on scripted long-context workload. KVSwap-style throughput within 20% of published 1.8× benchmark. Recovery from cold-page read failure without corrupting hot/warm state. STAR-KV decompression failure → GAAC fallback → uncompressed → disk-backed → CPU offload → refuse. Each rung tested with failure-injection. GAAC round-trip is bit-for-bit lossless — fuzz-tested against 1000 prompt/response KV pairs. Lynx promotion does not corrupt KV — tested with mid-flight eviction during promotion. STAR-KV + FA compatibility preserved — FA fused kernel path traced, no asymmetry. ReTrace dormant buffer tests: dormant tokens correctly stored in STAR-KV compressed paged format; Lynx promotion from cold to hot at backtracking layer preserves token fidelity; post-absorption pruning returns pages correctly to the tier pool; dormant buffer sized for Conversation's 16K context (operational max); lower profiles fit with headroom; failure-injection: forced dormant buffer overflow triggers E_RETRACE_DORMANT_OVERFLOW and drops oldest dormant tokens. sul-kv-compress trait integration: each backend (STAR-KV, GAAC, PalQuant, PuzzleKV, JoLT, turbo3, TCQ) loads and passes A.97's quality gate; per-tier selection works correctly; fallback chain engages correctly per §10.24 KC-1.

2.18 STAR-KV implementation contract
Purpose: Low-rank + 3.2-bit quantized KV compression with near-lossless quality (up to 20× compression) and FA compatibility.

Architecture: Model surgery (offline, one-time): per-head low-rank decomposition + 3.2-bit quantized codes + per-head mixed-precision fallback for high-rank heads. Irreversible. Reconstruction: STAR-KV reconstructs to f16 before FA kernel sees it. Both K and V are f16 — symmetric. Decompression cache: small LRU in VRAM for hot KV blocks. Miss triggers on-the-fly decompression from warm/RAM or cold/SSD. Sibling pair: every STAR-KV model ships with an uncompressed sibling GGUF. pair_verified_at timestamp gates sibling retention. If decompression fails, runtime can swap to the sibling uncompressed model without re-download. Version pinning: surgery version and runtime version must match. E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH refuses to load.

Throughput caveat (critical): llama.cpp b11980 added a SYCL DPAS flash attention kernel for quantized KV cache (#31125). The description is architecturally important: "Decode and small batches (1 to 31 query tokens) now run flash attention straight on q4_0 and q8_0 KV blocks, instead of scalar dequant or converting the whole cache to f16 per call." Measured on B580, Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M, q4_0 KV, 16K: 31.3 → 54.2 t/s — a 73% throughput improvement. STAR-KV's current design reconstructs to f16 before FA — exactly the "converting the whole cache to f16 per call" the DPAS kernel eliminates. A ground-up CUDA kernel that dequantizes STAR-KV's low-rank + 3.2-bit codes inside the attention computation — same shape as DPAS but for STAR-KV's format — is an A.4 research entry (§10.26, A.105). ~3–4 weeks for a CUDA developer. This turns STAR-KV from "compression that costs throughput" into "compression that is throughput-neutral or better."

KL@D gate (A.18). PPL alone can pass while attention logits are distorted in ways that matter for the Entity Ledger, tool-call structure, and OODA scaffold fields. TurboQuant+ documentation: "Methods that are strictly better under MSE are systematically worse under KL@D in deployment. MSE is a broken proxy for KV cache compression quality." A.18 measures both PPL delta AND KL divergence at the logit level. A.97 extends the same gate to every sul-kv-compress backend.

Failure handling: see failures.md KV-1 through KV-7 and MS-1 through MS-3. MS-4 is obsolete (fork deleted).

Test requirements: Miri clean on decompression paths. Reconstruct-to-f16 preserves symmetry (K and V both f16). FA fused kernel path traced to confirm FA still engages. PPL delta <2% vs f16 on 1000-prompt eval. KL@D below measured f16 baseline at target compression ratio. Decompression cache LRU correct under concurrent access. Version mismatch (E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH) refuses load without silently loading wrong-model. Sibling pair mismatch (E_STAR_KV_PAIR_MISMATCH) refuses load. Fork compatibility: E_STAR_KV_UNSUPPORTED_TREE no longer fires (fork deleted); the check remains in the code for future fork scenarios but is effectively unreachable in the shipping path. Failure-injection test: cargo test -p sul-kv-tier --features=failure-injection -- --force-failure=kv-1 exercises the KV-1 → GAAC fallback. KL@D gate failure (KV-8) → GAAC fallback.

2.19 sul-kv-compress — KV compressor trait with multiple backends
Purpose: Trait-based abstraction that lets STAR-KV, GAAC, PalQuant, PuzzleKV, JoLT, TurboQuant+ turbo3, TCQ sit behind the same interface with per-tier selection. The existing sul-kv-tier becomes the tiering layer; the compressors become plugins.

Architecture:

text
sul-kv-compress/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                          # KvCompressor trait + registry
│   ├── trait_def.rs                    # trait + associated types
│   ├── backends/
│   │   ├── star_kv_backend.rs          # wraps `star-kv` crate
│   │   ├── gaac_backend.rs             # wraps `gaac` crate
│   │   ├── palquant_backend.rs         # PalQuant implementation
│   │   ├── puzzlekv_backend.rs         # PuzzleKV implementation
│   │   ├── jolt_backend.rs             # JoLT implementation
│   │   ├── turbo3_backend.rs           # TurboQuant+ turbo3 implementation
│   │   └── tcq_backend.rs              # Trellis-coded quantization
│   ├── fallback.rs                     # fallback chain logic
│   ├── quality_gate.rs                 # A.97 verification (PPL + KL@D + identity)
│   └── multi_session_test.rs           # PalQuant-style identity preservation harness
└── tests/
    └── ...
Trait signature:

rust
pub trait KvCompressor: Send + Sync {
    fn compress(&self, kv: &mut KvBuffer) -> Result<CompressedKv, KvCompressError>;
    fn decompress(&self, compressed: &CompressedKv, out: &mut KvBuffer) -> Result<(), KvCompressError>;
    fn quality_gate(&self) -> QualityGateStatus;
    fn compression_ratio(&self) -> f32;
    fn throughput_delta_pct(&self) -> f32;
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
}

pub enum QualityGateStatus {
    Passed { ppl_delta_pct: f32, kl_d_pct: f32 },
    Failed { reason: &'static str },
    Pending,
}
Backend specifications:

STAR-KV — current primary, up to 20× compression, throughput cost due to f16 reconstruction. Wraps star-kv crate (§10.10).

GAAC — bit-for-bit lossless, 1.405×. Wraps gaac crate.

PalQuant — 7.42× on Qwen3-8B, 5.02× on Llama-3.2-3B. Calibration-free. Passes multi-session identity-preservation test at all levels up to 7.42×. Uses mean-of-top-4 weighted absolute error for K and warp-MSE for V. Recommended fallback if STAR-KV's measured ratio falls below 5×.

PuzzleKV — 60% storage → >96% full-KV; with INT4, 18.7% storage → >93% full-KV (~5.3×). Training- and calibration-free.

JoLT — 2–3× compression, <0.2% PPL degradation, RULER 64K near-lossless through 3×. Training-free, calibration-free. Near-lossless first tier.

TurboQuant+ turbo3 — ~4.6× compression at <1.5% PPL loss, cross-backend (CUDA dp4a, HIP/ROCm, Vulkan coopmat, Metal). Design principle is attention-product distortion, not MSE. Not yet upstreamed — long-lived feature branch.

Trellis-coded quantization (TCQ) — 3.25–4.25 bits per value, matches or beats FP16 quality through regularisation; 10–44% KL-divergence reduction over scalar quantization at 2–3 bits. Quality-first research path.

A.18/A.97 quality gate measures both PPL delta AND KL divergence at the logit level (KL@D). PPL alone can pass while attention logits are distorted in ways that matter for the Entity Ledger, tool-call structure, and OODA scaffold fields. TurboQuant+ documentation is explicit: "Methods that are strictly better under MSE are systematically worse under KL@D in deployment. MSE is a broken proxy for KV cache compression quality." A.97 requires each backend to pass both PPL delta <2% AND KL@D below the measured f16 baseline at its target compression ratio, plus multi-session identity preservation (PalQuant's test — critical for the Entity Ledger, which requires that the same entity remains the same entity across sessions).

Multi-session identity preservation test: the PalQuant test constructs a KV cache from session A, compresses it, decompresses it in session B, and checks whether entity tokens (specific UUIDs, file paths, table names) still map to the same positions and logits. The threshold is the same as PalQuant's published threshold (>95% identity preservation at the target compression ratio). This is critical because the Entity Ledger in Ch. 11 §11.6 requires that the model sees the same entity in the same place across sessions — a compression backend that silently shifts entity positions would defeat the Entity Ledger.

Failure handling: KC-1 (backend A.97 fail) → fall back to STAR-KV/GAAC per trait fallback order. KC-2 (multi-session identity fail) → fall back to GAAC (lossless), which passes.

Test requirements: Each backend: PPL delta <2% on 1000-prompt eval. Each backend: KL@D below f16 baseline at target compression ratio. Each backend: multi-session identity preservation ≥95%. Each backend: compression_ratio() matches published values within 10%. Each backend: throughput_delta_pct() measured on reference rig; STAR-KV measures the reconstruction cost vs DPAS-style direct-quantized-FA baseline. Fallback chain engages correctly: KC-1 → STAR-KV → GAAC → uncompressed. Fallback chain engages correctly: KC-2 → GAAC (lossless). Miri clean on all backend unsafe paths. Failure-injection: --force-failure=kc-1 and --force-failure=kc-2 each tested.

Release: shipping (STAR-KV, GAAC) / gated shipping (PalQuant, PuzzleKV, JoLT) / research (turbo3, TCQ). R2 per releases.md.

2.20 sul-spec-draft — RIFT draft cache compression
Purpose: RIFT-style draft-cache compression for external drafters. Solves decode staleness — prefill-selected KV becomes stale as generation progresses.

What it actually is: RIFT solves decode staleness with three components: Allocation — split active cache between importance-selected positions and a recent-token window. Refresh — RIFT-stat (static), RIFT-dyn (refreshed every N steps), RIFT-ada (adaptive). Compressibility training — drafter fine-tuning with sparse attention masks.

The selection algorithm is worth building (~400 lines, ~2 weeks). The compressibility training is NOT worth building — DFlash and ChainFlow are upstream models; re-training requires the upstream training pipeline and GPU time.

Activation threshold: draft cache >32 MB.

Dormant across the current shipping architecture: Combat Full — Medusa heads and phrase head read target hidden states; no separate draft cache → not applicable.
