Deep with ChainFlow / LiLiCorr — ChainFlow draft cache at 4K context is ~10 MB; at 8K ~20 MB. Below the 32 MB threshold → dormant. Deep at 32K context — draft cache ~80 MB → would activate, but this is a research configuration. Deep Extended (cut) — no drafter → not applicable.

The wrapper is built as a future-proofing piece — it activates the moment a tier grows an external drafter or crosses 32 MB of draft cache.

Architecture:

text
sul-spec-draft/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                          # public API
│   ├── rift_selection.rs               # allocation + refresh (ground-up)
│   ├── rift_refresh.rs                 # RIFT-stat / RIFT-dyn / RIFT-ada
│   ├── activation_gate.rs              # 32 MB threshold check
│   ├── unispec_adapter.rs              # thin adapter over `unispec` crate
│   └── draft_cache.rs                  # cache abstraction
└── tests/
    └── ...
Public API:

rust
pub trait DraftCacheCompressor: Send + Sync {
    fn compress(&self, draft_cache: &mut DraftCache) -> Result<CompressedDraftCache, RiftError>;
    fn refresh(&mut self, compressed: &mut CompressedDraftCache, recent_window: &DraftWindow) -> Result<(), RiftError>;
    fn should_engage(&self, cache_size_mb: f32) -> bool;  // 32 MB threshold
    fn stats(&self) -> RiftStats;
}
Config additions ([ai.speculative]):

toml
draft_kv_compress_threshold_mb = 32
draft_refresh_interval_steps = 32       # RIFT-dyn default
draft_type_k = "q8_0"                   # KVarN per-K/V bit-width
draft_type_v = "q8_0"
ubd = 128                                # draft micro-batch
UniSpec adapter: sul-spec-draft::unispec_adapter is a thin adapter over the unispec crate. Feeds a SUL-tuned retrieval index (tool-call history, OODA state, Entity Ledger), calibrates confidence thresholds on the SUL tool-call eval set, writes candidates directly into the llama_batch tree-attention structure without an intermediate copy. Roughly 1–2 weeks.

Gate A.98: ship the wrapper when DFlash acceptance retention is ≥95% and ChainFlow retention is ≥95% at the configured draft KV budget, and when the wrapper adds ≤5 ms per refresh step. Does not require the paper's 98% figure (that depends on compressibility training SUL is not building).

Failure handling: SD-1 (draft cache below threshold) → wrapper not engaged. SD-2 (refresh stall) → drop to RIFT-stat (static), log.

Test requirements: should_engage() returns false for cache sizes ≤32 MB, true for >32 MB. Selection algorithm preserves acceptance retention ≥95% on scripted 1000-prompt test set. Refresh (RIFT-dyn) at 32-step interval adds ≤5 ms per refresh. RIFT-stat fallback engaged when RIFT-dyn stalls. Miri clean. Failure-injection: --force-failure=sd-1 (below threshold) and --force-failure=sd-2 (refresh stall) each tested.

Release: shipping (dormant, activates when draft cache >32 MB). R2 per releases.md.

2.21 Speculation implementation paths
Purpose: Ordered per-tier speculation chains with fallback, startup benchmark selection, and Medusa/phrase/UniSpec/LiLiCorr/ChainFlow rung support.

Module structure in sul-ai-native/src/:

speculative.rs — chain dispatcher. Reads [ai.speculative] &lt;tier&gt;_chain from config, iterates rungs, verifies each rung's availability, caches winner. Recognized rungs: medusa, phrase, unispec, chainflow, lilicorr, ngram, none. DFlash and EAGLE-3 are recognized rung names but are not in any shipping chain.

medusa.rs — Medusa-1 shared-LM-head loader (PyTorch .pt → Candle tensors), temperature scaling, candidate tree builder, llama_batch construction with tree attention mask. Feeds llama.cpp's existing batch-verify path (no fork).

phrase_head.rs — MLP head loader, draft vocabulary table, greedy longest-match expansion.

unispec_adapter.rs — thin adapter over the unispec crate (sul-spec-draft::unispec_adapter). Feeds a SUL-tuned retrieval index (tool-call history, OODA state, Entity Ledger), calibrates confidence thresholds on the SUL tool-call eval set, writes candidates directly into the llama_batch tree-attention structure without an intermediate copy.

chainflow.rs — flow-matching drafter loader + integrator. One to two flow steps.

lilicorr — new rung handler (mainline llama.cpp v0.7.0+, PR #30506). Joint candidate scoring across the draft block, no additional backbone VRAM.

Startup benchmark: 30 s per tier, cached to %APPDATA%\\SUL\bench\. For each rung except none, measure effective decode tok/s and acceptance rate. Pick winner. Verify acceptance ≥ floor. Cache result. Subsequent launches read cache in <100 ms.

Combat Full has one chain, not per-profile. The combat_chain = ["medusa", "phrase", "unispec", "ngram", "none"] in [ai.speculative] applies to all four Combat Full profiles. The target model is the same; the drafter predicts the same target's next tokens regardless of profile. There is no per-profile chain.

Chain composition: ordered arrays. Every chain terminates in "none". E_SPEC_CHAIN_UNTERMINATED if not. --spec-type required per §10.24 SP-8.

Test requirements: Chain validator: all chains terminate in "none". E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET fires at startup if any tier has a draft model loaded and no --spec-type. E_SPEC_CHAIN_UNTERMINATED fires if any chain does not end in "none". E_SPEC_VERIFY_MISMATCH fires when draft tokens diverge from target logits (failure-injection test sp-5). E_UNISPEC_LOW_ACCEPTANCE fires when acceptance falls below floor; falls back to n-gram. E_SPEC_TOKENIZER_MISMATCH fires when draft tokenizer ≠ target tokenizer; refuses speculation for that tier. E_MEDUSA_TEMP_SCALING_MISSING fires at startup if temperature scaling is not enabled (SP-12). E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT fires at startup if own-LM-head variant is configured (SP-13). Each path's acceptance rate benchmarked and cached. Startup benchmark selects winner ≥10% better than fixed default. Combat Full chain has one entry (combat_chain); adding a per-profile chain is a config error (rejected by validator). Medusa head loads correctly from PyTorch .pt → Candle tensors; byte-identical .pt round-trip after conversion. Medusa temperature scaling applied correctly; speculative logits divided by temperature before softmax. Phrase head MLP produces identical output to greedy decoding up to FP tie-breaking on 1000-prompt test set.

Benchmarks (xtask spec-bench):

spec_bench.py::medusa — Medusa-1 acceptance + speedup. Produces [ai.speculative.medusa] *.

spec_bench.py::phrase — Phrase-level head acceptance + speedup. Produces [ai.speculative.phrase] *.

spec_bench.py::unispec — UniSpec acceptance + speedup. Produces [ai.speculative.unispec] *.

spec_bench.py::lilicorr — LiLiCorr acceptance + speedup. Produces [ai.speculative.lilicorr] *.

spec_bench.py::chainflow — ChainFlow acceptance + speedup. Produces [ai.speculative.chainflow] *.

spec_bench.py::chain_validator — Config validator pass rate. Produces [ai.speculative.fallback] spec_chain_validator_pass.

spec_bench.py::rift — RIFT acceptance retention + activation threshold. Produces [ai.speculative.rift] *.

2.22 sul-quant — VLM-aware quantization toolchain
Purpose: Wrap the public SPEED-Q pipeline (github.com/antgroup/SPEED-Q, AAAI 2026, arXiv:2511.08914) and add APEX-style layer-wise precision planning. SPEED-Q 4-bit brings InternVL3-2B from 3,984.5 MB BF16 to 1,454.6 MB (~63% reduction); 2-bit is 1,218.7 MB (~69%, 6× higher accuracy than prior 2-bit methods). APEX-style planner protects early and late layers (Q6_K first/last 5), Q5_K attention projections, Q4_K middle FFN — calibrated on SUL tool-call traces via imatrix. Runs on standard llama.cpp (each layer is a standard K-quant type). Applies to InternVL3-2B where there is ~4.55 GB of headroom under the 8 GB cap.

Architecture:

text
sul-quant/
├── Cargo.toml
├── build.rs                            # CMake invocation on vendor/speed-q/
├── vendor/
│   └── speed-q/                        # git submodule, pinned commit
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                          # public API
│   ├── speed_q_wrap.rs                 # FFI to SPEED-Q C++/CUDA kernels
│   ├── apex_planner.rs                 # ground-up APEX layer-wise precision planner
│   ├── imatrix_extractor.rs            # calibration data extraction from SUL traces
│   ├── gguf_emitter.rs                 # emits K-quant GGUF (no custom format)
│   └── quality_gate.rs                 # A.96 verification harness
└── models/
    └── imatrix_sul_traces.bin          # calibration data from SUL tool-call traces
APEX planner (ground-up piece): Protects early and late layers (Q6_K for first/last 5), Q5_K for attention projections, Q4_K for middle FFN layers. Calibrated on SUL's tool-call traces (imatrix), not generic corpus. Outputs mixed-precision GGUF that runs on standard llama.cpp — no fork needed because each layer is a standard K-quant type. Roughly 1–2 weeks for the planner. Applies to Combat Full (where there's ~4.55 GB of headroom under the 8 GB cap) not Deep (where the cap is binding).

Why the standard-llama.cpp constraint matters: SPEED-Q's own ViT-quantized output requires a fork of llama.cpp (custom ViT quantization path). We do NOT ship SPEED-Q's ViT-quantized output. We ship SPEED-Q's quantized weights (via the APEX-planned K-quant GGUF) — the APEX planner selects which layers get which K-quant type, and the resulting file is a standard llama.cpp GGUF. SPEED-Q is a reference for the "which layers can be compressed safely" methodology, not a runtime dependency. This preserves the single-mainline-tree architecture that the K2 merge established.

LiteRT independent confirmation: Google's LiteRT-LM InternVL3-2B production quantization confirms the modality split: int8 vision encoder (InternViT-300M + projector, 256 image tokens per 448×448), int4 LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B decoder, symmetric blockwise-32 + OCTAV), INT8 input embedding. Total 1.43 GB. Measured throughput: Galaxy S26 GPU decode 34.4 tok/s, prefill 573 tok/s, TTFT 380 ms. The SPEED-Q 4-bit figure (1,454.6 MB) is the desktop CUDA equivalent. Two independent confirmations of the same ~1.4 GB envelope.

Gate A.96: SPEED-Q 4-bit on InternVL3-2B holds the A.63 per-profile gates (Instruct BFCL ≥65, Thinking BFCL ≥65, Conversation quality ≥ threshold). SPEED-Q 2-bit holds them within 2% absolute.

Failure handling: QT-1 (A.96 fail) → fall back to llama.cpp Q4_K_S. QT-2 (2-bit A.96 fail) → fall back to SPEED-Q 4-bit. QT-3 (APEX planner fail) → fall back to SPEED-Q 4-bit uniform.

Test requirements: SPEED-Q 4-bit on InternVL3-2B holds A.63 per-profile gates. SPEED-Q 2-bit on InternVL3-2B holds A.63 per-profile gates within 2% absolute. APEX-planned mixed-precision GGUF holds A.63 per-profile gates and passes cargo xtask gguf-check. APEX-planned GGUF loads on unmodified llama.cpp (no fork) — verified by CI. imatrix calibration data extracted correctly from SUL tool-call traces. Miri clean on FFI paths. Failure-injection: QT-1, QT-2, QT-3 each tested.

Release: shipping (4-bit) / gated shipping (2-bit, APEX). R2 per releases.md.

2.23 sul-toolprm — distilled cross-encoder
Purpose: Replace ToolRM Qwen3-4B generative backbone (2.3–2.5 GB Q4) with a cross-encoder at ~100–300M params (~60–180 MB Q4). Distilled from ToolRM-4B teacher on ToolPref-Pairwise-30K + SUL traces.

The problem: current ToolRM Qwen3-4B generative backbone is 2.3–2.5 GB Q4. Combined with Combat Full's 1.3–1.45 GB, it exceeds the 3 GB general combat ceiling by ~2 GB. The spec previously structurally disabled ToolPRM on HD2.

The fix: distill to a cross-encoder at ~100–300M params, ~60–180 MB at Q4.

Reference: ToolRM (arXiv:2510.26167), ToolPRM (ACL 2026), TRM (ICLR 2026). The ACL 2026 ToolPRM paper's own summary: "1.5B small model + ToolPRM approaches 3B, 3B approaches 7B, 7B exceeds 32B."

Architecture:

text
sul-toolprm/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs                          # public API
│   ├── encoder.rs                      # 12-layer × 768 (base) or 6-layer × 1024 (wide)
│   ├── heads.rs                        # scalar reward + per-field auxiliary heads
│   ├── scoring.rs                      # coarse-to-fine beam scoring
│   ├── score_cache.rs                  # (function_name, arg_structure_hash, context_fingerprint) cache
│   └── inference.rs                    # one forward pass per (context, candidate) pair
├── train.py                            # PyTorch distillation pipeline
└── models/
    └── sul_toolprm_enc_q4.gguf         # ~60-180 MB Q4
Architecture: Encoder: 12 layers × 768 hidden (base) or 6 layers × 1024 (wide) — Candle implementation. Input: TSCG-compiled schema + OODA scaffold state + candidate call. Output: scalar reward + per-field auxiliary heads (function name, param name, param value). Quantization: Q4_K_M default, Q3_K_M for HD2 co-residency.

Training: Teacher: ToolRM-4B preference scores on ToolPref-Pairwise-30K + SUL's own tool-call traces. Distillation loss: Bradley-Terry ranking + per-field cross-entropy + KL against teacher. Router-aware auxiliary head: profile-conditional quality signal, training-time only, baked into encoder.

Runtime integration: sul-agent beam search: coarse-to-fine scoring at end-of-call (top-M scored once, top-N retained) instead of per-step scoring. Score cache keyed on (function_name, arg_structure_hash, context_fingerprint) — Combat Full's tool-call distribution is highly repetitive, so cache hit rate should be measurable. [ai.combat_full] toolprm_model default changes from "toolrm_qwen3_4b" to "sul_toolprm_enc"; the 4B variant remains selectable for ED.

What this restores on HD2: Combat Full (SPEED-Q 4-bit after sul-quant): ~1.45 GB. Distilled cross-encoder (Q4): ~60–180 MB. PP-OCRv5: ~21 MB. Total: ~1.53–1.65 GB — comfortably inside the 3 GB general combat ceiling, with ~1.35 GB headroom.

Gate A.100: ship when: (a) cross-encoder ranking accuracy on TRBench-BFCL is within 2 pp of the ToolRM-4B teacher's pairwise accuracy. (b) end-to-end tool-call accuracy on BFCL non-live + live improves ≥3 pp over no-PRM baseline. (c) cross-encoder VRAM at Q4 ≤ 200 MB. (d) forward-pass latency ≤ 15 ms. (e) score-cache hit rate ≥ 40% on a 200-turn session. (f) coarse-to-fine produces ≥95% of full-step-scoring tool-call accuracy. (g) on HD2, Combat Full (SPEED-Q 4-bit) + cross-encoder + OCR fits within 3 GB with ≥200 MB headroom.

Failure handling: TP-1 (A.100 fail) → fall back to no-PRM baseline. TP-2 (load fail) → fall back to no-PRM baseline. TP-3 (score cache thrash) → disable cache, log.

Test requirements: Ranking accuracy within 2 pp of teacher on TRBench-BFCL. End-to-end tool-call accuracy +3 pp over no-PRM baseline. VRAM ≤ 200 MB at Q4. Forward pass ≤ 15 ms (single (context, candidate) pair). Score-cache hit rate ≥ 40% on 200-turn session. Coarse-to-fine produces ≥95% of full-step-scoring accuracy. HD2 co-residency fits with ≥200 MB headroom. Miri clean on FFI paths. Failure-injection: TP-1, TP-2, TP-3 each tested.

Release: shipping. R2 per releases.md.

2.24 ReTrace implementation contract
Purpose: Backtracking-aware visual token compression for Combat Full (InternVL3-2B). ~90% KV cache reduction, 2.83× prefill speedup, 100% benchmark retention at 11.1% token retention.

Architecture (four stages):

Token saliency computation (encoder-level): reads InternViT attention layers 6–12. Buffer combines three subsets: global saliency, diversity cues, and pivot set. Runs once per inference pass. Read-only attention analysis — no weights modified.

Dormant token state (KV cache buffer): non-pivot tokens moved to a separate KV buffer outside layer-wise computation. Quantized q8_0, sized to hold the full token set before pruning. Uses STAR-KV compressed paged format (reuses existing stack — no new compression method).

Backtracking window restoration: at the backtracking layer, dormant tokens restored via selective dequantize-and-attend. Injection layer identified dynamically per inference pass (not hardcoded). This is what enables the 2.83× prefill speedup.

Post-absorption pruning: after context injection, redundant enriched pivots pruned. Irreversible for the current pass. Pruned pages returned to the tier pool.

SUL-specific tuning:

Parameter	Value
Saliency source layers	Encoder layers 6–12
Pivot set size	64 tokens (vs 256 per patch)
Backtracking injection layer	Dynamic per inference pass
Dormant buffer quantization	q8_0
Pruning threshold	Attention mass <0.01
Mode-agnostic: ReTrace compression is the same for all Combat Full profiles. The dormant buffer is sized for Conversation profile's 16K context (larger) so all lower profiles fit with headroom (~30–40 MB allocated of ~40 MB for Conversation, ~20 MB used for Thinking, ~10 MB used for Instruct, ~15 MB used for Coding). No profile-specific ReTrace configuration.

Integration with sul-kv-tier: Dormant buffer uses STAR-KV compressed paged format. Lynx promotion: dormant tokens promoted via anchor-first decode when the backtracking injection layer demands them. GAAC lossless fallback if STAR-KV quality gate fails. Decompression cache holds hot dormant blocks.

Performance contract:

Metric	Baseline	ReTrace
Vision KV cache (Conversation 16K)	~0.8–1.2 GB	~0.04–0.08 GB
Vision KV cache (Thinking 4K)	~0.1–0.2 GB	~0.01–0.02 GB
Prefill latency	Baseline	2.83× faster
Total Combat Full VRAM (Instruct)	~1.65–1.75 GB	~1.30–1.35 GB
Total Combat Full VRAM (Thinking)	~1.70–1.80 GB	~1.35–1.45 GB
Total Combat Full VRAM (Conversation)	~2.7–2.9 GB (16K KV)	~1.25–1.30 GB
Total Combat Full VRAM (Coding)	~1.55–1.65 GB	~1.15–1.30 GB
Benchmark retention (MMB, MMBCN, POPE, SQAI, MME)	100%	100% at 11.1% token retention
Benchmarks (retained 100% at 11.1% retention): MMB 80.8, MMBCN 79.0, POPE 89.9, SQAI 95.7, MME 2221.

The Combat Full VRAM figures (~1.25–1.45 GB) assume ReTrace is active. Without ReTrace, Combat Full is ~1.55–1.80 GB (profile-dependent). ReTrace is a mandatory optimization (Phase 2 VRAM posture) and ships as soon as A.54 passes. R0 ships Combat Full Instruct without ReTrace at ~1.65–1.75 GB; R0.1 adds ReTrace when A.54 passes and drops to ~1.5 GB; R2+ ships with ReTrace, ToolPRM, and the full spec chain. All configurations fit the 3 GB general combat ceiling (Phase 2).

Failure handling: E_RETRACE_UNAVAILABLE — saliency layers or dormant buffer unavailable → fall back to full-token baseline for the session (VRAM cost +0.3–0.4 GB, pushing Instruct to ~1.65–1.75 GB and Thinking to ~1.70–1.80 GB). Mode E. E_RETRACE_DORMANT_OVERFLOW — dormant buffer exceeded capacity → drop oldest dormant tokens, log. Non-fatal. E_RETRACE_BACKTRACK_INJECTION — backtracking layer injection failed → fall back to full-token baseline for that pass. Non-fatal.

Test requirements: Miri clean on saliency computation, dormant buffer management, backtracking injection. Reconstruct-to-f16 preserves vision token fidelity. Benchmark retention ≥95% at 11.1% token retention on MMB, POPE, SQAI. Dormant buffer LRU correct under concurrent access. Backtracking injection layer selection is stable across runs. Prefill speedup ≥2.5× at 11.1% token retention. Failure-injection: forced saliency failure falls back to full-token baseline for that pass. Dormant buffer sized for Conversation profile's 16K context; Instruct and Thinking fit within the same buffer with headroom (verified by test: no profile overflows the Conversation-sized dormant buffer).

Release: shipping (blocker for Combat Full, all profiles). R2 per releases.md.

Benchmarks (xtask retrace-bench):

retrace_bench.py::saliency — Saliency computation latency. Produces [ai.combat_full] retrace_saliency_ms.

retrace_bench.py::dormant_buffer — Dormant buffer size + LRU. Produces [ai.combat_full] retrace_dormant_mb.

retrace_bench.py::retention — Token retention ratio. Produces [ai.combat_full] retrace_retention_pct.

retrace_bench.py::benchmark_retention — MMB, MMBCN, POPE, SQAI, MME at 11.1% retention. Produces [ai.combat_full] retrace_benchmark_retention.

retrace_bench.py::prefill_speedup — Prefill speedup vs baseline. Produces [ai.combat_full] retrace_prefill_speedup.

2.25 sul-ai-native performance contract
Single llama.cpp build: mainline b12207+ for every model. K2-Horizon support is included as of b11454 (PR #29535). No fork, no PrismML. arch.rs selects by GGUF general.architecture: qwen2, qwen2.5, qwen2.5-coder, qwen3, qwen3.5, hammer2, internvl3, k2_horizon → mainline tree. Unknown → E_UNKNOWN_ARCH.

PrismML patches: removed. PrismML is not in the build. The 262K-context capability that PrismML provided is capability, not the shipped deployment — SUL ships Deep at 4K–8K default with 32K ceiling. The 64K+ context window is not in the shipping release (A.70).

KV cache: symmetric q8_0/q8_0 for all FA-enabled tiers except Deep 8K. Deep 8K uses asymmetric q8_0 (K) / q5_1 (V) — K needs more precision than V; 45.3% of BF16 size at 94.2% p99 precision. FA receives f16/BF16 reconstructed from whichever storage format is active (q8_0, asymmetric q8_0/q5_1, STAR-KV, or GAAC) — "symmetric" refers to the FA-facing reconstruction being uniform K/V, not to the on-disk format. STAR-KV replaces this when [ai.kv_tier] method = "star_kv"; GAAC replaces it when STAR-KV quality gate fails; PalQuant/PuzzleKV/JoLT/turbo3/TCQ replace it when method selects them per sul-kv-compress. Asymmetric K/V forbidden when FA on; E_KV_ASYMMETRIC_FA fires on load.

method = "auto" resolves to STAR-KV or GAAC. Under method = "auto" (the default), the loader consults the A.18 gate outcome: if A.18 passed, STAR-KV activates; if A.18 failed, GAAC is used. "auto" never silently falls back to symmetric q8_0 — it always resolves to STAR-KV or GAAC. The symmetric q8_0 default only applies when [ai.kv_tier] method = "uncompressed" is explicitly set (or when STAR-KV/GAAC are unavailable on the current hardware).

Speculation integration: speculative.rs dispatches by chain. New module paths: medusa.rs, phrase_head.rs, unispec_adapter.rs (thin adapter over unispec crate), chainflow.rs, lilicorr rung handler (recognized by speculative.rs, mainline in llama.cpp v0.7.0+). DFlash and EAGLE-3 remain recognized rung names but are not in any shipping chain.

--spec-type refactor: -md no longer auto-enables. Config validator raises E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET.

Universal flags: see §10.7 (authoritative). The only tier-specific note in this section is the profile-dependent --reasoning-budget behavior for Combat Full.

Sampling (per profile): see §10.7.

Pre-created contexts per profile: Combat Full Instruct (2K), Thinking (4K), Conversation (16K lazy no-game), Coding (8K research); Deep Q5/Q4 (4K). Deep 8K on demand with asymmetric KV.

Persistent CUDA streams: Created at init, reused across llama_decode. ~200–500 µs per inference.

Batch tuning: -b 1024 -ub 512 at 8 GB (was 2048/512 in v6.8 — tighter batch saves ~50–100 MB per tier with no measurable throughput cost).

Speculative decoding benchmarked, not hardcoded: 30 s sweep on first load. Combat Full (all profiles share one chain): Medusa → phrase → UniSpec → n-gram. Deep: ChainFlow → LiLiCorr → UniSpec → n-gram. Winner cached.

SubSpec integration (gated shipping component): For disk-backed Deep, construct a quantized substitute draft model from the offloaded layers. Lossless, training-free. 9.1× speedup for Qwen2.5-7B at 8 GB VRAM. SubSpec paper (arXiv:2509.18344). Theoretical ceiling on offloaded layers, not end-to-end shipping.

Qwen VL CPU offload: When --enable-vlm, vision encoder (mmproj) is offloaded to CPU via --no-mmproj-offload. Reduces peak VRAM by 600–800 MB.

Two distinct mmproj flags — do not conflate. --no-mmproj disables multimodal projector loading entirely; --no-mmproj-offload loads the projector but offloads it to CPU. Combat Full uses neither: InternVL3-2B's InternViT encoder is bundled with the InternVL3 GGUF and loaded as part of the vision path (Ch. 8 §8.4). The opt-in Qwen2.5-VL-3B path uses --no-mmproj-offload.

YaRN gating: read GGUF rope_scaling; never double-apply. Conservative factor 2.0 for 64K. Combat Full uses native contexts (2K/4K/16K/8K) — no YaRN. Deep uses native 32K ceiling — no YaRN. If a future tier uses 64K, the double-scale check in Ch. 1 §2.7 step 2.5 prevents this.

VL path via mtmd: Qwen2.5-VL-3B loaded on demand; separate context. Scene understanding via sul-vlm uses the Rust-native backend (Ch. 8 §8.4), not mtmd. InternVL3-2B uses mtmd (InternViT-300M is bundled with InternVL3 GGUF).

Sampler → ring direct write: No String assembly.

Model load via FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN.

KV cache allocated via sul-alloc on 2 MB pages: (example: Combat Full Conversation 16K under q8_0 ~800 MB; under GAAC ~570 MB; under STAR-KV ~40–80 MB. Deep Q5 at 4K under q8_0 ~1.2 GB; under GAAC ~850 MB; under STAR-KV ~60–120 MB. See Ch. 1 §3.3 for the full per-profile table.) 1 GB pages reserved for tensor regions >1 GB.

Combat Full multi-profile contract. All profiles share one checkpoint and one llama_context. Instruct uses --reasoning-budget 0 and 2K context. Thinking uses a bounded positive budget (default: -1 unbounded; will be bounded to 512–1024 after the first A.63 measurement) and 4K context. Conversation uses 256 budget and 16K context. Coding uses 0 budget and 8K context. Profile flip is a runtime parameter change on the same context; target <50 ms. All profiles use the same speculation chain, same ReTrace compression, same OODA-Tool scaffold, same TSCG schemas, same sampling top-k and min-p; only temperature, top-p, and context/budget differ.

Medusa-1 head loader. medusa.rs loads PyTorch .pt head files, converts to Candle tensors, applies temperature scaling to speculative logits, builds the candidate tree, and constructs a llama_batch with the tree attention mask (feeding llama.cpp's existing batch-verify path, not forking llama.cpp). Constraint: shared-LM-head variant only; own-LM-head variant rejected by config validator (would be ~1 GB for 5 heads on 2B model with 151k vocab, defeating the general combat ceiling). Head VRAM ≤50 MB at Q4.

Phrase head loader. phrase_head.rs loads the ~3.4M-param MLP head, reads the frozen target's hidden state, predicts a one-to-three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary, maps back via greedy longest-match expansion. Output identical to greedy decoding up to FP tie-breaking. Head VRAM ~2–5 MB.

LiLiCorr rung. New rung recognized by speculative.rs (mainline in llama.cpp v0.7.0+, PR #30506). Improves on DFlash with joint candidate scoring across the draft block, no additional backbone VRAM. Expected acceptance 0.60 median / 0.75 p99; speedup 2.7× median / 3.2× p99.

RIFT draft cache compression (dormant). sul-spec-draft activates when draft cache >32 MB. Not active for Combat Full (Medusa/phrase read target hidden states, no separate draft cache) or Deep at 4K (ChainFlow draft cache ~10 MB). Activates at Deep 32K (~80 MB draft cache) or if a future tier grows an external drafter.

Tiered soft degradation: context reduction → KV precision → batch. STAR-KV quality failure → GAAC fallback (§10.11). Combat Full profile degradation (Thinking OOM → Instruct) is a router decision (§10.4), not a config-driven degradation.

Thread count: Combat 4 (all profiles); Deep 6.

ReTrace performance contract: §10.16.

CIG GPU scheduling: Enabled at sul-ai.exe init. Prevents CUDA submissions from collapsing the game's render loop. CIG contexts are not compatible with compute-only CUDA contexts — sul-ai-native FFI layer is CIG-aware. (Ch. 13 §13.5 covers the hardware side.)

Test requirements: Per-profile context loads correctly: VRAM within budget ±5%. Combat Full profile tests (per-profile): Instruct BFCL non-live ≥65 on SUL tool registry (target after fine-tuning; Hammer's historical ceiling was 81.42 non-live — see §10.1 and §10.6). Thinking BFCL non-live ≥65. Conversation turn quality ≥ threshold (TBD from A.63; expected mean rubric ≥75%). Coding HumanEval ≥60 (A.101). Router profile-selection accuracy ≥95% on 200 SUL-shaped turns. Router destructive-action detection recall = 100% on the router's destructive-action test set (100 scripted destructive triggers — any miss is a hard fail). Profile-switch latency <50 ms (flip --reasoning-budget and --ctx-size on the same llama_context). Instruct never emits thinking tokens (positive-negative-example test with 200 prompts, zero thinking-token leaks). Thinking never skips reasoning for complex calls (200-prompt test, scaffold always populates all four fields with reasoning traces). Conversation does not emit tool-call-shaped output for non-tool turns (200-prompt test). Coding does not emit conversational fluff (200-prompt test). Router deterministic given fixed inputs (proptest 1000 iterations, no nondeterministic classification). Router fallback (Thinking OOM → Instruct) fires correctly with scripted VRAM-spike workload; CombatRouterFallback telemetry event emitted. User override respected (manual profile = "instruct" honored unless destructive action detected; CombatProfileDenied emitted if safety invariant overrides). Medusa head tests: acceptance rate ≥0.55, head VRAM ≤50 MB at Q4, temperature scaling applied (acceptance drops ≥30% without it). Phrase head tests: acceptance rate ≥0.45, head VRAM ≤5 MB, byte-identical output to greedy decoding up to FP tie-breaking. LiLiCorr rung acceptance ≥0.60. UniSpec adapter acceptance ≥0.45. RIFT dormant check: not engaged for Combat Full or Deep at 4K; engaged for Deep at 32K. Deep Q5 multi-turn completion: Q5 is the quality-first default; test that Q5 quality beats Q4 by the expected margin on agentic eval. K2 tool-call parser: 100% format round-trip on all three supported formats. Speculative decode: benchmark-driven selection beats fixed default by >10%. Qwen VL CPU offload reduces peak VRAM by >600 MB. Symmetric KV keeps quality: perplexity delta <2% vs f16 on 1000-prompt eval. Asymmetric K/V rejected with E_KV_ASYMMETRIC_FA when FA is on. STAR-KV PPL delta <2% vs f16 on 1000-prompt eval; KL@D below measured f16 baseline. STAR-KV + FA compatible: FA still engages (fused kernel path traced). Speculation chain validator: all chains terminate in "none"; E_SPEC_CHAIN_UNTERMINATED fires if not. --spec-type validation: E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET fires at startup if any tier has a draft model loaded and no --spec-type. Medusa, phrase, UniSpec, LiLiCorr, ChainFlow acceptance benchmarks: each path measured and cached at startup; winner by effective decode tok/s. YaRN does not double-scale: test with a GGUF that has rope_scaling baked in; assert no --rope-scaling flag is passed. Miri clean for FFI boundary: llama_* calls no UB. ReTrace tests: preserved (saliency, dormant buffer, backtracking injection, retention, prefill speedup). sul-quant SPEED-Q 4-bit holds A.63 per-profile gates (Instruct BFCL ≥65, Thinking BFCL ≥65, Conversation quality ≥ threshold); SPEED-Q 2-bit holds within 2% absolute. APEX planner produces K-quant GGUF that runs on standard llama.cpp (no fork).

§10.18 Disk-backed Deep + CPU offload architecture
Contract: §10.9 (tiered KV cache) — authoritative. Gates: A.25/A.53 (STAR-KV on MBZUAI-IFM fork) — now obsolete; the fork was deleted after the b11454 mainline merge. Baselines: [kv_tier.*]. Boundary: Ch. 16 §16.1 (KV Boundary).

Deep Coder's 6.46 GB Q5_K_M weights (see §10.1) with 4K context and q8_0 KV total ~6.96 GB VRAM. When free VRAM is below this threshold, disk-backed mode activates:

Weights mmap via FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN. Keeps weights out of model process's resident set. Same discipline LlamaWeb (A.48) validates.

KV tier via sul-kv-tier (§10.9): hot VRAM / warm RAM / cold SSD.

Speculation via ChainFlow → LiLiCorr → UniSpec.

Batch and µ-batch reduced to -b 512 -ub 256 for disk-backed mode.

SubSpec (gated shipping component): quantized substitute draft from offloaded layers.

Why dense-model weight streaming is rejected: weights are read once at load. Disk-backed streaming adds latency for no benefit at SUL's model sizes. DirectStorage is for game asset loading, not LLM weights.

§10.19 Deep Q5/Q4 selector
After HAGS measurement and VRAM hygiene, diagnostics reports which Deep quant fits current free VRAM. With Q5_K_M at 4K + q8_0 KV, total is ~6.96 GB — fits under 8 GB with ~1 GB headroom. Recommendation: "Q5_K_M is the quality-first default at 8 GB; Q4_K_M is available for additional headroom; Q6_K does not fit (7.40 GB before KV)."

The JQ5_K variant (same 6.02 GiB size, 17.1% lower mean KLD, 19.9% lower 99% KLD, 8.4% lower RMS Δp, 0.35 pp higher top-1 agreement) is the preferred quantization if the fork PRs merge into mainline. Blocker: JQ types require PR #30716 (CPU + Metal) or #30717 (CPU + Metal + CUDA) to merge. Both are open. The moment either merges, sul-quant emits JQ5_K for K2-Horizon-7B. Until then, Q5_K_M is the shipping quantization. Do not vendor the fork — that reintroduces exactly the maintenance burden the mainline merge was supposed to remove.

§10.20 AI optimization presets (merged [ai.optimization] + [performance.deep] + [features.deep.*])
The Settings UI exposes a "Performance vs Quality" preset group. Every optimization the spec supports is selectable here, with the tuned configuration as the default. The presets override the underlying config sections ([ai.kv_tier], [ai.speculative], [ai.combat_full_*] weight_quant, [frame_gen], [audio.governor]) — they do not replace them.

Authority rule (three views of the same fields):

[ai.optimization] — the preset view. Resolves into the target config section. auto means "follow the target config section."

[performance.deep] — the tuning view. Individual optimization toggles for the Deep tier.

[features.deep.*] — the release-gate view. Which features are enabled in this release class.

Precedence: preset ([ai.optimization]) → target config section → per-game override. The [features.deep.*] view does not override behavior; it only gates whether the feature is present at all in the current release. A feature disabled in [features.deep.*] cannot be re-enabled via [ai.optimization] or [performance.deep] — the release gate wins.

Preset table:

Setting	Options	Default	Effect
offload_mode	auto, nkvo, none	auto	nkvo forces CPU KV offload (extreme VRAM saving, 10–20× latency penalty; formally A.6). none disables offload entirely (may OOM on some tiers). auto uses sul-kv-tier with STAR-KV/GAAC.
kv_method	auto, star_kv, gaac, palquant, puzzlekv, jolt, turbo3, tcq, uncompressed	auto	Forces a specific KV compression path. auto follows the A.18/A.97 gate outcome.
spec_chain	auto, medusa_first, phrase_first, unispec_first, ngram_only	auto	Overrides the per-tier speculation chain order. auto uses the tier chain from §10.1. Combat Full has one chain (all profiles share it), so this override affects Combat Full as a single unit, not per-profile.
pruning	off, 20pct_ffn	off	Enables 20% FFN pruning + RestoreLCC if its gate passes.
quant	auto, q4_k_m, q5_k_m, sul_quant	auto	Forces the decoder quantization. auto uses sul-quant SPEED-Q 4-bit for InternVL3-2B (once A.96 passes) and Q5_K_M for Deep.
frame_gen	off, auto, 2x, 3x, 4x	off	Enables frame generation with the selected multiplier. auto picks the highest multiplier the VRAM reservation and base-framerate gate will support. Backend is chosen by the governor (§9.2). Does not override per-game fg_unsafe flags.
audio_budget	latency_first, balanced, quality_first	balanced	Nudges the audio governor's buffer-size and filter-length decisions. latency_first = 256-sample buffer, shorter FIRs; balanced = 512-sample buffer, standard FIRs; quality_first = 1024-sample buffer, longest FIRs. The governor still enforces the WASAPI period.
Default = the tuned configuration. The user-facing preset group exists so users can trade latency for memory (or vice versa) without editing TOML. The default values are what the tuned rig uses after gate measurement.

Safety rails: offload_mode = "nkvo" during kernel_level: true gameplay is allowed (it is model-process-only, per Ch. 16 §16.1). pruning = "20pct_ffn" and quant = "sul_quant" are hidden when their respective gates have not passed on the current hardware. frame_gen refuses to activate on kernel_level: true titles and on fg_unsafe titles (unless the user explicitly overrides the fg_unsafe flag, which is a Tier 1 event). These are user-visible presets, not silent overrides. Combat Full profile override is a separate toggle under the same preset panel — not a preset row — and is a Tier 1 event per releases.md.

§10.21 Distillation pipeline (GAD + CADENCE — research)
Status: research queue only, not a shipping dependency. The distillation target is no longer a 3B Qwen coder (Coding Low cut). If distillation is attempted, it applies to whichever tier benefits, gated by the A.8 eval harness.

Training-time pipeline, not a runtime component. Runs on rented GPUs (Vast.ai / RunPod A100 40GB at ~$1.50/hr), not dispatch_ci.

Stage 1 — GAD (Generative Adversarial Distillation): Warm-up: One SeqKD epoch at learning rate 5×10⁻⁶. Joint training: Generator (student) and discriminator adapters updated jointly. Discriminator acts as on-policy reward model. Eval: LMSYS-Chat held-out set. Ship if GAD adapter matches or exceeds teacher+SeqKD baseline.

Stage 2 — CADENCE (Coverage-Adaptive On-Policy Distillation): DRIFT mechanism (per-token convex mixture of forward-KL and reverse-KL surrogate objectives on student-sampled trajectories); COVA (coverage-adaptive β schedule); FTB (forking-token boost concentrating gradient at high-entropy positions); CCD (dense reward adding numerical-proximity partial credit); LAP (brevity-preferential correct-rollout reinforcement); EMR (entropy-matching calibration regularizer); BSD (bootstrapped self-distillation phase). Eval: GSM8K and MATH-500. Target: 0.5B student → 69.8% GSM8K, 3B teacher → 72.1%.

Committed to crates/sul-lora/gad/ and crates/sul-lora/cadence/ with train.py, eval.py, package.sh. Upstream references: GAD (arXiv:2511.10643), CADENCE (arXiv:2607.16955).

Three-gate procedure: Gate 1 — A.8 eval harness exists and measures uncompressed baseline. Gate 2 — single GAD-only training run shows >3 points improvement on the harness. Gate 3 — CADENCE refinement adds >2 points beyond GAD. If any gate fails, do not proceed. ~$110 total compute across three gates.

    UserOverride,         // [ai.combat] profile or per-game combat.profile

    ToolVerification,     // prior tool call failed verification → Thinking

}

§10.24 Failure codes, AST guards, and model file tampering
AI-specific failure taxonomy
See SUL-LEDGER/failures.md §"AI" for the full table (KV-1 through KV-8, SP-1 through SP-14, MS-1 through MS-4, RT-1 through RT-4, MO-1 through MO-5, CP-1, QT-1 through QT-3, KC-1 through KC-2, SD-1 through SD-2, TP-1 through TP-3). The table content is authoritative there.

Mode F classification (Ch. 1 §3.4):

E_STAR_KV_QUALITY — Mode C (fall back to GAAC + decompression cache; session continues).

E_STAR_KV_DECOMPRESS — Mode C (fall back to GAAC).

E_STAR_KV_FALLBACK_EXHAUSTED — Mode E (persistent; refuse to load).

E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH — Mode D (quarantine).

E_STAR_KV_PAIR_MISMATCH — Mode D (quarantine).

E_GAAC_ROUND_TRIP — Mode E (persistent; fall back to uncompressed).

E_KV_COLD_READ_FAILED — Mode C (fall back to hot/warm).

E_KV_ASYMMETRIC_FA — Mode E (refuse to start; never silently degrade — silent quality degradation from asymmetric FA is worse than refusing to start).

E_RETRACE_UNAVAILABLE — Mode D (fall back to full-token baseline).

E_RETRACE_DORMANT_OVERFLOW — Mode C (drop oldest dormant tokens).

E_RETRACE_BACKTRACK_INJECTION — Mode C (fall back to full-token baseline for that pass; persistent → Mode E — disable ReTrace for session).

E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID — Mode E (persistent — Thinking-only failure degrades to Instruct-only with a warning; all-profile failure drops Combat Full entirely).

E_COMBAT_ROUTER_INIT_FAILED — Mode C (fixed profile fallback, router bypassed, warning chip).

E_DESTRUCTIVE_INSTRUCT_OVERRIDE — informational (no mode transition — logged as warning, not error).

E_DESTRUCTIVE_PROTECTION_DISABLED — informational (logged as warning).

E_QUANT_SPEED_Q_FAILED, E_QUANT_APEX_PLANNER_FAILED, E_QUANT_GGUF_NOT_K_QUANT — Mode C (fall back to llama.cpp Q4_K_S).

E_KV_COMPRESS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, E_KV_COMPRESS_IDENTITY_FAILED — Mode C (fall back to STAR-KV/GAAC).

E_RIFT_REFRESH_STALLED — Mode C (drop to RIFT-stat).

E_TOOLPRM_LOAD_FAILED, E_TOOLPRM_CACHE_THRASH — Mode C (fall back to no-PRM baseline).

E_MEDUSA_TEMP_SCALING_MISSING, E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT — config-error (Mode F at startup — abort startup with clear error).

E_COMBAT_PROFILE_AMBIGUOUS — Mode C (default to Instruct; log).

E_SPEC_TYPE_UNSET, E_SPEC_CHAIN_UNTERMINATED — config-error at startup.

Cascading escalation (Mode F): repeated E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE across sessions → Coder proposes repair diff. ReTrace or search pipeline cascade → Coder proposes repair diff. Persistent E_OODA_INCOMPLETE across sessions → Coder reviews prompt scaffold logic. Persistent E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED on specific schemas → Coder reviews TSCG compiler. Persistent E_QUANT_SPEED_Q_FAILED → Coder reviews the APEX planner or SPEED-Q wrap. Persistent E_KV_COMPRESS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE → Coder reviews the backend A.97 quality gates. Persistent E_TOOLPRM_CACHE_THRASH → Coder reviews the score-cache key design. Persistent E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT misconfiguration → Coder reviews the config (this should be caught at validator, not runtime — a Mode F here means a validator bypass). Repeated E_COMBAT_ROUTER_INIT_FAILED across sessions → Coder reviews router initialization and pre-created context allocation. Persistent instruct_fallback_rate_pct above tolerance → Coder reviews the router's fallback handling for Thinking OOM. Recurring E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID → Coder reviews VRAM reservation and context sizing for Combat Full's four profiles.

AST guards (AI-specific)
From SUL-LEDGER/guards.md (architectural invariants, multi-profile and quant/KV guards):

sul-agent::combat_profile must not import HTTP client.

sul-agent::combat_profile must not import wasapi.

The router's destructive_action_thinking config must be sourced only from [ai.combat] and per-game combat blocks (no ad-hoc path).

[ai.combat_full.thinking] context must be strictly greater than [ai.combat_full.instruct] context (AST check against config.toml).

[ai.combat_full.conversation] context must be strictly greater than [ai.combat_full.thinking] context.

[ai.speculative] must not contain combat_instruct_chain / combat_thinking_chain / combat_conversation_chain / combat_coding_chain keys (single combat_chain only).

Medusa temperature scaling must be enabled.

Medusa own-LM-head variant must not be present.

sul-quant must emit pure K-quant GGUF (no custom quant format — verified by checking general.file_type in the emitted GGUF against llama.cpp's K-quant types).

sul-kv-compress must not import wasapi.

sul-spec-draft must not import HTTP client.

sul-toolprm must not import wasapi.

sul-toolprm must not import ReadProcessMemory.

sul-ai-native ReTrace paths must not import ReadProcessMemory.

Model file tampering detection
Threat: attacker modifies a model file between sessions to inject malicious behavior.

Defense: SHA-256 verification against the signed manifest on every session start (not just first load). Modified model → immediate unload if loaded, Mode D quarantine lifecycle, user alert. Applies to every model in the ladder: InternVL3-2B, K2-Horizon-7B, MiniCPM-V, LFM2.5-VL, jina-vlm, Qwen2.5-VL, PP-OCRv5, Medusa/phrase/LiLiCorr/UniSpec drafters, STT models, TTS voices, vault auth models (RetinaFace/ArcFace/sherpa-onnx), Game Boy ROMs, and — from the handoff — CSI edge inference models, BCI decoding models, GEV geolocation models, VoiceStudio character voice models.

Mode-tagged LoRA tampering detection. jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora and jarvis_deep_tools.lora are special cases because they are the multi-profile design's load-bearing adapters. In addition to the standard SHA-256 verification against the signed manifest, sul-watchdog verifies:

The adapter's mode-tagged data hash matches the manifest entry. A tampered adapter that swaps in single-profile-only training data would break the multi-profile behavior silently (Combat Full Thinking might lose reasoning capability, or Instruct might emit thinking tokens, or Conversation might emit tool-call JSON). The mode-tagged data hash is a separate field from the adapter's binary hash — it records the exact training data configuration used to produce the adapter.

The adapter's per-profile BFCL and router accuracy gates pass against a small verification set (cached from the last A.63 run). If the adapter has been tampered with in a way that regresses one profile's capability without changing the binary hash (e.g., manifest tampering), the verification set catches it.

If either check fails, the adapter is quarantined (Mode D), Combat Full reverts to the last verified adapter, and the user is notified with the specific profile regression (Instruct BFCL drop, Thinking BFCL drop, Conversation quality drop, Coding HumanEval drop, or router accuracy drop).

ReTrace saliency layer definitions SHA-256 verified on every session start. The InternViT attention layers 6–12 used for saliency computation are part of the InternVL3-2B GGUF; their integrity is verified by the InternVL3-2B model hash. The ReTrace configuration (pivot set size, pruning threshold, injection layer selection logic) is part of the sul-ai-native binary and follows the standard binary signing chain. Dormant buffer format version is verified against the runtime. ReTrace is profile-agnostic — the same saliency computation, dormant buffer, and backtracking injection apply to all Combat Full profiles. Tampering detection does not need per-profile handling.

STAR-KV surgery version mismatch — E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH refuses to load without silently loading wrong-model. STAR-KV pair mismatch — E_STAR_KV_PAIR_MISMATCH refuses to load.

sul-quant integrity. The SPEED-Q submodule (pinned commit in vendor/speed-q/VERSIONS.toml) is part of the SUL binary release and follows the standard signing chain. The APEX planner is part of the SUL binary. Emitted GGUFs are pure K-quant files — no custom quant format — so their integrity is verified by the standard llama.cpp GGUF parser plus the model-file signing chain (same as any other model).

sul-kv-compress integrity. sul-kv-compress ships with the SUL binary. Backend crates (palquant, puzzlekv, jolt, turboquant, tcq) are workspace deps with pinned versions. No separate artifact. When the user switches backends (Tier 1 event), the config change goes through the standard config-signing path.

sul-spec-draft integrity. sul-spec-draft ships with the SUL binary. The unispec_adapter follows the unispec crate's release cadence. RIFT selection/refresh algorithm is part of the SUL binary. No separate artifact.

sul-toolprm integrity. The cross-encoder model file (sul_toolprm_enc_q4.gguf) follows the standard model-file signing chain. The training script (train.py) is part of the SUL repo, not shipped. A modified cross-encoder triggers Mode D quarantine and E_TOOLPRM_LOAD_FAILED; ToolPRM falls back to no-PRM baseline for the session.

Combat Full profile router integrity. The router code (sul-agent::combat_profile) is part of the SUL binary and follows the standard binary signing chain. The router's configuration ([ai.combat], [ai.combat_router], per-game combat blocks) is signed as part of config.toml and game_registry.json. The router has no separate artifact, model, or update path. Tampering with the router's config (e.g., silently setting destructive_action_always_thinking = false outside the Tier 1 approval flow) triggers a signature mismatch on config.toml and a Mode D quarantine lifecycle on the config file. The router's runtime behavior is tested at binary release; there is no post-release tampering vector beyond the config file.
