SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 13 — Hardware-Tailored Integration and Advanced Optimization.md
1. Purpose
Hardware-specific integration: NVMe/HDD storage tier discipline, DirectStorage pre-warm, binary asset bundling, thread priority discipline, one-click optimization scripts, CIG GPU scheduling, HAGS measurement, large-page allocation, and the size optimizations that keep the release binary lean. Where the AI pipeline touches the GPU (CIG scheduling, VRAM reservation), Ch. 10 references this chapter for the hardware side and holds the AI-policy side.

Reference rig note: hardware named in this chapter is the developer's reference (RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB, Ryzen 5 5600X, 64 GB DDR4, 970 EVO Plus NVMe). All code paths are driven by the runtime hardware profile (Ch. 11 §11.3).

Contract: §13.5 (CIG), §13.6 (one-click scripts), §13.7 (frontend code splitting), §13.8 (size optimization) — authoritative. Gates: A.51 (ZenDNN — research), A.48 (LlamaWeb — applied), A.43 (zstd_gpu — gated), A.49 (RidgeFill — gated). Baselines: [sustained] (§13.15). Boundary: Ch. 16 §16.15 (AST guards).

2. Architecture
2.1 Storage tier discipline
NVMe system drive core pipeline: binaries, SQLite metadata, config, model weights, high-priority active titles. The reference rig's 970 EVO Plus 500 GB NVMe holds the OS, the SUL binary, the model weights, and the active-game install (Helldivers 2 on the reference rig).

HDD asynchronous asset indexing: bulk game libraries via memmap2 + rayon. Bulk scans run at BELOW_NORMAL priority. Never blocks foreground reads. The reference rig's Seagate 2 TB HDD holds the secondary game library; scanning it does not impact SSD-backed foreground operations.

KV cache tier policy: sul-kv-tier (Ch. 10 §10.9) uses a three-tier cache: hot (VRAM), warm (RAM), cold (SSD). The cold tier lives on the NVMe. Disk-backed Deep mode (Ch. 10 §10.18) additionally uses FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN for weights. The HDD is never used for KV cache tiering — the latency is too high for the block-swap pattern (sul-kv-tier's ~5 ms cold-read budget assumes SSD).

Save shadow path: ReFS snapshots and sparse-copy snapshots live on the same drive as the save. VSS snapshots are always on the system drive. The %APPDATA%\\SUL\saves\ path is on the NVMe.

2.2 Embedded binary asset bundling
Purpose: core assets via include_bytes! for single-file portable execution.

The SUL binary (sul.exe) embeds: the default config template, the default persona.sulpack template, the WebView2 UI bundle (via Tauri's asset bundling), the default DSP artifact (small), the default voice model (if bundled), and the icon set. Large assets (models, extra voices, layer manifests) are not embedded — they live in %APPDATA%\\SUL\ and are downloaded/verified at first launch.

Single-file portable execution means the user can copy sul.exe to a machine, run it, and it works — no installer required for the base launcher. The %APPDATA%\\SUL\ directory is created on first run; optional downloads are user-initiated.

Size impact: include_bytes! adds the embedded assets to the binary. Tauri's asset bundling is already optimized for this (WebView2 handles the HTML/CSS/JS at runtime; the Tauri binary carries only the bundle metadata + the asset map). The icon set is a few hundred KB. The config template and persona template are a few KB.

2.3 Normal priority scheduling
Launcher core and egui overlay at NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS. Background AI inference at BELOW_NORMAL. Active game process never de-prioritized.

Thread priority discipline (across the whole system):

Thread	Priority	Rationale
Game process	(unchanged)	Never de-prioritized
sul.exe main thread (UI, egui overlay)	NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS	UI must respond
sul.exe IPC hub thread	NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS	IPC latency-critical
sul.exe supervised threads (sul-prosody, sul-governor)	BELOW_NORMAL	CPU-side, latency-tolerant
sul-ai.exe inference threads	BELOW_NORMAL	GPU-bound, not CPU-latency-critical
sul-audio audio callback	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Must never be preempted
sul-dsp / sul-voice / sul-voice-fx callbacks	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Part of sul-audio callback
sul-music.exe audio callback	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Separate process; must not be preempted
sul-music.exe decoder thread	ABOVE_NORMAL	Preload thread (bounded)
sul-broadcast.exe compositor thread	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Real-time compositing
sul-broadcast-audio audio callback	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Same discipline
sul-broadcast.exe encoder submission threads	ABOVE_NORMAL	Encode latency-sensitive
sul-broadcast.exe ISO muxer thread	BELOW_NORMAL	Disk-bound
sul-metrics rollup thread	BELOW_NORMAL	Background
sul-crash	(inherits panicking thread)	—
sul-stt whisper thread	Pinned per thread_affinity (Ch. 4 §4.4)	Away from game + audio
sul-csi / sul-bci real-time threads	THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL	Sensor-bound; latency-critical
sul-vision.exe inference	BELOW_NORMAL	Background
The AST guard (Ch. 16 §16.15) verifies that no sul-ai.exe thread runs above BELOW_NORMAL, and no sul-audio / sul-dsp / sul-voice / sul-music-engine / sul-broadcast-audio callback thread runs below THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL.

Why this matters: SUL runs alongside a game. If the launcher's UI thread is at NORMAL and inference is at NORMAL, the game's threads (typically ABOVE_NORMAL or higher) would be preempted by both. Moving inference to BELOW_NORMAL and keeping UI at NORMAL is the minimum-safe discipline. The audio callback at TIME_CRITICAL is the only SUL thread allowed above NORMAL — audio glitches are unacceptable, and the callback runs for <1 ms at a time.

2.4 CIG GPU scheduling and HAGS
§13.5.1 CIG GPU scheduling: Enabled to prevent CUDA submissions from collapsing the game's render loop (WDDM context switch — reference llama.cpp patch enables CIG without IGI). Windows 11 unified memory split recommendation exposed.

Configuration:

Setting	Value	Why
CIG mode	Enabled	Fine-grained load balancing between CUDA inference and game graphics
HAGS	Measured, not forced	Can help DWM VRAM but can hurt 8 GB cards; measure before enabling
VRAM reservation	Windows 11 unified memory split	New setting to reserve unified memory for graphics vs. AI; SUL recommends a split based on Combat Full's VRAM footprint (all profiles fit within the same reservation)
Priority	BELOW_NORMAL for inference	Active game process never de-prioritized
What CIG does: Compute Instance Grouping lets the GPU driver schedule CUDA work at fine-grained priority alongside D3D12 graphics work. Without CIG, every CUDA submission forces the driver to context-switch away from the D3D12 graphics queue and back, collapsing the game's render loop. With CIG, the CUDA work is interleaved with graphics work on the same GPU without full queue teardown.

CIG constraints (important):

CIG contexts are not compatible with compute-only CUDA contexts. Accessing CUDA pointers outside the CIG context can cause API errors.

The sul-ai-native FFI layer is CIG-aware — the llama.cpp CUDA backend is built with CIG support, and sul.exe does not create separate compute-only contexts.

The AST guard (Ch. 16 §16.15) verifies that sul.exe does not create compute-only CUDA contexts; the only CUDA context is the CIG-aware one.

Without CIG (fallback): If CIG is unavailable (older driver, unsupported GPU), sul-ai-native initializes without CIG. The render loop can be collapsed by CUDA submissions on affected systems; the game's frame time is more variable. sul-ai.exe logs a warning at init and the diagnostics check (§2.4) reports "CIG unavailable."

Hardware reference: Reference rig RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB supports CIG (the CIG-without-IGI patch is in mainline llama.cpp). Older GTX-series cards do not. AMD/Intel hardware does not use CIG (the concept is NVIDIA-specific); the equivalent on AMD is the Windows GPU scheduler's default behavior, and on Intel it is the driver's priority queue.

§13.5.2 HAGS measurement: HAGS (Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling) is a Windows 10 2004+ feature that lets the GPU manage its own VRAM and command queues instead of the OS. Its effect on SUL's VRAM budget is hardware-dependent:

On some systems (higher VRAM cards), HAGS reduces DWM's VRAM overhead by ~100–200 MB.

On 8 GB cards, HAGS can increase VRAM pressure because the driver holds more textures resident.

Decision: The reference rig is an 8 GB card. HAGS is measured, not forced. At startup (first run only), the diagnostics check (§2.4) toggles HAGS off → measures VRAM → toggles HAGS on → measures VRAM → reports the delta → leaves HAGS in whatever state it found it in. If the measured delta is negative (VRAM increased), it warns the user instead of offering one-click enable. If positive, it offers one-click enable. Requires reboot to toggle.

The [telemetry] hags_vram_delta_mb baseline (§2.10) captures this measurement.

Config: [gpu] hags_measured = true — runs the measurement. [features] hardware.hags_enabled = false — HAGS starts disabled by default; the user enables it after the measurement recommends it.

Config override: [gpu] hags_measured = true (default) — the measurement runs. [features] hardware.hags_measured = true (default) — the feature toggle that gates the measurement. [features] hardware.hags_enabled = false — HAGS is not forced on at startup; the user decides.

§13.5.3 VRAM reservation (Windows 11 unified memory split): Windows 11 exposes a "unified memory split" setting that reserves VRAM for graphics vs. AI workloads. SUL recommends a split based on Combat Full's VRAM footprint (all profiles fit within the same reservation; the difference between profiles is ~50–100 MB). The reference recommendation is to reserve the free VRAM envelope minus the game's peak usage minus Combat Full's worst-case profile (~1.45 GB with ReTrace).

Where this is surfaced: The Diagnostics → GPU panel (Ch. 1 §3.6) shows the current split and the recommendation. The user changes it via the Windows Settings app (SUL cannot change it programmatically — it is an OS setting). SUL's [gpu] config block records the user's intent but does not enforce it.

Config: [gpu] cig_enabled = true, [gpu] hags_measured = true. The unified-memory-split recommendation is derived, not configured.

2.5 One-click optimization scripts
Purpose: toggles for background telemetry suppression, Xbox Game Bar disabling, SysMain suppression, search indexer pausing, DWM visual effect reduction, high-performance power plan, standby memory cleaning, MMCSS game priority overrides, TCP/IP latency tweaks.

References in R.10: HotCakeX/Harden-Windows-Security, the1812/Malware-Patch, Sophia-Community/SophiApp. References in R.8: Raphire/Win11Debloat.

Each script is reversible — the script records the original state in %APPDATA%\\SUL\os-tuning\{script_name}.revert.json before changing anything, and a corresponding "Revert" button restores it. Reverting is important because a user who disables SysMain (for a game) may want it back after the game is uninstalled.

The scripts (each individually togglable via [features] diagnostics.os_tuning_scripts = true at the feature-toggle level, and via individual one-click buttons in Settings → Diagnostics → OS Tuning):

Script	What it does	Reference
Telemetry suppression	Disables Windows telemetry services (DiagTrack)	Harden-Windows-Security
Xbox Game Bar disable	Disables the Game Bar overlay + Game DVR background recording	SophiApp
SysMain suppression	Disables SysMain (SuperFetch) for the game's session	Malware-Patch
Search indexer pause	Pauses Windows Search indexing during gameplay	SophiApp
DWM visual effect reduction	Disables transparency, animations for the game session	SophiApp
High-performance power plan	Switches to the High-Performance plan	(native Windows)
Standby memory cleaning	Flushes standby memory list	Malware-Patch
MMCSS game priority override	Adjusts HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile\Tasks\Games	SophiApp
TCP/IP latency tweaks	Adjusts TcpAckFrequency and TCPNoDelay	(native Windows)
Safety: Every script that requires admin elevation prompts UAC. Every script that changes a service state warns first. Every script is reversible via the .revert.json mechanism. The AST guard verifies that no script changes a state it did not record.

Config: [features] diagnostics.os_tuning_scripts = true (default on, R1). [features] hardware.nvme_readahead = true (default on, R1) — the NVMe read-ahead tweak is part of this surface.

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_OS_TUNING_SCRIPT_FAILED	Script failed	Script returns non-zero (permissions, missing registry key)	Log; revert partial changes; user notified
E_OS_TUNING_REVERT_FAILED	Revert failed	Revert script cannot restore original state	Log; user notified; .revert.json retained for manual recovery
Release: R1.

2.6 DirectStorage pre-warm (gated shipping component)
Purpose: for games supporting DirectStorage, pre-warm assets via GPU-side decompression. Feature-flagged per game.

Note: DirectStorage is for game asset loading, not LLM weight streaming — see Ch. 10 §10.18 (dense-model weight streaming is rejected). The distinction matters: game assets are streamed repeatedly during gameplay (textures, meshes, audio) and benefit from GPU-side decompression because the decompressed data is used many times. Model weights are read once at load and then stay resident in VRAM; streaming them adds latency for no benefit.

References in R.7: Tsukisoft/direct-storage-rs, MarijnS95/direct-storage-rs, microsoft/DirectStorage.

Config: [features] hardware.direct_storage_prewarm = false (gated shipping component; enabled per game).

Gate: no specific A.x gate listed in the original spec; ships as part of the gated-shipping-components category (A.2) when DirectStorage support in the reference rig's games is confirmed.

Release: gated shipping component (A.2 category).

§13.5.4 Application-Wide Runtime & Build Performance Optimizations (D-143)

Zero-compromise runtime and build optimizations applied across all SUL binaries (`sul.exe`, `sul-ai-native.exe`, `sul-vision.exe`) without cutting features or violating the one-product / no-kernel invariants:

- **Global Allocator (`mimalloc`)**: All Rust binaries set `mimalloc` (`v2`, MIT) as `#[global_allocator]` with large-OS-page support when `[performance.runtime] large_page_allocation = true`. Eliminates Windows `HeapAlloc` lock contention across Tokio, Tauri IPC, SQLite, and ring buffers (20–40% lower multi-threaded allocation latency and reduced heap fragmentation toward the `<50 MB` idle RSS target).
- **Cache-Line-Padded Wait-Free SPSC Rings (`sul-wire`, `sul-ring`)**: Producer `head` and consumer `tail` atomics are padded to 64-byte cache lines (`#[repr(align(64))]` / `crossbeam_utils::CachePadded`) with `Acquire`/`Release` memory ordering (zero `SeqCst` on hot token-streaming or telemetry paths), eliminating false sharing between `sul-ai-native` / `sul-ocr` and `sul.exe` / `sul-overlay`.
- **Windows 11 EcoQoS Opt-Out & Hybrid Core Affinity**: Real-time threads (`sul-audio` WASAPI callback, `sul-broadcast` clock/muxer, `sul-overlay` DComp compositor) explicitly disable Windows 11 Efficiency Mode (`SetThreadInformation` with `ThreadPowerThrottling` `EXECUTION_SPEED` = 0) so backgrounded or game-focused states never throttle audio or frame pacing. Inference threads (`sul-ai-native`) remain at `BELOW_NORMAL` process priority and bind to P-cores on hybrid CPUs.
- **Unified SQLite Performance Profile**: `sul-metrics`, `sul-music`, and `sul-agent.memory` enforce `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL; PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY; PRAGMA mmap_size = 268435456; PRAGMA cache_size = -16384; PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;` with `prepare_cached` statements and 250 ms / 256-event batched commits in `sul-metrics`.
- **Async Overlapped `.sulpack` & Vault I/O + `blake3` / `zstd` Dicts**: `.sulpack` section reads and `sul-vault-core` STREAM chunks use `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED` + `PrefetchVirtualMemory` for cold-start pages, SIMD-accelerated `blake3` verification, and pre-trained `zstd` dictionaries for `<4 KB` JSON/TSCG/Entity Ledger payloads (2–3× better ratio and faster decode than raw zstd).
- **Parallel WebView2 Pre-Warm**: During Ch. 13 §2.8 three-stage boot, WebView2 environment creation (`--renderer-process-limit=1 --disable-features=msWebOOUI,msPdfOOUI`) runs concurrently with `sul-core` Step 1–2 trust/config checks rather than serializing behind them.
- **SIMD Target & Cargo Build Profiles**: `.cargo/config.toml` targets `target-cpu=x86-64-v3` (AVX2/FMA/BMI2, matching the Ryzen 5 5600X and Windows 10 1909+ baseline) for auto-vectorization in `sul-dsp`, `sul-ring`, `sul-ocr`, and `sul-wire`. `Cargo.toml` adds `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2` (fast dev iteration with optimized deps) and `[profile.release-ci]` (`lto = "thin"`) for fast PR gates while keeping `lto = "fat"` on shipping `release` / `release-small`.

§13.5.5 Ground-Up & Open-Source-Backed Performance Sweep (D-144)

Additional zero-compromise performance optimizations leveraging SUL's existing `Ch. 17` (`R.8` / `R.14`) open-source references and ground-up Rust/CUDA/Win32 primitives, without altering any feature behavior or licensing boundaries:

- **SIMD Vector Similarity (`simsimd`, `R.8`)**: `sul-agent.memory` (A.186), `.sulpack` vector recall, and `sul-toolprm` embedding scoring use `simsimd` (Apache-2.0) for AVX2/AVX-512 cosine and L2 distance on CPU, delivering 5–15× faster vector recall with 0 MB GPU VRAM cost.
- **Single-Pass DFA Prefiltering (`aho-corasick` + `memchr`, `R.8`)**: The destructive-action detector (`Ch. 10 §2.12`), `sul-net` citation/PII filter, and `sul-metrics` game-state extractor replace multi-pattern linear regex scans with a single-pass `aho-corasick` DFA + `memchr` prefilter, cutting per-frame/per-turn scan latency from ~1.5 ms to <100 µs.
- **Low-Overhead Synchronization (`parking_lot`, `R.8`)**: All non-async locks in `sul-core`, `sul-compat`, `sul-toggle`, and `sul-metrics` use `parking_lot::{Mutex, RwLock}` (1-byte uncontended fast path, zero OS handle allocation, no lock poisoning).
- **Double-Buffered `mmap` Frame Slot (`mmap-sync` / `shm-rings` pattern, `R.8`/`R.14`)**: `sul-vision.exe` (WGC capture → `sul-ocr` / `sul-vlm`) shares captured frames via a double-buffered `mmap` region instead of copying raw BGRA buffers over named pipes, eliminating frame-copy CPU overhead.
- **Pinned Host-Memory DMA Pool (`sul-ai-native`, `Ch. 10`/`Ch. 13`)**: Ground-up pre-allocated page-locked (`cudaHostAlloc`) staging ring for `sul-kv-tier` hot↔warm↔cold transfers and ReTrace dormant-buffer swaps, enabling async `cudaMemcpyAsync` overlapped with compute (~2× faster PCIe transfers without consuming VRAM).
- **Per-Turn / Per-Frame Arena Scratchpads**: `sul-agent` OODA packet assembly and `sul-dsp` / `sul-gb` scratch paths use pre-allocated, reset-on-boundary arenas so hot loops perform zero system heap allocations.

§13.5.6 Zero-Copy GPU Capture, Completion I/O, Exclusive Audio & Ground-Up Kernels (D-145, D-146)

Additional ground-up and open-source-backed upgrades locked in with full compatibility across SUL's one-product (`sul.exe`), zero-kernel-mode, and single-CIG-CUDA-context invariants:

- **Zero-Copy D3D11 → CUDA / NVENC Capture (`windows-capture` + `cudarc` / `NVIDIA/cuda-rust`)**: `sul-vision.exe` and `sul-broadcast.exe` (`A.42`, `A.127`) pair `NiiightmareXD/windows-capture` (WGC / DXGI) with `IDXGIResource::GetSharedHandle` and `cudaGraphicsD3D11RegisterImage` via `cudarc` and `NVIDIA/cuda-rust` (`Tensor::from_foreign`) so captured frames stay strictly in VRAM from game swapchain to NVENC, OCR, and VLM preprocessing (retaining the `D-144` double-buffered CPU `mmap` slot as the non-NVIDIA fallback). Shares the single CIG-aware CUDA context (`Ch. 13 §2.4`, `Ch. 16 §16.15`).
- **Completion-Based Async I/O (`compio-rs/compio`)**: `.sulpack` streaming, save-shadow sparse copies, and bulk HDD/NVMe library scans use `compio` (native Windows IOCP completion-based I/O) to eliminate `tokio::fs` blocking-pool dispatch overhead and extra buffer copies, while `tokio` remains on the control-plane/IPC runtime.
- **Pure Zero-Copy IPC (`rkyv` over `sul-wire`)**: Resolves `A.22` / `A.22b` by standardizing `sul-wire` shared-memory ring payloads on `rkyv` (`bytecheck`-validated archived structs) for Entity Ledger updates, OODA tool packets, and telemetry rollups.
- **PagedAttention + Copy-on-Write Prefix Caching (`mistral.rs` pattern)**: `sul-kv-tier` / `sul-ai-native` (`A.4`, `A.19b`) partition KV memory into fixed blocks with copy-on-write prefix sharing so Combat Full's system prompt, persona, and Entity Ledger prefix stay pinned across rapid profile switches with zero re-prefill.
- **Bit-Perfect Exclusive WASAPI + SIMD Resampling (`wasapi-rs` + `rubato`)**: `sul-audio` and `sul-music.exe` (`A.119`–`A.122`) use `HEnquist/wasapi-rs` (event-driven WASAPI exclusive mode) paired with `HEnquist/rubato` (SIMD polyphase resampling) to bypass the Windows APO mixer and hold callback jitter <1 ms.
- **Ground-Up Rust/CUDA Kernels (`NVIDIA/cuda-rust` / `cutile-rs`)**: `sul-vision` image resize/normalize/crop preprocessing, `A.105` fused STAR-KV dequant-and-attend, and `A.43` `zstd_gpu` decompression are implemented in stable Rust via `cutile-rs` inside the single CIG-aware CUDA context, eliminating C++ `.cu` FFI glue.
- **Transactional Embedded KV & VFS Journal (`redb`)**: `cberner/redb` (pure-Rust ACID zero-copy B-tree) backs the `A.41` VFS writeback journal, `A.40` atomic `.sulpack` delta migration state, and `A.58` / `A.58b` `blake3`-keyed search verification cache.
- **Ultra-Low-Latency Compression (`lz4_flex`) & Fast Tokenization (`kitoken`)**: `PSeitz/lz4_flex` (`>= 0.13.0` with `safe-decode` enabled, mitigating `CVE-2026-32829`) handles sub-millisecond `sul-kv-tier` warm-RAM swap and screenshot ring compression (`zstd` + dicts remain for `.sulpack`/cold storage), while `Systemcluster/kitoken` provides local Rust BPE/Unigram/WordPiece token counting and prompt budgeting without IPC round-trips.
- **Clean-Room Frame-Gen Post-Process FX DAG (`A.182`) & Hybrid Agent Memory (`A.186`)**: A `wgpu`/SPIR-V compute DAG performs CAS sharpening and tone mapping after optical-flow synthesis (no `Lossless.dll` dependency), and `sul-agent.memory` pairs SQLite `FTS5` lexical recall with `simsimd` AVX2 cosine re-ranking at 0 MB VRAM cost.

§13.5.7 Handoff Rectification, Core-Pinned Epoch Reclamation, CFG & Windows SHM Alignment (D-147)

Applies the verified runtime, security, and build-validation items from the master handoff while rectifying Linux/ungrounded claims to match SUL's Windows 11 (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and RTX 3060 Ti (Ampere SM 8.6) baseline:

- **Core-Pinned Concurrency & Epoch Reclamation (`core_affinity` + `crossbeam-epoch`)**: Critical runtime threads (audio, overlay, `sul-wire` ring pump) pin to isolated physical cores on the AMD 5600X via `core_affinity = "0.8.3"` (crates.io package name, not `core_affinity_rs`) paired with `crossbeam-epoch = "0.9.21"` and lock-free SPSC/SPMC ring buffers (`sul-ring` / `sul-wire`).
- **Windows Shared-Memory IPC & Capability Gates**: Fixed-bucket shared-memory IPC uses Win32 `CreateFileMappingW` / `MapViewOfFile` (`FILE_MAP_READ` / `SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES`) rather than POSIX `fcntl` FD seals, paired with Tauri 2 compile-time capability grants and `rkyv` `bytecheck` validation gates (`Ch. 7`).
- **Windows Control Flow Guard (`-C control-flow-guard`)**: Replaces Linux/nightly `-Z sanitizer=cfi` with native MSVC Control Flow Guard in `.cargo/config.toml` alongside FatLTO and `cargo-pgo` (`Ch. 13 §2.15`).
- **Completion I/O (`compio` Windows IOCP)**: Drops the Linux-only `io-uring` feature from workspace `Cargo.toml` so `compio` targets Windows IOCP cleanly.
- **Ampere Attention & Real SUL Subsystems Preserved**: On RTX 3060 Ti (Ampere SM 8.6), CUDA attention uses **FlashAttention-2** (gating FlashAttention-3 strictly to Hopper SM 9.0+ per `Dao-AILab/flash-attention`). Combat Full remains the single `Q4_K_S` checkpoint (`Ch. 10 §2.1`, ~1.05 GB weights / ~1.30–1.35 GB with ReTrace — not BitNet b1.58), `.sulpack` remains SUL's signed data-pack format (`Ch. 11` — not CoW game-asset mod overrides or `.susc`/Cranelift JIT), `sul-vault-core` remains XChaCha20-Poly1305 + TPM + DPAPI (`Ch. 02` — not VBS enclaves), and Tier 1 remains the 21 OS-level approval modal events (`releases.md`).
- **`xtask` R0 Build Order Validator Rules**: `xtask` enforces Rust Edition 2024 / MSRV 1.85, zero-`electron` / zero-`io-uring` manifest guards, crate layer boundaries (`sul-ipc-types`, `sul-wire`, `sul-ring`), feature-flag orthogonality, and release asset/schema parity (`§13.5.7`, `CLAUDE.md`).

§13.5.8 Whole-Chart Module & Feature Performance Optimization Sweep (D-148)

Applies zero-cut, module-by-module runtime and memory optimizations across every chapter (`Ch. 01`–`Ch. 16`) using verified MIT/Apache-2.0 crates and Windows-native primitives:

- **Ch. 01 / Ch. 12 (`sul-core`, `sul-toggle`, `sul-metrics`)**: `arc-swap` (`1.9.5`) provides wait-free config/feature-flag hot-reload with zero `RwLock` read contention; `rustc-hash` (`2.1.3`, `FxHashMap`) replaces SipHash on internal ID/metric/game-registry maps; `smallvec` (`1.16.5`) and `bumpalo` (`3.20.3`) eliminate short-lived heap allocations on per-turn and per-frame hot paths.
- **Ch. 02 (`sul-vault-core`, `sul-auth-app`)**: Chunked `64 KB` cache-aligned `XChaCha20-Poly1305` STREAM encryption/decryption paired with `PrefetchVirtualMemory` for vault index warm-up and non-blocking Win32 modal handoff.
- **Ch. 03 (`sul-vfs`, `sul-unpack`, `steam-library-parsing`)**: `compio` IOCP parallel directory scans, `memchr` + `aho-corasick` single-pass VDF/ACF parsing, and `redb` group-committed writeback transactions (`100 ms` / `64`-entry batching).
- **Ch. 04 (`sul-audio`, `sul-voice-auth`)**: Pre-allocated lock-free `sul-ring` PCM buffers with zero heap allocation inside the `wasapi-rs` event-driven exclusive callback, pinned to an isolated AMD 5600X core via `core_affinity`, and `rubato` SIMD polyphase resampling.
- **Ch. 05 / Ch. 06 (`sul-overlay`, `sul-broadcast`)**: External DirectComposition (`DComp`) dirty-rect damage tracking to skip compositing unchanged overlay regions, paired with `windows-capture` D3D11 shared-handle -> CUDA/NVENC zero-copy VRAM capture (`D-145`).
- **Ch. 07 (`sul-ipc`, `sul-wire`, `sul-ring`)**: `rkyv` `bytecheck` zero-copy framing over `CachePadded<AtomicU64>` SPSC rings, `crossbeam-epoch` snapshot reclamation, and Win32 `CreateFileMappingW` section alignment.
- **Ch. 08 / Ch. 09 (`sul-net`, `sul-agent`, `sul-vision`)**: `blake3`-keyed `redb` search cache, SQLite `FTS5` + `simsimd` AVX2 cosine hybrid memory (`0 MB` VRAM), and `cutile-rs` GPU image preprocessing kernels.
- **Ch. 10 / Ch. 13 (`sul-ai-native`, `sul-kv-tier`, `ReTrace`, `STAR-KV`)**: FlashAttention-2 on Ampere SM 8.6, `mistral.rs`-pattern PagedAttention CoW prefix caching, `lz4_flex` (`safe-decode`) warm-RAM KV swap, `cudaHostAlloc` async DMA staging ring, and `kitoken` local prompt budgeting.
- **Ch. 11 / Ch. 14 / Ch. 15 / Ch. 16 (`sulpack`, `sul-music`, `sul-health`, `sul-compat`)**: `memmap2` + `zstd` trained dictionaries + Rayon `blake3` merkle verification, bit-perfect `wasapi-rs` + `rubato` audio, SQLite WAL batched commits, and `cargo-pgo` + FatLTO + `/OPT:REF,ICF` + `-C control-flow-guard`.



2.7 Release-profile size optimization
[profile.release-small] with opt-level = "s", lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1, panic = "abort", strip = true — 20–30% binary size reduction for portable sul.exe.

Size impact per component:

sul-wire's ring view adds ~120 KB to the binary.

sul-fg's layer adds ~80 KB.

The vault and auth crates add ~2.5 MB (ring + AES primitives + DPAPI/TPM bindings + face/voice auth embedding stores).

All acceptable for the shipping binary. The portable build target is <50 MB idle RAM excluding WebView2, egui, and model weights (Ch. 1 §2.1).

Profiles (from Cargo.toml):

toml
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "unwind"
strip = false
debug = 1

[profile.release-small]
inherits = "release"
opt-level = "s"
panic = "abort"
strip = true
debug = 0

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug = 1
Which profile is used where:

Shipping binary: release (with the option to build release-small for the portable variant).

Benchmarks: bench.

Development: dev.

PGO: release with PGO profile data (see Ch. 1 §10).

2.8 Frontend code splitting
React.lazy + Suspense, Vite manualChunks. tauri.conf.json "removeUnusedCommands": true strips dead IPC surface. vite-plugin-imagemin for asset compression.

Expected: ~500 ms faster initial render and smaller bundle.

Token-streaming path no longer goes through React reconciliation on every token — sul-wire writes to a plain ArrayBuffer that the token display component reads via requestAnimationFrame. ~2 ms per-frame reduction during streaming, on top of the Tauri IPC bypass (Ch. 7 §2.5).

Three-stage boot: Shell (native Tauri window) → Core (IPC + trust + config) → Full Interactive (React hydration, pack load, AI warm-up). Eliminates the white screen during startup.

Config: tauri.conf.json app > windows and bundle sections configure this; no config.toml field.

2.9 Hardware-related measurement and reference entries
LlamaWeb memory-footprint reference (A.48): LlamaWeb (arXiv 2026) achieves 29–33% less memory and 45–69% higher decode throughput than other browser LLM frameworks. The architecture pattern (shared-weight WASM instances) is not directly applicable to native Rust, but the memory-mapping discipline — keep weights out of the model process's resident set and mmap them from disk — is the same discipline sul-ai-native already uses (FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN). No action needed; pattern already applied. Added to References (R.4).

RidgeFill TTFT pattern (A.49): RidgeFill (arXiv, Nov 2026) achieves 1.25–1.31× faster TTFT at 16K–120K tokens via training-free late-layer cache fill. Not applicable at base release because Deep's context is 4K–8K; becomes applicable when Deep's context grows past 32K or when 64K-tier research is revived. Gate: "if RidgeFill reduces Deep cold TTFT by >20% at 32K, integrate into sul-ai-native."

Vec-LUT edge-kernel (already in llama.cpp): Vec-LUT is a table-lookup-based kernel for 4-bit quantized inference, integrated into llama.cpp and measured at up to 4.2× faster than SOTA baselines on edge devices. No action needed — sul-ai-native's mainline pin to b12207+ includes it. Note in Ch. 10 §10.25 that 4-bit GGUFs benefit automatically.

ZenDNN on AMD CPUs (A.51): ZenDNN achieves up to 4.5× prompt processing speedup for llama.cpp on AMD EPYC CPUs. Not applicable to reference rig (Ryzen 5 5600X is Zen 3, but ZenDNN's largest gains are on EPYC server CPUs). Added to gates.md A.51 as future-gate for AMD-CPU users on Linux, not the reference rig. No action in the shipping release.

Frame generation GPU interaction (Ch. 9 §2.2): Frame generation adds GPU work (optical flow + synthesis) that competes with both the game and the AI tier for GPU resources. On the reference rig (RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB), FG at 2× typically consumes 5–10% additional GPU utilization at 1080p, rising to 15–20% at 1440p. The governor (Ch. 9 §2.1) accounts for this in VRAM reservation but does not account for GPU utilization; the user-facing preset group (Ch. 9 §2.3) surfaces a warning if [frame_gen] enabled = true is combined with an already-saturated GPU. CIG scheduling (§2.4) helps mitigate the contention but does not eliminate it.

Frame generation + audio governor interaction (Ch. 9 §2.2): FG raises GPU utilization, which can raise DPC latency, which can starve the WASAPI callback. The audio governor (Ch. 4 §4.10) monitors WASAPI callback jitter; if jitter p99 exceeds 2× the pre-FG baseline, it recommends reducing the FG multiplier by one step (AudioUnderrunRiskFromFg event). This is a recommendation, not an auto-disable.

Frame generation + Combat Full interaction (Ch. 9 §2.2): FG's VRAM reservation and Combat Full's ~1.3–1.45 GB must coexist within the free VRAM envelope. On 8 GB (reference rig), ED with FG at 2× (~300 MB reserved) leaves ~6 GB for the game + Combat Full + OCR + Deep if co-resident. HD2 with kernel-level AC blocks FG entirely — no contention to compute. On ED, the governor accounts for Combat Full's VRAM footprint in the reservation calculation but does not account for the router's choice of profile (all four Combat Full profiles have nearly identical VRAM; the difference is ~50–150 MB across profiles, below the reservation granularity). No special case needed.

2.10 Hardware-tailored performance contract (sustained)
Sustained benchmark: xtask bench-sustained runs 10-minute continuous inference, measures tok/s at end (catches thermal throttling). Run 10× to populate p99 for entries like [ai.deep] tok_per_sec.

Baselines ([sustained] section from baselines.md, status per Ch. 1 §8):

[sustained] deep_q4_tok_per_sec_after_10min = { median = 30, p99 = 25, higher_is_better = true, status = "target" }

[sustained] deep_q5_tok_per_sec_after_10min = { median = 25, p99 = 20, higher_is_better = true, status = "target" }

What sustained benchmarking catches: thermal throttling on the reference rig. The RTX 3060 Ti's boost clock drops as the GPU heats up; the sustained benchmark catches when the tok/s drops below the p99 target. If the p99 is below the target, the governor recommends lowering the Deep tier to Q4_K_M (Ch. 10 §10.19), reducing the VRAM reservation (Ch. 9 §2.1), or dropping FG to 2× (if FG was 3× or 4×). The recommendation is surfaced in Diagnostics (Ch. 1 §3.6).

Sustained benchmark consumers: [sustained] baselines feed the Deep quant selector (Ch. 10 §10.19), the FG multiplier selector (Ch. 9 §2.1), and the presets in Ch. 10 §10.20.

Config semantics:

[gpu] cig_enabled = true — enables CIG (see §2.4). If unsupported, logs a warning and continues with default scheduling.

[gpu] hags_measured = true — HAGS measurement runs at first launch (§2.4).

[features] hardware.direct_storage_prewarm = false — per-game gated shipping component.

[features] hardware.cig_scheduling = true — CIG feature toggle (mirrors [gpu] cig_enabled).

[features] hardware.hags_enabled = false — HAGS starts disabled; the user enables it after measurement.

[features] hardware.nvme_readahead = true — NVMe read-ahead tuning runs at first launch.

[performance.runtime] — runtime optimization toggles; all default true (per the performance-presets philosophy in Ch. 1 §2.5). The hags_enabled = false default is a safety choice (HAGS on 8 GB cards can hurt VRAM), not a performance choice.

2.12 Large-page allocation
Purpose: KV cache allocated via sul-alloc on 2 MB pages. 1 GB pages reserved for tensor regions >1 GB.

Why this matters: The Windows memory manager uses 4 KB pages by default. For a multi-gigabyte KV cache, the TLB (translation lookaside buffer) would thrash — every access requires a page-table walk. 2 MB pages reduce TLB pressure by ~512× (one TLB entry covers 512× more memory). 1 GB pages reduce it further, but only for very large regions.

Which regions get 2 MB pages: The KV cache for every tier. The model weights for Combat Full and Deep. The sul-ring memory-mapped ring (Ch. 7 §2.3).

Which regions get 1 GB pages: Only the Deep model weights (6.46 GB Q5_K_M) when the region exceeds 1 GB. The reference rig's RTX 3060 Ti supports 1 GB pages; older cards and most AMD/Intel cards do not.

Allocator: sul-alloc is the custom allocator crate that wraps VirtualAlloc with MEM_LARGE_PAGES and MEM_COMMIT | MEM_RESERVE. The allocator is used by sul-ai-native (for KV cache and weights), sul-ring (for the ring), and sul-kv-tier (for hot-tier KV pages). The AST guard verifies that no other crate allocates large pages directly.

Config: [performance.runtime] large_page_allocation = true (default on).

Failure taxonomy:

Code	Category	Trigger	Recovery
E_ALLOC_LARGE_PAGE_UNAVAILABLE	Large page unavailable	VirtualAlloc fails with large-page flag	Fall back to 4 KB pages; log; continue (Mode C)
E_ALLOC_OUT_OF_MEMORY	Out of memory	Allocation fails	Refuse to load tier; user notified
Test requirements: Large-page allocation succeeds for the KV cache on the reference rig; fallback to 4 KB pages works when large pages are unavailable; TLB pressure reduction is measurable via perf counters (optional).

2.13 Persistent CUDA streams and batch tuning
Persistent CUDA streams: Created at init, reused across llama_decode. ~200–500 µs per inference saved (per-inference stream creation cost).

Batch tuning: -b 1024 -ub 512 at 8 GB (was 2048/512 in v6.8 — tighter batch saves ~50–100 MB per tier with no measurable throughput cost). At 4 GB, -b 512 -ub 256. Disk-backed mode uses -b 512 -ub 256 (Ch. 10 §10.18).

Zero-copy model loading: FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING | FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN for weight files. Keeps weights out of the model process's resident set, so the OS page cache does not compete with the KV cache for RAM.

Cold/warm model loading: Combat Full is loaded at startup (cold). Deep is loaded on demand when a coding task is detected (warm). Profile switches (Instruct ↔ Thinking ↔ Conversation ↔ Coding) are runtime parameter changes, not model reloads (Ch. 10 §10.12).

Context checkpoints: When switching from Combat Full to Deep and back, the context is preserved. The context_checkpoints optimization (default on) snapshots the KV state at checkpoint boundaries so the switch does not re-process the prompt.

Per-language profiles: Deep's LoRA adapters are merged per language (Rust/Python/TypeScript/shell/general; Ch. 10 §10.26 A.111). The router selects the profile per task.

All of these are under [performance.runtime] and default on (per §2.11).

xtask bench-sustained (from Ch. 1 §10 and this section): bench_sustained.py::deep_q4 — Deep Q4 10-min sustained throughput. Produces [sustained] deep_q4_tok_per_sec_after_10min. bench_sustained.py::deep_q5 — Deep Q5 10-min sustained throughput. Produces [sustained] deep_q5_tok_per_sec_after_10min.

xtask bench-telemetry (from Ch. 12 §2.10): bench_telemetry.py::hags_vram_delta — HAGS VRAM delta measurement. Produces [telemetry] hags_vram_delta_mb. bench_telemetry.py::game_state — Game-state machine latency. Produces [telemetry] game_state_machine_us. bench_telemetry.py::screenshot_ring — Screenshot ring allocation. Produces [telemetry] screenshot_ring_alloc_mb.

xtask bench_ai (from Ch. 10 §10.23): bench_ai.py::deep_q4_vram_measure — Measured VRAM at 4K context. Produces [ai.deep_q4] vram_4k_gb. bench_ai.py::deep_q5_vram_measure — Measured VRAM at 4K context. Produces [ai.deep_q5] vram_4k_gb. bench_transitions.py::deep_quant_swap — Q4→Q5 swap latency. Produces [ai.transitions] deep_q4_q5_swap_ms.

PGO training: xtask pgo train runs a scripted session (launch → load Combat Full → 10 inferences → open overlay → 10 s capture → close). The PGO profile data is then used for the shipping build. See Ch. 1 §10.

BOLT (Linux ELF reference only; skipped on Windows PE per `D-145`): LLVM BOLT currently supports Linux ELF binaries only (`llvm/llvm-project#72205`); on Windows PE (`sul.exe`), `xtask pgo` uses `Kobzol/cargo-pgo` + FatLTO + `/OPT:REF,ICF` without a Linux-only post-link step.

Reference-rig specific build flags: -C target-cpu=native for reference-rig binaries (Ch. 1 §10). This is not used for the shipping binary — the shipping binary is compiled for a generic CPU and does runtime CPU-feature detection (AVX2 dispatch, AVX-512 dispatch). The reference-rig binary is used for benchmarks and for the CI regression suite.

2.16 Hardware threat model
Threat: A hardware-specific attack (e.g., a compromised driver, a malicious firmware update, a hardware flaw) subverts SUL's VRAM reservation or CIG isolation.

Defense: SUL does not run kernel-mode code (Ch. 16 §16.5). Driver-level compromise is outside SUL's threat model — SUL treats the OS and drivers as trusted. If a driver is compromised, every application on the machine is compromised, not just SUL; the response is OS-level (Windows Update, driver rollback, reinstall). SUL's contribution to defense-in-depth is that it does not add a kernel-mode attack surface (no virtual audio driver, no anti-cheat bypass, no kernel-mode EDR). The sul-watchdog process monitoring (§2.8) detects some driver-level tampering in SUL's own address space but not at the driver level.

Threat: A malicious process tries to read SUL's VRAM (e.g., through a compromised driver or a GPU-side attack).

Defense: VRAM is not directly readable from another process without kernel-level access. SUL's VRAM contains model weights (public), KV cache (contains user prompts and game state), and compositor buffers (the game screen — already visible to the game itself). The KV cache is the sensitive part. Windows' GPU scheduler isolates VRAM per-process at the OS level; a malicious process needs a compromised driver or kernel access to read another process's VRAM. SUL's defense is that it does not add a kernel-mode attack surface, so it does not become the driver-level compromise vector.

Threat: A hardware-specific side channel (e.g., Meltdown-class, Spectre-class, or GPU-side channel) leaks KV cache or model weights.

Defense: SUL treats hardware side channels as an OS/microcode responsibility (Windows patches, CPU microcode, GPU firmware). The vault's key material is in DPAPI + TPM; the KV cache is in VRAM. A side channel that can read VRAM at scale is a hardware vulnerability, not a SUL vulnerability; the mitigation is hardware/OS-level. SUL's contribution is that it does not cache sensitive data longer than necessary — the vault is locked when idle, and the KV cache is ephemeral (cleared on session end).

Threat: A hardware failure (VRAM corruption, SSD failure) corrupts a model file or a save.

Defense: Model files are SHA-256 verified on every session start (Ch. 10 §10.24). Save shadows (§2.5) provide a rollback if a save is corrupted. The vault (Ch. 2 §2.10) has its own integrity check + Ed25519 signatures. SQLite WAL mode + hourly backups (§2.1) protect the telemetry and library databases.

2.17 Hardware AST guards
Enforced by cargo xtask ac-regression on every PR:

sul-ai.exe does not create compute-only CUDA contexts (CIG-aware only).

No thread above BELOW_NORMAL in sul-ai.exe.

No thread below THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL in sul-audio / sul-dsp / sul-voice / sul-music-engine / sul-broadcast-audio callbacks.

Large-page allocation only via sul-alloc (no direct VirtualAlloc with large-page flag outside sul-alloc).

sul-watchdog runs at BELOW_NORMAL; never blocks the game or the audio callback.

HAGS is measured, not forced (the AST guard verifies that hags_enabled is not set to true without a recorded measurement).

CIG is enabled unless a warning was logged (the AST guard verifies that cig_enabled = true is the shipped default and that the warning path exists).

2.18 Cross-references
Reference rig (§2.1 and Ch. 1 §10); storage tier discipline (§2.1); embedded binary asset bundling (§2.2); normal priority scheduling (§2.3); CIG GPU scheduling (§2.4 and Ch. 10 §10.25 AI side); HAGS measurement (§2.4 and Ch. 12 §2.4); VRAM reservation (§2.4); one-click optimization scripts (§2.5); DirectStorage pre-warm (§2.6); release-profile size optimization (§2.7); frontend code splitting (§2.8); LlamaWeb memory pattern (§2.9 and A.48); RidgeFill TTFT pattern (§2.9 and A.49); Vec-LUT edge-kernel (§2.9 and Ch. 10 §10.25); ZenDNN (§2.9 and A.51); frame generation GPU interaction (§2.9 and Ch. 9 §2.2); sustained benchmark (§2.10 and Ch. 1 §10); config (§2.11); large-page allocation (§2.12); persistent CUDA streams and batch tuning (§2.13); baselines (§2.14); benchmarks (§2.15); threat model (§2.16); AST guards (§2.17); PGO + BOLT (§2.15 and Ch. 1 §10); CIG AI-side policy (§2.4 and Ch. 10 §10.25); KV tier SSD policy (Ch. 10 §10.9); disk-backed Deep mode (Ch. 10 §10.18); HAGS VRAM delta diagnostic (Ch. 12 §2.4); Deep quant selector (Ch. 10 §10.19); presets (Ch. 10 §10.20); performance toggles (Ch. 1 §2.5); AST guards base list (Ch. 16 §16.15); driver/hardware threat model (Ch. 16 §16.7); sul-alloc large-page allocation (§2.12); sul-watchdog (Ch. 12 §2.8); sul-kv-tier cold-tier read budget (Ch. 10 §10.9).

SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 14 — Autonomous Hive-Mind and Safety Protocol.md
1. Purpose
The Coder AI's operating envelope, the dual-gate safety protocol that constrains it, the hive-mind compatibility registry, the auto-updater, the SOTA self-improvement pipeline, the self-healing watchdog's recovery modes (A–F), the real-time integrity watchdog, the threat quarantine, the hive-mind threat logging, the model and artifact tampering detection, and the safety invariants and structural refusals that every other subsystem depends on. This chapter is the safety substrate.

2. Architecture
2.1 Tier 1 events — classification principle
The full Tier 1 event list per release class is maintained in SUL-LEDGER/releases.md (Ch. 1 §2.4). This section holds only the classification principle.

Classification principle (from Ch. 1 §2.4): A setting is Tier 1-core if it disables a safety invariant, weakens authentication, weakens WebView hardening, or attempts a structural refusal. The 21 Tier 1-core events are the tier1_events array in R0 of releases.md. Everything else is Tier 1 by release class: R1-scoped model-ladder and vision-config changes, search backend, audio routing, voice FX, STT, emulation, music-player, broadcast settings; R2-scoped frame-generation, quantization, KV-compress, spec-draft, audio governor, optimize settings; R3-scoped sensing, security, uncensored-models, VoiceStudio settings.

Enforcement: Every Tier 1 event fires an OS-level approval modal (native Win32, outside LLM context, prompt-injection-proof).

Agent memory, custom entities, and user tasks (gated extensions):
- `[agent.memory]` (R2, A.186): claude-mem-inspired SQLite FTS5 + `sulpack` vector recall (<50 ms) with address pointers.
- `[agent.entity_ledger.custom_types]` (R2, A.187): Twenty-inspired JSON Schema custom entity types stored in `sulpack` (<10% size growth).
- `[agent.user_tasks]` (R1, A.188): Taskee-inspired local SQLite task table (<5 ms write) with Vault-AEAD-encrypted notes. The modal is not dismissible by any config edit, any script, or any LLM action; the user must explicitly approve. The modal's record is stored in %APPDATA%\\SUL\tier1-approvals.json (Ed25519-signed, DPAPI-wrapped) and referenced by the Coder's Gate A verification (§14.3) and by the auto-updater's Tier 1 checks (§14.5).

A note on terminology. The original spec's "§12.1 Tier 1 model" sometimes referred to the Data Pack Evolution Tier 1 (Assisted Migration Drafting; §14.2.2 below), which is unrelated to Tier 1 events. This chapter keeps both usages but they are distinguished by context: "Tier 1 event" = config approval; "Data Pack Evolution Tier 1" = migration drafting.

Per-event rationale is in releases.md. The full rationale paragraphs are not duplicated here.

2.2 Jarvis-Coder control hierarchy
§14.2.1 Three roles:

Jarvis (Orchestrator): Read access to local codebase, docs, sul-hive-mind reference repos. Evaluates telemetry, performs diagnostics, formulates task specifications.

Coder AI (Worker): Drafts code refactoring, bug fixes, patches in isolated git worktrees. Drafts autonomously, never merges without user approval except under Coder allowlist. Hardcoded zero write authority over: sul-trust, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog, Ed25519 signing keys, auto-updater manifest, and now also sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, sul-voice-auth (the vault's cryptographic material and auth logic), sul-auth-app (app-level auth). Compiles + runs sandbox test suites before proposing.

User (Governor): Veto power.

§14.2.2 Autonomous Data Pack Evolution (three-tier policy):

Tier 0 — Autonomous Registry Sync (no approval): .sulpack schema behind → fetch signed migrations, apply, run validation + round-trip test. Both pass: commit, log. Either fails: auto-rollback.

Tier 1 — Assisted Migration Drafting (one-click approval): Registry has no migration. Coder parses failing log/config, produces schema delta, writes migration in isolated worktree, runs tests, presents modal. On approve: commits, proposes PR against sul-hive-mind. Runs on GitHub Actions via dispatch_ci.

Tier 2 — Unknown-Schema Fallback: Disable only the specific feature, show clear message, offer "draft locally with note."

§14.2.3 Coder write restrictions: Coder never writes outside %APPDATA%\\SUL\sulpack\ and never touches trust primitives at any tier. This is enforced by the AST guard (cargo xtask ac-regression) and by the Gate A check (§14.3) — a PR that touches trust primitives is refused regardless of Gate B outcome.

Hardcoded zero write authority over:

sul-trust, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog (security substrate).

Ed25519 signing keys (in %APPDATA%\\SUL\trust\).

Auto-updater manifest.

sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, sul-voice-auth (vault cryptographic material).

sul-auth-app (app-level auth).

A PR that touches any of these files is refused by the Gate A check with E_TRUST_PRIMITIVE_WRITE (Ch. 1 §3.4 base error codes). The user can override the refusal only via a Tier 1 approval modal, which is a deliberate multi-step action (Ch. 16 §16.6).

Additional protections (from Ch. 16 §16.15 AST guards):

sul-auth-app must not expose a bypass path in release builds.

The trust primitive files are Ed25519-signed; a modified file fails signature verification and triggers quarantine (Mode D, §14.10).

The Coder AI's worktree has no write access to %APPDATA%\\SUL\trust\ (filesystem permission enforced at worktree creation).

2.3 Dual-gate safety protocol
§14.3.1 The two gates:

Gate A (Upstream Code Change Check): verify game binary checksum, API contract, or anti-cheat manifest actually modified.

Gate B (Functional Breakage Check): evaluate whether active functionality is impaired.

Rule: Gate A AND Gate B must both be true. (Augmented in R2+ by `security_audit`, A.183: a 4-stage Coder diff check—secrets → dependency CVEs → `unsafe` review → IPC boundaries—where no agent instance may verify its own finding.)

Both gates are deterministic checks (not LLM-driven). The user approves the final diff via the OS-level modal; the gates ensure the diff is worth approving before it reaches the user.

§14.3.2 Gate A extensions: Gate A extends to every subsystem whose changes have security, quality, or anti-cheat implications. Each extension is a verification that must pass before the diff is presented to the user; a failure on any extension blocks the merge regardless of Gate B outcome.

Gate A extends to model file changes. If a Coder PR touches any file under models/ or lora/, Gate A additionally verifies: SHA-256 matches a signed manifest entry. The file parses as a valid GGUF (or ONNX for OCR models). The architecture string is in the supported set (qwen2, qwen2.5, qwen2.5-coder, qwen3, qwen3.5, hammer2, minicpm_v, lfm2_vl, qwen2.5-vl, jina_vlm, internvl3, k2_horizon). The quantization is in the allowed set per Ch. 10 §10.16. For OCR models: the ONNX model is the INT8 quantized variant (not FP32) unless ocr_fp32_fallback = true is explicitly set. A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to STAR-KV models. If a Coder PR touches any STAR-KV artifact or its uncompressed sibling, Gate A additionally verifies the pair_verified_at timestamp is current and the surgery version matches the runtime version. A mismatch on either blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to search pipeline config. Changes to [net.search] require explicit user approval (search backend changes have accuracy and privacy implications). ReTrace is a Tier 1 event (vision compression config change). The Gate A check verifies that config changes to [net.search] are accompanied by the required approval modal record, and that ReTrace config changes are accompanied by a re-verification of the saliency layers and dormant buffer.

Gate A extends to combat profile config and mode-tagged LoRA. If a Coder PR touches [ai.combat], [ai.combat_full.instruct], [ai.combat_full.thinking], [ai.combat_full.conversation], [ai.combat_full.coding], [ai.combat_router], any per-game combat block in game_registry.json, or the mode-tagged LoRA (jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora) or Deep LoRA (jarvis_deep_tools.lora), Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for combat profile changes (releases.md). For LoRA changes: the mode-tagged training data has not regressed to a single-profile-only configuration (verified by re-running the per-profile BFCL and router accuracy gates against the new adapter before merge). For config changes: the new configuration passes the config validator (Ch. 1 §4.2), including the multi-profile checks (Thinking context > Instruct context, Conversation context > Thinking context, Thinking reasoning_budget ≠ 0, Conversation reasoning_budget ≠ 0, single combat_chain, etc.). For destructive_action_always_thinking changes from true to false: the PR includes the destructive-action regression test results showing the safety invariant's disabled behavior is acceptable for the specific use case being enabled. A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to audio routing and voice FX. If a Coder PR touches [audio.routing], [audio.voice_fx], or the sul-voice-fx crate, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for routing/voice-FX changes (releases.md). For voice FX: the DSP p99 budget for the combined feature set is re-measured and remains within the A.88 target (≤8 ms at 512-sample / 48 kHz on AVX2). For neural VC: the ≤30 ms CPU gate is re-checked; the PR is rejected if neural VC is enabled without the gate having passed (E_CFG). For routing: the per-bus round-trip measurements are re-run and the drift gate (zero sample-level drift over 1 hour) is re-checked. For voice cloning: the value is refused in the config; any PR that changes it is rejected regardless of any other verification (structural refusal, Ch. 16 §16.5). A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to STT config and model files. If a Coder PR touches [stt], the whisper.cpp vendor tree, or any file under models/stt/, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for STT config changes (releases.md). For model or quant changes: the new (model, quant) pair is present in the bundled model manifest, and the first A.83 measurement run has been re-executed against the new pair (or the change is marked with a pending-a83-rerun label that blocks release). For [stt] flash_attn: the field is explicitly true in the config — the CI check refuses to merge a PR that removes the explicit setting (the whole point of the setting is that it cannot rely on a default). For [stt] vad = "none": rejected at merge (E_CFG — validator rule A-38 in Ch. 4 §4.4). A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to emulator / savestate config and cores. If a Coder PR touches [emu.gb], [emu.savestate], crates/sul-gb, or crates/sul-savestate, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for emulation config changes (releases.md). For sul-gb: the full Blargg + ACID2 + MBC + APU accuracy suite passes in CI (A.90 is the release gate; a PR that regresses any of (a)–(i) is blocked regardless of its other merits). For sul-savestate: the round-trip byte-identical test passes on every supported core, and the run-ahead p99 (< 200 µs) is re-measured. For [emu.savestate] ring_capacity reductions: rejected at merge if the new value would break run_ahead_frames = 2 (validator rule ES-1 in Ch. 3 §3.6). For [emu.gb] core = "sul_gb": rejected at merge if the A.90 gate has not passed on the current hardware (validator rule ES-4 in Ch. 3 §3.24). A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to vault changes. If a Coder PR touches [vault], crates/sul-vault-core, crates/sul-face-auth, crates/sul-voice-auth, or any vault-related file, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for vault changes (releases.md). All auth factors remain enabled (AND-logic preserved). Anti-debug layers (cynapse/astraguard/anti-dbg) remain active. Decoy vault behavior preserved. KDF parameters match the documented profile. AEAD construction matches the A.92 external review baseline. extra_paths cannot be extended via config edit. A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to WebView hardening. If a Coder PR touches [webview], tauri.conf.json, src-tauri/capabilities/, or the frontend bundle, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for WebView changes (releases.md). Isolation Pattern remains enabled (Tier 1 to disable). Strict ESM remains enabled (Tier 1 to disable). WebView2 runtime floor remains ≥ the current Microsoft security baseline. Tauri version floor remains ≥ 2.11.5. No shell:allow-execute granted to any window. CSP is not null; withGlobalTauri is not true in production. No wildcard fs scopes; no wildcard window capabilities. electron-audit passes. A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to sul-quant, sul-kv-compress, sul-spec-draft, sul-toolprm. If a Coder PR touches any of these crates or their config sections, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for the corresponding config change (releases.md). For sul-quant: SPEED-Q output still holds A.96 per-profile gates. For sul-kv-compress: each enabled backend still holds A.97's PPL + KL@D gates and the multi-session identity preservation test. For sul-spec-draft: RIFT acceptance retention ≥95% at the configured draft KV budget (when engaged). For sul-toolprm: cross-encoder still holds A.100's gates. A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

Gate A extends to app auth and feature/performance toggles. If a Coder PR touches [auth], [features], [performance], or [compat], Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for auth changes (releases.md). All auth factors remain enabled. No core feature is togglable. No structural refusal is togglable. The compatibility matrix still passes on the default config. cargo xtask electron-audit, tauri-capability-audit, and webview-runtime-audit all pass. A mismatch blocks the merge.

Gate A extends to music player. If a Coder PR touches [music], crates/sul-music, crates/sul-music-engine, crates/sul-music-tags, or crates/sul-music-lyrics, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for music-player changes (releases.md). Bit-perfect loopback verification (A.119) is re-run and passes. Gapless sample-accuracy (A.120) is re-run and passes. CPU overhead (A.121) is re-measured and within budget. Device coordination (A.124) refuses exclusive mode when it would conflict with sul-audio. A mismatch blocks the merge.

Gate A extends to broadcast engine. If a Coder PR touches [broadcast], crates/sul-broadcast, crates/sul-broadcast-video, or crates/sul-broadcast-audio, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for broadcast changes (releases.md). Encoder admission controller (A.126) refuses over-budget configurations and downgrades ISOs first. Zero-CPU-readback path (A.127) is re-verified (no copy_to_host in encode path). Per-destination audio mixes (A.128) are verified — Music is on Stream and Record, off VOD; Stream and VOD mixes differ by exactly the music content. USB/IP virtual audio devices (A.129) enumerate without a SUL driver. Audio performance (A.134) — 12 channels × 12 buses with all strip FX on <6% of one core, zero underruns over 60 minutes. A mismatch blocks the merge.

Gate A extends to handoff features. If a Coder PR touches any file under crates/sul-csi/, crates/sul-bci/, crates/sul-gev/, crates/sul-security-toolkit/, crates/sul-voicestudio/, or the corresponding config sections, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for the handoff feature (releases.md). For sul-csi: the CSI node firmware and the host-side FFT processing both still produce vitals within the accuracy gate. For sul-bci: decoding accuracy ≥90% on the eval set, end-to-end latency <200ms. For sul-gev: 10,000+ objects at 60fps, geolocation accuracy on the eval set. For sul-security-toolkit: each tool still passes its functional test; the container isolation is still enforced. For sul-voicestudio: voice cloning structural refusal is still present in the API surface (this is a hard gate — any PR that introduces a "clone specific person" code path is rejected regardless of any other verification); TTS latency <100ms. A mismatch blocks the merge.

Gate A extends to the release plan itself. If a Coder PR touches releases.md, Gate A additionally verifies: The PR is accompanied by the Tier 1 approval modal record for the release plan change (this is a new Tier 1 event in the release-ladder model — see releases.md). The PR preserves the "every release is a strict superset of the previous one" invariant (no component or feature is removed from an earlier release class). Every reference-config block is consistent with its components list. Every A.2 gate reference is valid (gates.md resolution). A mismatch on any of these blocks the merge regardless of Gate B.

2.4 Hive-mind compatibility registry
§14.4.1 Registry structure: Git-hosted registry. SUL fetches read-only, never uploads from user's machine.

Registry entries per game × model × config:

SUCCESS: Anti-cheat pass, game stability verified, mod hooks operate.

PARTIAL: Subsystems compromised. Warning card before launch.

FAILED: Blocks execution, reverts to last verified safe save state.

§14.4.2 Model compatibility matrix: The hive registry carries a per-model × per-game matrix:

Model	Elite Dangerous	Helldivers 2	Notes

Combat Full — Thinking (InternVL3-2B + ReTrace)	✅	✅	Planning/judgment profile; ~1.35–1.45 GB with ReTrace; router-selected per turn
Combat Full — Conversation (InternVL3-2B + ReTrace)	✅	✅	No-game open-ended dialogue; ~1.25–1.30 GB with ReTrace; replaces Butler; lazy-allocated
Combat Full — Coding (InternVL3-2B + ReTrace)	⚠️ opt-in	⚠️ opt-in	No-game code work; ~1.15–1.30 GB with ReTrace; ships only if A.101 passes (HumanEval ≥60); ED co-resident with Deep fits with 2–4 layer offload
K2-Horizon-7B (Deep)	✅	❌	Does not fit during HD2; Q5_K_M at 4K fits on ED with ~1 GB headroom
