§14.4.3 Registry sync: On session start: git fetch --dry-run against sul-hive-mind. If behind, prompt user to pull. During session: cache-when-fresh, network-when-stale (via fetch_hive, Ch. 11 §2.18).

[Correction D-132 note (Phase 2 consistency sweep): §2.4's model matrix previously carried 2.5 GB HD2 ceiling language in the sul_toolprm_enc and ToolRM Qwen3-4B rows ("fits HD2 ceiling", "exceeds HD2 ceiling by ~2 GB"). Those rows now read "fits the general 3 GB combat ceiling" and "exceeds the general 3 GB combat ceiling by ~0.8–1 GB" respectively, aligning with Phase 2's retirement of the HD2-specific ceiling (D-112). The remaining rows reference specific VRAM figures, not ceilings, and are unchanged. The "Does not fit during HD2" note for K2-Horizon-7B (Deep) is still accurate under the general 3 GB ceiling and is unchanged.]

2.5 Auto-updater
§14.5.1 Signing and rollback:

Ed25519 Minisign Verification: CI artifacts signed with TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY. Client rejects unsigned/tampered.

Silent hot-swap and relaunch: Rollback on failed launch. If new version fails init at any Ch. 1 §2.7 stage, revert, notify, log. State in %APPDATA%\\SUL\updater\rollback.

§14.5.2 Release-ladder enforcement on update: Every update package declares the release class of the version it installs (v0.1 = R0, v0.2 = R1, v0.4 = R2, v0.6 = R3; see releases.md). The updater refuses to install a package whose declared release class is not the immediate successor or a later successor of the currently-installed release class — no skipping from R0 to R2, because the R1 features in R2's enable set were not validated on the R0-installed config. In practice the update channel serves the latest minor within the current major; the release-class guard is a defense against a corrupted or tampered update manifest that jumps the ladder. A mismatch is E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP and the update is refused.

§14.5.3 Model-file auto-update: Model files follow the same signing chain. Model updates that change quantization, architecture, or KV config require the same Tier 1 modal as releases.md. Model updates that only patch weights (same architecture, same quant, newer commit) are Tier 0 (auto-apply with signature verification). OCR and VLM model updates follow the same rule.

§14.5.4 Mode-tagged LoRA auto-update: Updates to jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora and jarvis_deep_tools.lora are Tier 1 events (not Tier 0) because the adapter's mode-tagging, profile-specific loss weighting, and router-aware ToolPRM training are all load-bearing for the multi-profile design. A silent adapter swap that regressed one profile's BFCL or the router's accuracy would break Combat Full without the user knowing.

The auto-updater verifies:

Signature chain matches the release signing chain.

The new adapter's merged-GGUF passes the cargo xtask verify-lora-merge check (cosine similarity >0.998, output-token equality >98%).

The mode-tagged data hash matches a manifest entry (preventing a downgrade to single-profile-only data).

The new adapter passes per-profile BFCL and router accuracy gates against the current game_registry.json test set (using cached results from A.63 if recent, otherwise the update is deferred until the next A.63 measurement).

If any check fails, the adapter is not swapped in; the user is notified and the current adapter remains loaded. This is stricter than the general model-update rule because the adapter is the multi-profile design's load-bearing component.

§14.5.5 Speculation drafter auto-update: Medusa-1 heads, phrase-head MLP, ChainFlow, LiLiCorr, and UniSpec adapter updates follow the same rule: sign-verified at load, Tier 1 modal if architecture or quant changes, Tier 0 if only weights patched. STAR-KV surgery version must match runtime version — auto-updater refuses to swap in a model whose surgery version is incompatible.

Medusa-1 head auto-update: Medusa head files (.pt → converted GGUF) follow the standard signing chain. Tier 1 modal if the head architecture changes (e.g., shared-LM-head → own-LM-head — rejected by validator anyway). Tier 0 if only weights patched. The auto-updater verifies temperature scaling config is preserved.

Phrase-head auto-update: Phrase-head MLP files follow the same rule. Tier 1 if head architecture changes; Tier 0 if only weights patched.

LiLiCorr scorer auto-update: LiLiCorr scorer transformer follows the standard signing chain. Tier 1 if scorer architecture changes; Tier 0 if only weights patched.

§14.5.6 Search, ReTrace, OODA, TSCG auto-update:

Search pipeline config auto-update: Config changes to [net.search] require Tier 1 modal if they change backend or disable verification packet. RustXNG binary updates follow the standard signing chain. adblock-rust filter list updates are Tier 0 (auto-apply with signature verification — filter lists are signed by their maintainers).

GitHub search config auto-update: [net.github] enabled changes are Tier 1 events. cache_ttl_hours and rate_limit_per_session changes are Tier 0 (bounded fields with validator ranges).

ReTrace model auto-update: ReTrace saliency layer definitions and dormant buffer format follow same signing chain. Surgery version must match runtime version. If ReTrace artifact version is incompatible with the Combat Full model, auto-updater refuses to swap in either — both must be updated together.

OODA-Tool / TSCG updates: These are code-level changes to sul-agent, not model files. They ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain. Router code changes (sul-agent::combat_profile) follow the same rule — they ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain. Because the router is code (not config), router changes do not have a separate auto-update path; they are part of the SUL binary update, which is signed and verified as a whole. A router change that affects profile selection accuracy is caught by the binary's own test gates before release.

§14.5.7 Frame-generation and audio auto-update:

Frame generation layer auto-update: The sul-fg layer manifests (VkLayer_sul_fg.json, VkLayer_LSFGVK_frame_generation.json) and the native layer binary follow the standard release signing chain. They ship with the SUL binary. The upstream lsfg-vk layer, if vendored, follows the same rule (Tier 1 modal if the layer version changes). Lossless.dll is user-supplied and is not auto-updated. The auto-updater does not touch any file in %APPDATA%\\SUL\fg\ that is not a SUL-signed layer manifest or SUL-signed native layer binary. The user is responsible for re-supplying a valid Lossless.dll if they replace it manually or if the source Lossless Scaling application updates it; SUL re-imports on next launch.

Audio governor updates: sul-audio-governor ships with the SUL binary. Its decision loop parameters are code, not config; they follow the standard release signing chain. No separate auto-update path.

Audio routing and voice FX updates: sul-voice-fx ships with the SUL binary and follows the standard release signing chain — no separate auto-update path. The routing matrix and voice FX config are signed as part of config.toml (the whole config file is signed, not each section). Neural VC models (if/when A.89 ever ships) would follow the model-file signing chain, but neural VC is research only — nothing to update in the shipping release. Voice-cloning models do not exist in the shipping release and never will (Ch. 16 §16.5); the auto-updater has no path that could introduce one.

§14.5.8 Vault and auth auto-update:

Vault auto-update: sul-vault-core, sul-face-auth, and sul-voice-auth ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain — no separate auto-update path. The vault file format is versioned and the AEAD construction version is immutable (once a file is encrypted with format v1, it stays v1 until the user explicitly runs a re-encryption migration — which is Tier 1 and requires A.92 re-review). Updates to the runtime do not change the format; the runtime always supports the current format version plus one previous version for migration. Auth models (RetinaFace/ArcFace/sherpa-onnx) follow the standard model-file signing chain. Changes to KDF parameters (argon2id memory/time/parallelism) trigger a background re-KEK without re-encrypting the whole vault — Tier 1 event.

App auth auto-update: sul-auth-app ships with the SUL binary and follows the standard release signing chain. Auth factor enrollment data is stored at %APPDATA%\\SUL\auth\ and is signed with the user's Ed25519 key. Updates that change the auth store format are Tier 1 and include a migration path that re-signs the store.

§14.5.9 WebView, music, broadcast auto-update:

WebView auto-update: WebView2 runtime updates come from Windows Update (Microsoft's channel), not SUL. SUL checks the runtime version at launch and refuses to run below [webview] runtime_floor (E_WEBVIEW_RUNTIME_BELOW_FLOOR). When Microsoft releases a security advisory and updates the baseline, SUL surfaces a WebViewRuntimeReview to bump [webview] runtime_floor (Tier 1 event). Tauri updates follow the standard release signing chain (part of the SUL binary). Plugin updates (plugin-updater >= 2.12.0, plugin-dialog, plugin-http) are vendored in the workspace and follow the SUL binary release.

Music player auto-update: sul-music.exe and its crates ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain. The music library SQLite schema is versioned and migrations are applied on first launch after update (Tier 0 — schema-only). Tag-writing behavior changes (lofty updates) are Tier 1 if they change the backup-before-write guarantee. sul-music-engine WASAPI path updates are Tier 1 if they change the bit-perfect definition or device coordination logic.

Broadcast engine auto-update: sul-broadcast.exe and its crates ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain. Scene document schema changes are versioned and migrations are applied on first launch (Tier 0 — schema-only). Encoder backend updates (NVENC/AMF/QSV drivers) follow the driver vendor's channel; SUL re-probes throughput at engine start. The admission controller constants are part of the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain. Lossless.dll is user-supplied and is not auto-updated (same as sul-fg).

§14.5.10 STT, GB, savestate auto-update:

STT auto-update: whisper.cpp vendor tree updates follow the standard release signing chain (they ship with the SUL binary). Bundled STT models (tiny.en, base.en, small.en, medium.en at the shipping quant) follow the model-file signing chain. An STT model update that changes the model file or the quant is Tier 1 (releases.md) — the A.83 measurement must be re-run against the new file. An STT model update that only patches weights (same architecture, same quant, same file name) is Tier 0. The [stt] config section is signed as part of config.toml. STT has no separate auto-update path beyond these — it is a library in sul-audio's process, not a standalone artifact.

Game Boy / savestate auto-update: sul-gb and sul-savestate ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard release signing chain — no separate auto-update path. The [emu.gb] and [emu.savestate] config sections are signed as part of config.toml. A sul-gb update that regresses any Blargg / ACID2 / MBC / APU test blocks the binary release itself (the accuracy gate is a release gate, not a post-release check). There is no scenario where a broken sul-gb lands in a release and then needs a patched savestate to work around — the CI gate prevents that.

§14.5.11 Quant, KV-compress, spec-draft, ToolPRM auto-update:

sul-quant auto-update: sul-quant ships with the SUL binary. SPEED-Q submodule updates follow the standard release signing chain (pinned commit in VERSIONS.toml). The APEX planner is part of the SUL binary. When the SPEED-Q submodule updates, the CI job re-runs A.96 to verify the per-profile gates still hold; if they don't, the update is reverted. No separate auto-update path.

sul-kv-compress auto-update: sul-kv-compress ships with the SUL binary. Backend crates (palquant, puzzlekv, jolt, turboquant, tcq) are workspace deps with pinned versions. Updates are Tier 0 if only weights/code patches with no API change, Tier 1 if a new backend is enabled for a tier. A.97 must be re-run against any backend update that affects runtime behavior.

sul-spec-draft auto-update: sul-spec-draft ships with the SUL binary. The unispec_adapter thin wrapper follows the unispec crate's release cadence. RIFT selection/refresh algorithm is part of the SUL binary. When RIFT is engaged (>32 MB draft cache), an update that changes refresh behavior is Tier 1. When RIFT is dormant (the shipping state), updates are Tier 0.

sul-toolprm auto-update: The cross-encoder model file (sul_toolprm_enc_q4.gguf) follows the standard model-file signing chain. Cross-encoder architecture changes (e.g., 12×768 → 6×1024) are Tier 1. Weight-only updates are Tier 0 if the new weights pass A.100's gates against cached recent runs. The training script (train.py) is part of the SUL repo, not shipped — training runs happen on rented GPUs, and the resulting model ships through the standard model-file signing chain.

§14.5.12 Release-plan auto-update: The releases.md file is part of the SUL repo and ships with the binary. Its content is signed by the release signing key. The installed release class is recorded at %APPDATA%/SUL/release.toml at install time and is signed. A tampered release.toml that claims a different release class than the installed binary is caught by matching against the binary's own embedded release class (both must agree). A tampered releases.md is not actionable at runtime — it is a build-time artifact — but a build that ships a releases.md differing from the one the release binary was compiled with fails the release-audit check cargo xtask release-audit.

§14.5.13 Handoff feature auto-update:

sul-csi auto-update: ships with the SUL binary. ESP32 firmware updates follow the standard signing chain (firmware image signed by SUL maintainer key, ESP32 secure boot verifies signature on flash). Edge inference model updates (4 KB INT8 models) are Tier 1 if the model architecture changes, Tier 0 if only weights patched.

sul-bci auto-update: ships with the SUL binary. brain2qwerty-rs model updates follow the model-file signing chain. Model architecture changes are Tier 1.

sul-gev auto-update: ships with the SUL binary. Base globe tiles are vendored with the binary. Feed ingestion logic updates are part of the binary signing chain.

sul-security-toolkit auto-update: ships with the SUL binary. Container images (Shannon Lite, security toolkit) follow the standard release signing chain (signed Docker images verified at pull time). Wordlists are Tier 0 (auto-apply with signature verification — wordlists are signed by their maintainers).

sul-voicestudio auto-update: sul-voicestudio.exe and its crates ship with the SUL binary. VoiceStudio model updates follow the model-file signing chain. Character voice model updates that expand the voice catalog are Tier 1 (they change the available character voices). Any update that would introduce a "clone specific person" code path is rejected at the CI gate regardless of its other merits — the structural refusal is a hard invariant.

2.6 SOTA self-improvement pipeline
Jarvis maintains live understanding of SOTA patterns by ingesting docs, Rust RFCs, high-performance OSS designs. Technical Translation: Coder implements optimization, user asks "why?", Jarvis translates Git diff to plain language.

Model-benchmark ingestion: Jarvis ingests Local Agent Bench, BFCL, ToolPRM, SWE-bench, K2-Horizon vendor benchmarks, OCRBench, ScreenSpot-v2, and the PaddleOCR mobile benchmarks on a 30-day cycle. When a newly published benchmark materially changes the model ladder recommendation (e.g., a new model beats InternVL3-2B by >5 points on Agent Score for any of the four profiles, or a new OCR model beats PP-OCRv5 INT8 on HUD-specific accuracy), Jarvis surfaces a ModelLadderReview task via the Coder workflow. It never auto-swaps models — it drafts the review, the user decides.

Jarvis also ingests: STAR-KV quality reports from upstream; GAAC validation results; Medusa-1 acceptance reports; phrase-head acceptance reports; LiLiCorr acceptance reports; UniSpec and ChainFlow acceptance benchmarks; Fluxion/Silmic-RT DSP/voice papers; jina-vlm multilingual VQA benchmarks; Surya 2.5 OmniParseBench results; PalQuant/PuzzleKV/JoLT/TurboQuant+/TCQ KV compression benchmarks. New benchmark data can trigger a ModelLadderReview or KvTierReview (same workflow, Tier 1 event per §14.1).

Jarvis also ingests: ReTrace benchmark retention (MMB, MMBCN, POPE, SQAI, MME at varying token retention ratios); RustXNG search latency and result quality; adblock-rust filter performance; readdown extraction quality (token reduction ratio vs raw HTML); Exa-style excerpt selection accuracy; verification packet fallacy detection precision/recall; OODA-Tool multi-turn accuracy improvement; TSCG schema compression ratio and tool-accuracy retention; Combat Full fine-tuning BFCL results (from A.63); GitHub search API changes. New benchmark data can trigger a ModelLadderReview, KvTierReview, SearchPipelineReview, ReTraceReview, or CombatFullReview (same workflow, Tier 1 event per §14.1).

Jarvis also ingests router-specific benchmarks. New data on: router profile-selection accuracy from published sources or community reports; destructive-action detection recall from real-world failure reports; profile-switch latency from hardware reports; per-profile BFCL from fine-tuned model releases. When a new benchmark materially changes the router's expected behavior (e.g., a new fine-tuning recipe improves per-profile BFCL by >5 points on any profile, or a community report identifies a destructive-action class the deterministic detector misses), Jarvis surfaces a CombatRouterReview via the Coder workflow. The review includes the specific gap (detection class missed, accuracy regression), a proposed change to sul-agent::combat_profile or the training recipe, and a re-run of the router tests (200 SUL-shaped turns + 100 scripted destructive triggers). It never auto-updates the router — the user decides. New router data is also recorded in combat_profile_history.json (§14.5 / Ch. 10 §10.24) for post-hoc analysis.

Jarvis also ingests: frame-generation performance reports from lsfg-vk, win-fg, and Lossless Scaling upstreams; FSR3 optical-flow quality reports; emulator-specific FG compatibility reports; audio governor latency reports from CamillaDSP and WASAPI upstreams. New benchmark data can trigger a FrameGenReview or AudioGovernorReview (same workflow, Tier 1 event per §14.1).

Jarvis also ingests audio/STT/emulation-specific benchmarks. New data on: WhisperPipe, Nemotron 3 ASR, and FastConformer streaming benchmarks (A.83 rung 1/2/3); STT WER measurements on the SUL combat-speech eval set; whisper.cpp quantization quality reports (q5_1 vs fp16 on HUD-adjacent speech); STT pipeline-customization measurements from community deployments (VAD gate, silence removal, stereo split); VB-Audio / VoiceMeeter / Voicemod release notes; RVC / kNN-VC CPU-resident latency reports (A.89 gate); Game Boy accuracy-suite results from Mizu / boytacean / gb-emulator upstreams; Blargg / ACID2 test-suite changes; libretro C-ABI audit updates (any new UB class discovered upstream); PPSSPP async-savestate measurements. New benchmark data can trigger an SttReview, AudioRoutingReview, VoiceFxReview, GbAccuracyReview, or SavestateReview (same workflow, Tier 1 event per §14.1). The review includes the specific gap or improvement, a proposed change, and the re-run of the corresponding gate (A.83 / A.87 / A.88 / A.90 / A.91). It never auto-updates — the user decides.

Quantization-specific ingestion. Jarvis ingests SPEED-Q upstream updates (new ViT quant methods, LLM quant refinements), LiteRT quantization reports (the independent Google confirmation of the modality split), APEX mixed-precision reports from the llama.cpp community, and JQ-series fork PR status (#30716 / #30717 for CPU + Metal + CUDA JQ5_K support). When a new quantization method materially improves quality-per-VRAM beyond what sul-quant currently achieves, Jarvis surfaces a QuantReview (Tier 1 event). When the JQ PRs merge into mainline, Jarvis surfaces a QuantReview to enable JQ5_K for Deep.

KV-compression-specific ingestion. Jarvis ingests PalQuant, PuzzleKV, JoLT, TurboQuant+, and TCQ upstream reports. When a new backend materially improves A.97's quality gates or compression ratio, Jarvis surfaces a KvCompressReview (Tier 1 event). When the fused STAR-KV dequant-and-attend kernel (A.105 research entry) produces a working CUDA kernel, Jarvis surfaces a KvCompressReview to enable it.

WebView security ingestion. Jarvis ingests WebView2 release notes from Microsoft (to update [webview] runtime_floor), Tauri security advisories (to update the version floor), and CVEs in the Tauri plugin ecosystem. When a new WebView2 or Tauri CVE affects SUL's pinned version, Jarvis surfaces a WebViewReview (Tier 1 event). Updates are always accompanied by a re-run of tauri-capability-audit and webview-runtime-audit.

Vault security ingestion. Jarvis ingests AEAD cryptanalysis reports (XChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-256-GCM), DPAPI/TPM advisories from Microsoft and the TPM specification body, and any new side-channel disclosures for the primitives sul-vault-core uses. When a new disclosure affects SUL's vault, Jarvis surfaces a VaultReview (Tier 1 event). The review includes the specific disclosure, a proposed mitigation (rotate cipher? bump KDF parameters? add defense layer?), and a re-run of A.92's adversarial cases.

Music player ingestion. Jarvis ingests Musicolet release notes, Symphonia decoder updates, wasapi-rs/cpal/rodio releases, lofty tag library updates, ReplayGain/EQ DSP updates, and SMTC API changes. When a new codec support lands in Symphonia, or a new DSP backend materially improves quality/CPU, Jarvis surfaces a MusicReview (Tier 1 event). When a WASAPI device driver issue is reported, Jarvis surfaces a DeviceCoordinationReview.

Broadcast engine ingestion. Jarvis ingests OBS/Isocast/Smelter performance reports, NVENC/AMF/QSV driver releases, arcly-stream transport updates, wgpu compositor releases, USB/IP virtual device server updates, and VBAN protocol changes. When a new encoder preset or transport improves the pixel budget, Jarvis surfaces a BroadcastEncoderReview. When a new capture backend or compositor feature lands, Jarvis surfaces a BroadcastCompositorReview. When a new audio strip DSP or voice FX preset pack is released, Jarvis surfaces a BroadcastAudioReview. When a new virtual device mechanism (USB/IP or otherwise) is validated, Jarvis surfaces a BroadcastVirtualDeviceReview. All are Tier 1 events.

Handoff feature ingestion. Jarvis ingests: CSI sensing research (new pose estimation models, edge inference improvements); BCI decoding research (brain2qwerty-rs updates, OpenBCI hardware releases, new decoding models); geospatial intelligence research (new ADS-B/AIS feeds, geolocation models, globe rendering techniques); security tooling releases (hashcat, nuclei, mitmproxy, Shannon, Ghidra MCP updates); VoiceStudio updates (TTS improvements, language expansion, character voice models). When a new benchmark materially changes a handoff feature's expected behavior, Jarvis surfaces the corresponding Review (CsiReview, BciReview, GevReview, SecurityToolkitReview, VoiceStudioReview) — all Tier 1 events.

Release-plan ingestion. Jarvis ingests the releases.md state after every A.2 gate outcome. When a gate passes, Jarvis surfaces a ReleaseReadinessReview proposing that the corresponding feature move from gated to shipped in its release class — no automatic promotion; the user decides. When a gate fails or an A.4 research item graduates, Jarvis surfaces the corresponding change. This makes the release-ladder in Ch. 1 §2.3 a living artifact that tracks gate outcomes.

2.7 Self-healing watchdog — overview and Mode A
Coder elevation only after deterministic recovery matrix exhausted.

The recovery matrix:

Mode	Category	Recovery
A	LLM inference timeout	Retry once, halve context, retry, CPU-Only retry, mark degraded.
B	Invalid structured output	Retry 3× stricter schema. Fall back to unstructured text.
C	IPC channel death	Recreate channel, replay last message. 3× fail → degraded.
D	Model file corruption	SHA-256 verify against signed manifest. On mismatch: quarantine lifecycle, prompt redownload.
E	Rust panic in supervised subsystem thread	Capture minidump. Per-process handling: sul-ai / sul-ipc = kill + relaunch clean; supervised thread in sul.exe = validate shared state against last-known-good before respawn. 3× repeat → degraded.
F	Cascading persistent failure	Escalates to Coder. Bounded repair scope: reads minidumps, proposes specific diffs, runs cargo test via Ch. 11 §2.14 for >30s, presents each diff individually. Hardcoded zero write to trust primitives.
Mode A specifics (LLM inference timeout):

Retry once at the same settings.

Halve context, retry.

CPU-Only retry (drop CUDA, run on CPU).

If all fail, mark tier degraded; session continues with a degraded tier.

Mode A error classes: E_INFER_TIMEOUT, E_INFER_INVALID_OUTPUT (Ch. 1 §3.4).

2.8 Mode B
Mode B — invalid structured output:

Retry 3× with stricter schema.

Fall back to unstructured text.

Includes E_TOOL_UNFORMABLE after verification escalation is exhausted.

Also includes the audio governor's exclusive-mode refusal (E_AG_EXCLUSIVE_BLOCKED) and the frame generation refusals (E_FG_VRAM_RESERVE_UNAVAILABLE, E_FG_BASE_FPS_BELOW_THRESHOLD, E_FG_NATIVE_FPS_UNKNOWN, E_FG_AC_REFUSED, E_FG_UNSAFE_TITLE_REFUSED) — the game runs without the corresponding subsystem; these are non-fatal.

Also includes the routing and voice-FX refusals (E_ROUTING_VIRTUAL_CABLE_MISSING, E_ROUTING_DEVICE_IN_USE, E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED when the governor cannot disable enough FX to fit the budget) — the routing matrix is not enabled for the session, but the base Ch. 4 §4.2 DSP pipeline still runs; the game and audio still work.

Also includes the emulation refusals (E_GB_MAPPER_UNSUPPORTED, E_GB_ACCURACY_GATE_FAILED) — the emulated title runs under Gambatte instead of sul-gb; no user-facing functional loss, only the from-scratch core is not used.

Also includes E_STT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND when the bundled default is also missing (rare) — STT is disabled for the session and the voice loop (A.85) reports STT unavailable via overlay.

Also includes E_VAULT_UNLOCK_FAILED, E_VAULT_RATE_LIMITED, E_VAULT_HARDWARE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE — vault remains locked; session continues without vault access.

Also includes E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT — music player falls back to shared mode; E_BROADCAST_ADMISSION_REFUSED — stream refuses to start; game continues.

Also includes E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP — the update is refused; the currently-installed version continues to run; the release-ladder guard in §14.5.2 is what keeps the "strict superset" invariant.

Mode B error classes: E_TOOL_UNFORMABLE, E_AG_EXCLUSIVE_BLOCKED, E_FG_VRAM_RESERVE_UNAVAILABLE, E_FG_BASE_FPS_BELOW_THRESHOLD, E_FG_NATIVE_FPS_UNKNOWN, E_FG_AC_REFUSED, E_FG_UNSAFE_TITLE_REFUSED, E_ROUTING_VIRTUAL_CABLE_MISSING, E_ROUTING_DEVICE_IN_USE, E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, E_GB_MAPPER_UNSUPPORTED, E_GB_ACCURACY_GATE_FAILED, E_STT_MODEL_NOT_FOUND, E_VAULT_UNLOCK_FAILED, E_VAULT_RATE_LIMITED, E_VAULT_HARDWARE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE, E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT, E_BROADCAST_ADMISSION_REFUSED, E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP.

2.9 Mode C
Mode C — IPC channel death:

Recreate channel, replay last message.

3× fail → degraded.

Includes sul-kv-tier cold-read failure — fall back to hot/warm only.

Also includes E_WIRE_RING_NOT_MAPPED (remap via WireRemapRing) and E_KV_COLD_READ_FAILED (fall back to hot/warm only), E_SEARCH_PIPELINE_DEGRADED (fall back to direct fetch with truncated context), E_RETRACE_BACKTRACK_INJECTION (fall back to full-token baseline for that pass), E_FG_LAYER_LOAD_FAILED / E_FG_DLL_MISSING / E_FG_FRAME_CORRUPTED / E_FG_VULKAN_INCOMPATIBLE (disable FG for session, fall back to win_fg or off, game runs without FG), and E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW / E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN (drop the longest FIR or HRTF, session continues).

Also includes E_COMBAT_ROUTER_INIT_FAILED — if the router fails to initialize at startup (Ch. 1 §2.7 step 6.6), the session runs in fixed profile (default: Instruct) and the overlay shows a warning chip on CombatProfileIndicator. Fixed-profile operation is a documented degraded state, not silent — the user knows the router is not making decisions.

Also includes the routing and voice-FX degraded fallbacks: E_ROUTING_LIMITER_OVERFLOW (governor reduces limiter aggressiveness), E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED (governor disables the lowest-priority FX — ring mod → bitcrush → formant → pitch — until the DSP p99 fits the budget), E_STT_AUDIO_CTX_INVALID (clamp to default and log), E_STT_FLASH_ATTN_UNAVAILABLE (fall back to non-flash path — still functional, slower), E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED (fall back to gpu_both if GPU present, else cpu_both).

Also includes E_SAVESTATE_SIZE_MISMATCH / E_SAVESTATE_WORKER_STALLED / E_SAVESTATE_ROUND_TRIP_MISMATCH — run-ahead disabled for the affected core; emulation continues without run-ahead.

Also includes E_QUANT_SPEED_Q_FAILED (fall back to llama.cpp Q4_K_S), E_QUANT_APEX_PLANNER_FAILED (fall back to SPEED-Q 4-bit uniform), E_QUANT_GGUF_NOT_K_QUANT (fall back to llama.cpp Q4_K_S), E_KV_COMPRESS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE (fall back to STAR-KV/GAAC), E_KV_COMPRESS_IDENTITY_FAILED (fall back to GAAC), E_RIFT_REFRESH_STALLED (drop to RIFT-stat), E_TOOLPRM_LOAD_FAILED / E_TOOLPRM_CACHE_THRASH (fall back to no-PRM baseline), E_COMBAT_PROFILE_AMBIGUOUS (default to Instruct; log), E_GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED / E_GITHUB_AUTH_FAILED (disable github_search for session).

Also includes E_MUSIC_BIT_PERFECT_UNAVAILABLE (badge hidden, UI shows reason), E_BROADCAST_USBIP_ENUM_FAILED (fall back to VBAN bridge), E_BROADCAST_ENCODER_OVERLOAD (admission controller downgrade order; if still over, refuse), E_BROADCAST_AUDIO_UNDERRUN (governor adjusts buffer size / drops FX).

Handoff: E_CSI_NODE_DISCONNECTED (fall back to host-side processing); E_GEV_FEED_UNAVAILABLE (use cached tiles); E_VOICESTUDIO_MODEL_MISSING (fall back to Piper TTS).

Mode C error classes: (the above, plus) E_WIRE_RING_NOT_MAPPED, E_KV_COLD_READ_FAILED, E_SEARCH_PIPELINE_DEGRADED, E_RETRACE_BACKTRACK_INJECTION, E_FG_LAYER_LOAD_FAILED, E_FG_DLL_MISSING, E_FG_FRAME_CORRUPTED, E_FG_VULKAN_INCOMPATIBLE, E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW, E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN, E_COMBAT_ROUTER_INIT_FAILED, E_ROUTING_LIMITER_OVERFLOW, E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, E_STT_AUDIO_CTX_INVALID, E_STT_FLASH_ATTN_UNAVAILABLE, E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED, E_SAVESTATE_SIZE_MISMATCH, E_SAVESTATE_WORKER_STALLED, E_SAVESTATE_ROUND_TRIP_MISMATCH, E_QUANT_SPEED_Q_FAILED, E_QUANT_APEX_PLANNER_FAILED, E_QUANT_GGUF_NOT_K_QUANT, E_KV_COMPRESS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, E_KV_COMPRESS_IDENTITY_FAILED, E_RIFT_REFRESH_STALLED, E_TOOLPRM_LOAD_FAILED, E_TOOLPRM_CACHE_THRASH, E_COMBAT_PROFILE_AMBIGUOUS, E_GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED, E_GITHUB_AUTH_FAILED, E_MUSIC_BIT_PERFECT_UNAVAILABLE, E_BROADCAST_USBIP_ENUM_FAILED, E_BROADCAST_ENCODER_OVERLOAD, E_BROADCAST_AUDIO_UNDERRUN, E_CSI_NODE_DISCONNECTED, E_GEV_FEED_UNAVAILABLE, E_VOICESTUDIO_MODEL_MISSING.

2.10 Mode D
Mode D — model file corruption:

SHA-256 verify against signed manifest. On mismatch: quarantine lifecycle, prompt redownload.

Includes sul-ocr and sul-vlm model checksum failures (E_OCR_MODEL).

Also includes E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH (refuse load, prompt redownload), E_STAR_KV_PAIR_MISMATCH (refuse load), E_DSP_ARTIFACT_HASH (refuse DSP artifact, fall back to AVX2), E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING (disable voice isolation, log), E_RETRACE_UNAVAILABLE (refuse Combat Full this session, reload full-token baseline), and E_AG_DEVICE_LOST (re-query the audio device, re-decide the governor's six decisions, resume).

Also includes mode-tagged LoRA corruption — if jarvis_combat_full_tools.lora fails its mode-tagged data hash verification, the loader refuses to swap in the adapter and reverts to the last verified adapter; Combat Full runs with the previous adapter's behavior until the user re-imports a signed adapter.

Also includes E_GB_ROM_CORRUPT (quarantine lifecycle on the corrupted ROM; sul-gb refuses to load, Gambatte refuses too unless the ROM parses — the user is notified with the parse error).

Also includes E_MEDUSA_TEMP_SCALING_MISSING / E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT (config error, abort startup).

Also includes E_MUSIC_TAG_BACKUP_FAILED (refuse tag write; user must resolve backup failure).

Also includes E_BROADCAST_USBIP_ENUM_FAILED (Mode C) — but if the USB/IP device driver itself is corrupt, Mode D quarantine lifecycle on the driver file.

Handoff: E_CSI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED (quarantine); E_BCI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED (quarantine); E_GEV_GEOLOCATION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE (quarantine).

Mode D error classes: E_OCR_MODEL, E_STAR_KV_SURGERY_VERSION_MISMATCH, E_STAR_KV_PAIR_MISMATCH, E_DSP_ARTIFACT_HASH, E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING, E_RETRACE_UNAVAILABLE, E_AG_DEVICE_LOST, E_GB_ROM_CORRUPT, E_MEDUSA_TEMP_SCALING_MISSING, E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT, E_MUSIC_TAG_BACKUP_FAILED, E_CSI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED, E_BCI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED, E_GEV_GEOLOCATION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, E_VAULT_TAMPER_DETECTED, E_VAULT_DECOY_ACCESSED.

2.11 Mode E
Mode E — Rust panic in supervised subsystem thread:

Capture minidump.

sul-ai / sul-ipc processes: kill + relaunch clean.

Supervised thread in sul.exe: validate shared state against last-known-good before respawn.

3× repeat → degraded.

Mode E cases:

E_KV_ASYMMETRIC_FA at load → refuse to start; never silently degrade. Intentional: silent quality degradation from asymmetric FA is worse than refusing to start.

E_K2_ARCH at load (fallback mode only) → reload with previous known-good model; do not retry the bad architecture. Log the specific GGUF general.architecture value. Shipping path uses mainline llama.cpp b11454+; E_K2_ARCH only fires when the llama-cpp-2 fallback feature is enabled and K2-Horizon is attempted.

E_EAGLE_DRAFT at Deep load → fall back to LiLiCorr; continue with reduced throughput.

E_MEDUSA_TEMP_SCALING_MISSING / E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT → abort startup with config error (— startup abort). [Correction D-133 note: this line previously read "(Mode F)". Phase 1 Patch 8 / D-106 reclassified config-error startup aborts out of the Mode taxonomy. The parenthetical is now "(— startup abort)" to match failures.md and D-106. The preceding "abort startup with config error" language is unchanged.]

E_OCR_DIMENSION → preprocessing wrapper should have normalized it; if it reaches the backend, log and skip the frame (do not crash).

E_VLM_QUERY_COMPOUND → sul-agent should have decomposed it; if it reaches the backend, log and process the first instruction only, then queue the rest.

sul-vision-sidecar crash → respawn with --safe-mode (Windows App SDK OCR only).

sul-prosody crash → respawn with default_safe_intent = "assess" and log E_PRO_INTENT.

sul-ocr crash → respawn with Windows.Media.Ocr fallback.

sul-vlm crash → disable scene understanding for the session and log E_VLM_BACKEND.

E_STAR_KV_QUALITY → fall back to GAAC + decompression cache. Log. Session continues.

E_UNISPEC_LOW_ACCEPTANCE → drop to next rung in chain. Log. Session continues.

E_SPEC_VERIFY_MISMATCH → disable speculation entirely for that tier. Log. Session continues.

E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE → refuse to load artifact, fall back to AVX2 hand-written chain.

E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING → disable voice isolation, log.

E_RETRACE_BACKTRACK_INJECTION (persistent) → disable ReTrace for session, fall back to full-token baseline. Log. Session continues with +0.3–0.4 GB VRAM.

E_SEARCH_NO_RESULTS (cascade) → mark search pipeline degraded. Log. Model instructed to abstain.

E_VERIFICATION_AMBIGUOUS → surface to model as contested, not error. Model reasons about both sides. Log. Session continues.

E_OODA_INCOMPLETE → retry scaffold once, then skip scaffold for this call. Log. Session continues.

E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED → fall back to raw JSON schema for this call. Log. Session continues.

E_FG_FRAME_CORRUPTED (persistent) → disable FG for session, fall back to win_fg; if win_fg also corrupts, disable FG entirely for the session. Log. Session continues without FG.

E_FG_DLL_MISSING (persistent across auto backend selection) → fall back to win_fg for the session, log once. User is notified in FrameGenStatusIndicator that the native backend is unavailable until Lossless.dll is re-imported.

E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW (persistent) → drop the longest active FIR, log. Session continues with shorter filter.

E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN (persistent) → disable HRTF on the loopback stem, log. Session continues with non-HRTF stereo.

E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID (Thinking-only context failure) → the Instruct context is still available; the router is disabled for the session and all turns run in Instruct profile. CombatProfileIndicator shows a warning chip ("Thinking unavailable — Instruct only"). The user is notified via overlay. Session continues in degraded-but-functional state.

E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID (Conversation-only context failure) → the Instruct context is still available; Conversation is disabled for the session, no-game turns run in Instruct. CombatProfileIndicator shows a warning chip ("Conversation unavailable — Instruct only"). User is notified.

E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID (all-context failure) → neither Instruct (2K) nor Thinking (4K) nor Conversation (16K) nor Coding (8K) context can be allocated; Combat Full is dropped entirely for the session. There is no combat model — the session has no combat tier. The user sees a persistent overlay banner ("Combat Full unavailable this session"). If a game is running, gameplay continues without SUL's combat assistance (OCR still runs, JARVIS still answers from Deep if loaded, but combat-tier reasoning is unavailable). This is a Mode E fatal case for Combat Full specifically, not for the session — the process does not respawn, but the tier is gone.

E_ROUTING_DRIFT_EXCEEDED → routing matrix is disabled for the session; the user is notified ("Sample-level drift between buses exceeded the hard gate — routing disabled"). The Ch. 4 §4.2 DSP pipeline still runs (no routing, just the standard pipeline). Persistent across sessions escalates to Mode F for Coder review of the drift-safety logic.

E_STT_WHISPER_INIT_FAILED → retry once with CPU-only; if that fails, disable STT for the session. The translation/subtitle path degrades to text-only; the voice loop (A.85) reports STT unavailable via overlay. Session continues.

E_SAVESTATE_WORKER_STALLED (persistent) → run-ahead disabled for the affected core for the session; emulation continues without run-ahead. Persistent across sessions escalates to Mode F for Coder review of the worker-drain logic.

E_VAULT_TAMPER_DETECTED / E_VAULT_DECOY_ACCESSED → vault refuses to open; whole vault to quarantine; session continues without vault access; user notified; hive threat log.

E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT → music player falls back to shared mode; user notified.

E_BROADCAST_BUS_DRIFT_EXCEEDED → routing matrix disabled for session; base DSP pipeline continues.

E_BROADCAST_ADMISSION_REFUSED → stream refuses to start; game continues.

E_BROADCAST_AUDIO_UNDERRUN → governor adjusts buffer size / drops FX; session continues.

Mode E error classes: (the above, plus) E_KV_ASYMMETRIC_FA, E_K2_ARCH, E_EAGLE_DRAFT, E_OCR_DIMENSION, E_VLM_QUERY_COMPOUND, E_PRO_INTENT, E_VLM_BACKEND, E_STAR_KV_QUALITY, E_UNISPEC_LOW_ACCEPTANCE, E_SPEC_VERIFY_MISMATCH, E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE, E_SEARCH_NO_RESULTS, E_VERIFICATION_AMBIGUOUS, E_OODA_INCOMPLETE, E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED, E_FG_FRAME_CORRUPTED, E_FG_DLL_MISSING, E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW, E_AG_HRTF_OVERRUN, E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID, E_ROUTING_DRIFT_EXCEEDED, E_STT_WHISPER_INIT_FAILED, E_SAVESTATE_WORKER_STALLED, E_BROADCAST_BUS_DRIFT_EXCEEDED.

2.12 Mode F
Mode F — cascading persistent failure: Escalates to Coder. Bounded repair scope: reads minidumps, proposes specific diffs, runs cargo test via Ch. 11 §2.14 for >30s, presents each diff individually. Hardcoded zero write to trust primitives.

Mode F includes the error classes when they cascade (e.g., repeated E_DSP_ARTIFACT_UNSTABLE across sessions → Coder proposes a repair diff; ReTrace or search pipeline cascade → Coder proposes repair diff; persistent E_OODA_INCOMPLETE across sessions → Coder reviews prompt scaffold logic; persistent E_TSCG_COMPILE_FAILED on specific schemas → Coder reviews TSCG compiler; persistent E_FG_FRAME_CORRUPTED on a specific game/backend combination → Coder reviews the layer's frame hash logic; persistent E_AG_FIR_OVERFLOW on a specific device → Coder reviews the FIR/buffer arithmetic).

Also includes: repeated E_COMBAT_ROUTER_INIT_FAILED across sessions → Coder reviews router initialization and pre-created context allocation; persistent instruct_fallback_rate_pct above tolerance → Coder reviews the router's fallback handling for Thinking OOM; recurring E_COMBAT_PROFILE_INVALID → Coder reviews VRAM reservation and context sizing for Combat Full's four profiles.

Also includes: persistent E_ROUTING_DRIFT_EXCEEDED → Coder reviews the drift-safety logic in sul-audio's routing matrix; persistent E_VOICE_FX_BUDGET_EXCEEDED on a specific hardware profile → Coder reviews the DSP feature-cost estimates; persistent E_STT_WHISPER_INIT_FAILED on a specific hardware profile → Coder reviews the whisper.cpp init path and the model manifest; persistent E_STT_HYBRID_SPLIT_UNSUPPORTED on a specific backend → Coder reviews the hybrid-split availability check; persistent E_SAVESTATE_WORKER_STALLED → Coder reviews the worker-drain logic in sul-savestate; recurring E_GB_ACCURACY_GATE_FAILED for a specific cartridge on the reference rig → Coder reviews the accuracy regression against the Blargg / ACID2 test suite.

Also includes: persistent E_QUANT_SPEED_Q_FAILED → Coder reviews the APEX planner or SPEED-Q wrap; persistent E_KV_COMPRESS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE → Coder reviews the backend A.97 quality gates; persistent E_TOOLPRM_CACHE_THRASH → Coder reviews the score-cache key design; persistent E_MEDUSA_OWN_HEAD_VARIANT misconfiguration → Coder reviews the config (this should be caught at validator, not runtime — a Mode F here means a validator bypass); recurring E_VAULT_TAMPER_DETECTED on the same file → Coder reviews the signature verification path or the hive revocation list; persistent E_WEBVIEW_RUNTIME_BELOW_FLOOR → Coder reviews the runtime-floor check and prompts a WebView2 update flow.

Also includes: persistent E_MUSIC_DEVICE_CONFLICT on a specific device → Coder reviews the device-coordination logic; persistent E_BROADCAST_USBIP_ENUM_FAILED → Coder reviews the USB/IP server enumeration path; persistent E_BROADCAST_AUDIO_UNDERRUN on a specific hardware profile → Coder reviews the broadcast audio buffer sizing and DSP budget; persistent E_BROADCAST_ADMISSION_REFUSED on a configuration the user believes should work → Coder reviews the admission controller's throughput probe and downgrade order. Also includes: repeated E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP across update attempts → Coder reviews the update-manifest release-class declaration and the current installed release class.

Handoff: persistent E_CSI_NODE_DISCONNECTED across sessions → Coder reviews the ESP32 node discovery protocol; persistent E_CSI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED → Coder reviews the edge inference model integrity path; persistent E_BCI_CALIBRATION_FAILED on a specific user → Coder reviews the calibration wizard flow; persistent E_BCI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED → Coder reviews the model manifest; persistent E_GEV_FEED_UNAVAILABLE across multiple networks → Coder reviews the feed ingestion retry logic; persistent E_SECURITY_TOOL_CONTAINER_FAILED → Coder reviews the container lifecycle; persistent E_VOICESTUDIO_MODEL_MISSING → Coder reviews the model provisioning.

Modes A–E are runtime recovery. Mode F is assisted repair.

Mode F error classes: any of the above when it repeats across sessions.

2.13 Real-time integrity watchdog, threat quarantine, hive-mind threat logging
§14.13.1 Two-tier verification:

Tier 1 (Internal Code): Ed25519 Minisign + internal cryptographic binary watermarks. Reference: uzokingkong/BTG-packer (R.10).

Tier 2 (External Protected Runtimes): Read-only baseline SHA-256 manifests. SUL never modifies external protected files.

§14.13.2 Filesystem integrity guard: sul-watchdog uses async OS filesystem hooks to monitor binaries, sidecars, manifests against trusted baselines. Baseline computed at install time.

References in R.13: pandaadir05/ghost (injection/RWX/hook detection), memf-windows (process hollowing detection), wraith-rs (Windows PEB/TEB manipulation), psmux/pstop (htop for Windows).

§14.13.3 Process tamper detection: Scan SUL's own process for:

RWX regions not mapped by SUL.

API hooks in SUL's address space.

Foreign threads.

DLL hollowing.

Signed live code (D-159): attested code that no longer matches its record, and records that fail the signature, authority, order, producer or content checks.

Enables safe minhook opt-in on single-player (Ch. 7 §2.1). User-visible AV/EDR allowlist. leviathan-driver reference for kernel-mode monitoring (R.13, understanding not building — Ch. 16 §16.5); 0xor0ne/debugoff reference for hardening patterns.

§14.13.4 Threat quarantine isolation: copy → verify → record → verify → remove into encrypted quarantine. Immutable audit. sul-quarantine restore <id> with confirmation modal.

§14.13.5 Hive-mind threat logging: All incidents serialized to sul-hive-mind. Includes:

VaultDecoyAccessed, VaultTamperDetected.

E_WATCHDOG_TAMPER, E_WATCHDOG_HOOK_DETECTED, E_WATCHDOG_RWX_REGION, E_WATCHDOG_FOREIGN_THREAD, E_WATCHDOG_IMAGE_HOLLOWING, E_WATCHDOG_LIVE_CODE_MODIFIED, E_WATCHDOG_LIVE_CODE_REFUSED.

Every quarantined file with its hash and source.

Every E_MOD_INSTALL_FAILED with the malicious pattern that triggered it.

Every model-file tampering detection.

Every mode-tagged LoRA tampering detection (from §14.14).

Privacy: the threat log contains file hashes, detection reasons, and event types — never user file contents, never user paths beyond the file's own hash. (The hash is a fingerprint of the file the user already has; it does not reveal the file's contents to the hive-mind maintainers.)

§14.13.6 Zero-copy rollback: sul-save filesystem-appropriate snapshot (Ch. 12 §2.5).

2.14 Model weight and artifact tampering detection
The sul-watchdog verifies the SHA-256 of every trusted artifact on every session start. This section covers the framework and the artifacts that don't have a dedicated module chapter.

§14.14.1 The tampering detection framework: Every artifact the SUL binary trusts is verified at session start (not just first load). A modified artifact triggers E_*_TAMPER_DETECTED (or the artifact's specific error code), the Mode D quarantine lifecycle, and a user-facing alert. The framework is the same for all artifact types; the artifact-specific details are in the owning module chapter.

The framework covers:

Model files (GGUF, ONNX): SHA-256 against signed manifest.

LoRA adapters (merged GGUFs): SHA-256 + mode-tagged data hash (for mode-tagged adapters) + per-profile BFCL gate.

DSP artifacts (sul-dsp .suldsp + .suldspsig): SHA-256 + stability certificate.

Voice models (cIRM, Piper voices, Kokoro int8): SHA-256.

Vault auth models (RetinaFace, ArcFace, sherpa-onnx): SHA-256.

STT models (whisper GGML, tiny.en/base.en/small.en/medium.en at shipping quant): SHA-256.

TTS voices (Piper, Kokoro): SHA-256.

Frame gen layer manifests + native binary (VkLayer_sul_fg.json, VkLayer_LSFGVK_frame_generation.json, sul_fg.dll): SHA-256. Lossless.dll is user-supplied and not verified (logged SHA-256 only).

Config file (config.toml): Ed25519 signature.

Game registry (game_registry.json): Ed25519 signature + anti-cheat block hash verification.

Trust primitives (pubkey.minisig): Ed25519 trust root, cannot be verified by itself, integrity is via the trust directory's DPAPI + TPM protection.

Tile cache (GEV base globe tiles): vendored with binary, covered by binary signing chain.

Signature cache (sigcache.json): Ed25519-signed by the SUL binary's embedded key.

Tier 1 approval log (tier1-approvals.json): Ed25519-signed + DPAPI-wrapped.

Save shadows (saves/): SHA-256 per snapshot (Ch. 12 §2.5).

Git submodules (llama.cpp, speed-q): pinned commit hash + SHA-256.

§14.14.2 Model weight tampering detection: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24 (model file tampering detection). Covers all AI model files: InternVL3-2B, K2-Horizon-7B, MiniCPM-V, LFM2.5-VL, jina-vlm, Qwen2.5-VL, PP-OCRv5, Medusa/phrase/LiLiCorr/UniSpec drafters, STT models, TTS voices, vault auth models, Game Boy ROMs, CSI edge inference models, BCI decoding models, GEV geolocation models, VoiceStudio character voice models.

§14.14.3 Mode-tagged LoRA tampering detection: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24. Special handling because the mode-tagged adapters are the multi-profile design's load-bearing component.

§14.14.4 Prosody calibration privacy: The voice-calibration.json file (Ch. 4 §4.7) is local, unsigned, aggregate-only. sul-watchdog verifies it has not been modified by any process other than sul.exe. Modification triggers a warning and resets to conservative defaults (default_safe_intent = "assess"). Raw audio is never stored; only aggregate pitch/energy/rate statistics and per-phrase corrections.

§14.14.5 DSP and voice artifact tampering detection: sul-dsp artifacts and sul-voice model files are SHA-256 verified on every session start. Modification triggers quarantine lifecycle (Mode D for E_DSP_ARTIFACT_HASH / E_VOICE_MODEL_MISSING). Additionally, sul-watchdog verifies the stability certificate of sul-dsp artifacts is still signed by the expected build key. sul-voice-fx ships with the SUL binary (no separate artifact); its integrity is covered by the binary signing chain, not the artifact-verification path.

§14.14.6 Speculation drafter tampering detection: Medusa-1 heads, phrase-head MLP, ChainFlow draft, LiLiCorr scorer, and UniSpec retrieval index are SHA-256 verified on every session start. Draft corruption triggers E_SPEC_VERIFY_MISMATCH or E_SPEC_TOKENIZER_MISMATCH and falls back to next chain rung. Combat Full has a single chain (combat_chain) shared by all profiles — tampering any rung affects all profiles equally, which is expected. The tampering detection does not need per-profile handling because there is no per-profile chain.

§14.14.7 ReTrace saliency layer definitions: SHA-256 verified on every session start. Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.8 Search pipeline config: Verified against signed manifest. The [net.search] config section is signed as part of the overall config.toml and verified against the SUL trust model. Individual pipeline component binaries (RustXNG, adblock-rust, readdown, excerpt-select) follow the standard binary signing chain. Filter lists are signed by their maintainers.

§14.14.9 GitHub search config: Verified against signed manifest. The [net.github] config section is signed as part of the overall config.toml. Auth tokens (if configured) are stored in the vault (encrypted). The github_search tool verifies the token is not expired before each call; expired tokens trigger E_GITHUB_AUTH_FAILED and disable the tool for the session.

§14.14.10 Frame generation layer integrity: Full text in Ch. 9 §2.11.

§14.14.11 Audio governor config: The [audio.governor] config section is signed as part of the overall config.toml. No separate artifact or model; sul-audio-governor ships with the binary. Audio routing and voice FX config sections ([audio.routing], [audio.voice_fx]) are signed as part of config.toml. sul-voice-fx ships with the binary. Neural VC models (if ever) would follow the model-file signing chain — but A.89 is research only, nothing to verify in the shipping release. The voice-cloning refusal is structural (Ch. 16 §16.5) and has no model or config to tamper with.

§14.14.12 Combat Full profile router integrity: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.13 STT integrity: Full text in Ch. 4 §4.4.

§14.14.14 sul-gb / sul-savestate integrity: Full text in Ch. 3 §3.17 (failure codes) and Ch. 3 §3.5.1 / §3.6 (crate contracts).

§14.14.15 sul-quant integrity: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.16 sul-kv-compress integrity: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.17 sul-spec-draft integrity: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.18 sul-toolprm integrity: Full text in Ch. 10 §10.24.

§14.14.19 Vault integrity: Full text in Ch. 2 §2.10.

§14.14.20 WebView integrity: The WebView2 runtime is Microsoft-signed and comes from Windows Update — SUL does not vendor or verify it (it verifies the version against [webview] runtime_floor at launch and refuses to run below that). Tauri and the Tauri plugins are vendored in the workspace and follow the SUL binary signing chain. The React/TypeScript UI bundle is part of the SUL binary and follows the SUL binary signing chain. The three CI gates (electron-audit, tauri-capability-audit, webview-runtime-audit) run on every PR and gate the binary release.

§14.14.21 Music player integrity: sul-music.exe, sul-music-engine, sul-music-tags, and sul-music-lyrics ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard binary signing chain. The music library SQLite database is user data, not code; its integrity is the user's responsibility. Tag-writing backups are stored at %APPDATA%\\SUL\music-backups\<timestamp>\ and are not signed — they are user data. The bit-perfect path is verified at runtime by the loopback capture test (A.119) during diagnostics, not by a signature.

§14.14.22 Broadcast engine integrity: sul-broadcast.exe, sul-broadcast-video, and sul-broadcast-audio ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard binary signing chain. Scene documents are versioned and signed when shared (Ed25519); local scene documents are user data and not signed. ISO recordings are user data and not signed. The USB/IP virtual audio device server is part of the SUL binary; Windows enumerates the devices using the built-in USB audio class driver, no SUL driver is installed. The virtual device enumeration is verified at startup (BR-2 on failure). Lossless.dll is user-supplied and not SHA-256 verified (same as sul-fg).

§14.14.23 App auth integrity: Full text in Ch. 2 §2.1.

§14.14.24 Feature toggle and compatibility integrity: sul-toggle and sul-compat ship with the SUL binary and follow the standard binary signing chain. The default feature classification and the compatibility matrix are part of the binary. User overrides in config.toml are signed as part of config.toml. A tampered config.toml that silently enables a gated feature (e.g., features.deep.grasprune = true before A.109 passes) triggers a signature mismatch and Mode D quarantine on the config file. A tampered config.toml that silently enables a feature from a later release class than the installed release is caught by the release-ladder validator rule #32 (Ch. 1 §4.2) and refused with E_RELEASE_FEATURE_MISMATCH.

§14.14.25 Release plan integrity: Full text in §14.15 below.

§14.14.26 Handoff feature integrity:

sul-csi integrity: sul-csi.exe ships with the SUL binary. ESP32 firmware images follow the standard signing chain (signed by SUL maintainer key; ESP32 secure boot verifies signature on flash). Edge inference models (4 KB INT8) follow the model-file signing chain. A tampered edge model is rejected by the ESP32 secure boot and the node fails to initialize (E_CSI_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED on the host).

sul-bci integrity: sul-bci.exe and its models follow the standard binary and model signing chains. brain2qwerty-rs model tampering triggers Mode D quarantine.

sul-gev integrity: sul-gev ships with the SUL binary. Base globe tiles vendored with the binary follow the standard signing chain. Feed ingestion logic is part of the binary. The geolocation model (geo-sleuth) follows the model-file signing chain.

sul-security-toolkit integrity: sul-security-toolkit ships with the SUL binary. Container images (Shannon Lite, security toolkit) follow the standard release signing chain (signed Docker images verified at pull time by Docker's content trust mechanism plus SUL's own signature check). Wordlists follow the maintainer signing chain. A tampered container image is refused at pull time.

sul-voicestudio integrity: sul-voicestudio.exe and its models follow the standard binary and model signing chains. Character voice models follow the model-file signing chain. The voice cloning structural refusal is code-level (the API surface has no code path that could accept a specific real person's voice sample as a cloning target). No model or config can be tampered with to introduce this capability because it doesn't exist in the code. This is verified by an AST check on every PR that touches sul-voicestudio or the clone_voice tool — the CI gate rejects any PR that adds a code path accepting a "target specific person" parameter to the cloning function.

Hive-mind compatibility registry integrity: The hive-mind compatibility registry (game_registry.json hive entries) is signed by the maintainer key. Client verifies against the user's trust store. A tampered hive entry is refused and the user sees a "stale matrix entry" warning.

2.15 Release-plan integrity
releases.md is part of the SUL repo and ships with the binary. Its content is signed by the release signing key. The installed release class is recorded at %APPDATA%/SUL/release.toml at install time and is signed. A tampered release.toml that claims a different release class than the installed binary is caught by matching against the binary's own embedded release class (both must agree). A tampered releases.md is not actionable at runtime — it is a build-time artifact — but a build that ships a releases.md differing from the one the release binary was compiled with fails the release-audit check cargo xtask release-audit.

Release-plan validation rules: see Ch. 1 §4.2 (cross-cutting rules #29–#34) and §14.5.2 (release-ladder enforcement on update).

2.16 Safety invariants and structural refusals
The safety invariants are documented in their module chapters. This section is a summary and an index.

Safety invariants (code-level, cannot be disabled by config):

Destructive-action → Thinking (Ch. 10 §10.12). The router intercepts every turn before tool emission and scans for destructive-action indicators. If detected and destructive_action_always_thinking = true (default), the router selects Thinking profile regardless of user override. Disabling this per-game is a Tier 1 event (releases.md). Hardcoded zero-write to the router's config except via the Tier 1 approval modal.

Voice cloning of a specific real person (Ch. 16 §16.5). The API surface has no entry point; the config has no toggle; the auto-updater has no path to introduce one. This is a structural refusal, not a policy choice. Applies to sul-voice-auth (authentication is allowed — the user authenticates with their own voice) and sul-voicestudio (cloning is refused — the tool only accepts character voice presets trained on licensed data).

Kernel-AC structural refusals (Ch. 16 §16.7). Frame generation, flip-model overlay, VFS, ETW per-process, game-hook capture, and sul-optimize are structurally refused on anti_cheat.kernel_level: true titles. The AST guard verifies the refusal at build time.

The Electron exclusion (Ch. 1 §2.2). SUL ships zero Electron components. Enforced by cargo xtask electron-audit.

WebView hardening (Ch. 1 §2.2, §4). Isolation Pattern + Strict ESM + runtime floor. Tier 1 to disable.

Vault auth AND-logic (Ch. 2 §2.5). All configured factors must pass simultaneously. Disabling any factor is a Tier 1-core event.

App auth AND-logic (Ch. 2 §2.1). Same discipline.

Uncensored-model safety layer (A.154, DECIDED). The destructive-action safety invariant, the Verifier, and the structural refusals are enforced at the agent/router level, not at the model level. An abliterated or third-party uncensored model does not bypass any of them. This is a documentation invariant — the mechanism was already correct.

Structural refusals (from Ch. 16 §16.5):

Voice cloning of a specific real person.

Frame generation on kernel-level anti-cheat titles.

Mod loading on mods_allowed_online: false games.

Per-process ETW on kernel_level: true titles.

Kernel-mode interaction of any kind. (Third-party user-installed drivers are permitted; see Ch. 16 §16.5.1.)

Bypassing anti-cheat hypervisor detection.

Broadcast game-capture hook on kernel-AC titles.

Security toolkit runs without a signed consent file.

Voice cloning of a specific real person (VoiceStudio).

Uncensored models bypassing the safety layer (they don't; A.154).

All of these are enforced by code paths that return E_REFUSAL_POLICY, not by config toggles. The AST guard verifies the refusal at build time.

2.17 AST guards for the safety layer
From Ch. 16 §16.15:

sul-auth-app must not expose a bypass path in release builds.

[auth] enabled = false must be a Tier 1 event.

sul-trust, sul-quarantine, sul-watchdog are not touched by Coder PRs without Tier 1 approval modal (§14.3 Gate A extension to trust primitives).

The router's destructive_action_thinking config is sourced only from [ai.combat] and per-game combat blocks (no ad-hoc path).

[ai.combat_full.thinking] context strictly greater than [ai.combat_full.instruct] context.

[ai.combat_full.conversation] context strictly greater than [ai.combat_full.thinking] context.

[ai.speculative] must not contain per-profile chain keys (single combat_chain only).

sul-kv-compress must not import wasapi.

sul-toolprm must not import wasapi or ReadProcessMemory.

[audio.voice_fx] voice_clone must remain "refused" in every shipped config.

sul-savestate's libretro shim must allocate its buffer once at retro_serialize_size() and never resize mid-session.

sul-net must not import HTTP client beyond the declared network surface (RustXNG localhost + GitHub API).

sul-csi must not import ReadProcessMemory or any game memory access.

sul-gev must not import ReadProcessMemory.

sul-security-toolkit's container must be enforced (AST check that no tool runs outside the container).

sul-security-toolkit's hashcat/nuclei/mitmproxy wrappers must not import wasapi or ReadProcessMemory.

The complete list is in Ch. 16 §16.15. This subsection is a summary of the safety-relevant guards.

2.18 Failure codes
The safety/watchdog layer's failure codes are documented in Ch. 1 §3.4 (base):

E_TRUST_PRIMITIVE_WRITE — write attempt to a trust primitive file.

E_WATCHDOG_TAMPER — trust primitive file modified.

E_QUARANTINE_RESTORE_FAILED — quarantined file restore failed.

E_REFUSAL_POLICY — structural refusal triggered.

E_KANI_INVARIANT_FAIL — Kani formal verification invariant violated.

E_MIRI_UB — Miri detected undefined behavior.

E_RELEASE_FEATURE_MISMATCH — feature toggle enabled in a release class where it does not exist.

E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP — update attempted to skip a release class.

Plus the Mode A–F error classes (each in their respective Mode section above).

Mode F classification for each error code is in its owning module chapter. The summary:

E_TRUST_PRIMITIVE_WRITE — Mode F (fatal — the Coder is not allowed to touch trust primitives; a write attempt is a violation of the write restrictions).

E_WATCHDOG_TAMPER — Mode E (persistent — quarantine + hive threat log).

E_QUARANTINE_RESTORE_FAILED — Mode C (log; quarantined file retained).

E_REFUSAL_POLICY — Mode B (refuse the action; the game/system continues without the refused feature).

E_KANI_INVARIANT_FAIL — Mode F (fatal for the build; the binary is not shipped).

E_MIRI_UB — Mode F (fatal for the build; the binary is not shipped).

E_RELEASE_FEATURE_MISMATCH — Mode C (recoverable config error — the feature is disabled and a warning is emitted).

E_RELEASE_UPDATE_SKIP — Mode B (the update is refused; the currently-installed version continues to run).

SUL-ARCHITECTURE/Ch. 15 — Sensing, Security, and Handoff Features.md
1. Purpose
The handoff features are a set of sensing, security, and voice-synthesis capabilities added to the spec as a distinct feature bundle. They all ship in R3 (v0.6+) per releases.md, and every one of them is gated on A.152 (legal and ethical framework) being written and reviewed before any of them ships. A.152 is the scheduling prerequisite; it keeps every feature in the spec and makes the framework a condition rather than a stub.

What "handoff features" means: The original handoff proposal (dated 2026-11-11) introduced these features with gate numbers that collided with the existing spec's gate numbering. They were renumbered to A.136–A.152 per the migration table in gates.md (and the A.153 entry in gates.md). Every handoff feature section references its finalized gate number, and every tier-1 event and failure code is preserved.

Every handoff feature is R3 unless noted. The release class determines which release class in releases.md the feature lands in. A.152's review is the prerequisite for all of them. See Ch. 1 §2.3 for the releases.md R3 components list and tier1_events_added list.

Where the handoff features live:
